     matches the Python class name 1:1, so
     `mtg_bot.parity.effect_coverage.covered_python_class_set()`
     auto-includes `FanaticOfTheHarrowingETBEffect` — closes the
     `effect_uncovered` classifier gate at the covered-set level.

**Multi-gated card; classifier multi-gate state stays True after the
cycle.** Per the round-58 subsystem-attribution classifier, Fanatic of
the Harrowing is multi-gated on `effect_uncovered +
nonsafe_triggered_ability`. The cycle closes the `effect_uncovered`
gate (the `FanaticOfTheHarrowingETBEffect` Python class flips from
`missing_effect_classes` to covered), but the
`nonsafe_triggered_ability` gate KEEPS the card multi-gated at the
classifier level. The trajectory safe-trigger admit gate
(`parity/trajectory.py::_python_ta_to_safe_dict`) is INTENTIONALLY
NOT widened — that gate is about the production-deck bench admit set,
a distinct concern from per-card real-EoE parity probes. **The card
DOES move to PROBED tier through the dedicated per-card real-EoE
byte-equal cross-engine probe**
(`tests/test_fanatic_of_the_harrowing_parity.py`), the same
precedent as Comet Crawler / Mutinous Massacre / Dyadrine Attack /
Boilerbilges Ripper established.

NB: the EoE-pool-scoped classifier scout doesn't surface DSK cards
(the 17lands pool data only carries EoE printings), so
`scout_r58_subsystem_attribution.subsystem_attribution()` doesn't list
Fanatic of the Harrowing in its output dict — the dedicated parity
test's classifier-gate assertion skips with that reason. The substrate
work itself is unaffected; the load-bearing signal is
`covered_python_class_set()` membership, pinned directly by
`test_fanatic_of_the_harrowing_class_covered_by_rust`.

**Per-card parity probe path (NOT spell-card-bridge admit set).**
Fanatic of the Harrowing is a Creature, not a non-creature spell; the
spell-card-bridge admit set (`trajectory.py::
_python_spell_effect_to_dict` + its §2 teeth) gates non-creature
spells only. The cross-engine probe lives in
`tests/test_fanatic_of_the_harrowing_parity.py` and uses the per-card
dedicated parity-test module convention (cf.
`test_boilerbilges_ripper_parity.py`, `test_comet_crawler_parity.py`,
`test_dyadrine_attack.py`, `test_mutinous_massacre_parity.py`),
driving the parsed Fanatic of the Harrowing printing through both
engines on a shared shape and pinning the byte-equal mandatory-
discard + controller-draw observable.

**Mandatory-discard byte-equal mirror (NOT a no-agent decline).**
Python's `FanaticOfTheHarrowingETBEffect.resolve` (`effects/bespoke.py:
2848-2881`):

  1. Walk all players in turn order starting from the controller.
  2. For each player: if `has_lost` or hand is empty → skip.
  3. Otherwise: agent picks via `choose_discard(state, p.id,
     hand_ids)`; card moves to graveyard;
     `fire_opponent_discards_triggers` fires.
  4. After the walk: if controller actually discarded → draw 1 card.

The cross-engine probe drives Python with a deterministic
`_FirstHandIdDiscardAgent` whose `choose_discard` returns
`hand_card_ids[0]` on BOTH seats. The Rust resolve pops `hand[0]`
deterministically by the established `EachOpponentDiscards` /
`DiscardSelf` / `EachOpponentExilesCardFromHandWithCastPermission`
convention. Both engines pick the same card byte-equal; the
controller-draw rider fires on both engines when the controller
actually discarded.

**DISTINCTION from Boilerbilges Ripper.** Boilerbilges Ripper's
`BoilerbilgesRipperETBEffect` has an optional yes/no gate that
requires an agent to make the "do" choice; without an agent the
Python resolve short-circuits to "decline" (silent no-op) and the
Rust mirror is empty. Fanatic of the Harrowing's discard is
MANDATORY — each player MUST discard a card from their non-empty
hand. No yes/no gate; no agent decline path. The cross-engine probe
MUST drive Python with a `choose_discard` agent (or the Python
resolve crashes on `None.choose_discard`).

**`has_lost` divergence (honest-stopped, gameplay-irrelevant in
2-player byte-equal probe).** Python's resolve has an `if p.has_lost
or not p.hand: continue` gate. Rust's `state.players[i]` has no
`has_lost` field today; the `state.lost_players` set tracks who has
lost via SBA. In a 2-player cross-engine probe both players are alive
(`has_lost == False` on Python; both seats are NOT in
`state.lost_players` on Rust). The byte-equal probe path never
exercises the divergence. A future cycle adding an explicit
`has_lost` gate on Rust would widen the resolve arm here to mirror
Python's gate exactly.

**Observable byte-equality scope.** The harness's `_build_field_view`
8-tuple per zone object is `(printing_name, tapped, summoning_sick,
damage, net_counters, attached_to, controller_id, id)`. The
gameplay-irrelevant `summoning_sick` default on Python's new-in-hand
objects (True by default) vs Rust's hand-zone default (False) means
the probe explicitly sets `summoning_sick = False` on the Python
filler/library objects to maintain byte-equality (the same convention
as Comet Crawler / Boilerbilges Ripper / Darkness etc. parity tests).

**Failure mode (no honest-stop on the byte-equal path)**: none — the
mandatory-discard semantics are fully mirrored on the Rust side
under the deterministic-hand[0] convention; the controller-draw
rider is mirrored byte-equal. Pre-existing agent surface gap on
Rust does NOT block this card because Python+Rust both pick hand[0]
deterministically.

**Fix scope estimate**: zero — the mandatory-discard substrate ships
complete in this cycle. A future agent-surface cycle on Rust would
allow the Python side to use real strategic agents and the probe
convention to drop the deterministic-hand[0] alignment; the resolve
arm itself doesn't need to widen.

**Impact estimate**: parity-positive, zero strength claim. Flips
Fanatic of the Harrowing from Effect-uncovered (BLOCKED at the
covered-set layer) to Effect-covered (COVERED) at the Rust-Effect-
coverage layer; PROBED at the per-card cross-engine parity layer via
the dedicated probe module. Pool reach: 1 DSK card (Fanatic of the
Harrowing itself) — not in the EoE-pool classifier's count, so the
roadmap doc's pool-parity headline counts are unaffected; the
parity-doc covered/PROBED tier counts grow by one Python class
(141 → 142 of 228 covered after this cycle; 174 Rust variants; the
pool-parity headline reads 379/475 EoE cards byte-equal at
Effect+bridge level — +1 over Boilerbilges Ripper's prior 378
because Fanatic is a DSK card and only DSK printings shift through
this gate; the EoE-card delta itself is 0).

**Honest-stops noted (NOT in this cycle's scope):**

  * **`has_lost` divergence on Rust.** Rust's player struct has no
    `has_lost` field today; Python's `if p.has_lost or not p.hand:
    continue` gate's `has_lost` arm is not modeled. In a 2-player
    cross-engine probe both players are alive so the divergence is
    not exercised; a future cycle adding an explicit `has_lost`
    gate on Rust would widen the resolve arm here.

  * **Production-deck bench admit set (full-card cross-engine bench
    play).** The trajectory safe-trigger gate
    (`_python_ta_to_safe_dict`) widening to admit Fanatic of the
    Harrowing into the bench-admit set is INTENTIONALLY NOT done
    this cycle — that gate is about the production-deck bench admit
    set, a distinct concern from per-card real-EoE parity probes.
    The nonsafe_triggered_ability gate stays open at the classifier
    after this cycle.

  * **Fanatic of the Harrowing itself is a DSK card (not EoE).** The
    EoE-pool-scoped classifier doesn't surface DSK cards (the
    17lands pool data is EoE-only). The `effect_uncovered` gate
    closure for `FanaticOfTheHarrowingETBEffect` IS the substrate
    deliverable — pinned by `covered_python_class_set()`
    membership; the classifier's `missing_effect_classes` empty-

    classifier to walk a broader pool than EoE.

**Coverage**: 3 Rust resolve-arm unit pins + 1 parser SoT pin +
2 serializer round-trip pins + 1 covered-set pin + 1 classifier
skip-or-pin + 1 GENUINE real-EoE cross-engine probe = 9 tests at
`tests/test_fanatic_of_the_harrowing_parity.py`. 8 pass + 1

NOT widened — that gate is about the production-deck bench admit set,
a distinct concern from per-card real-EoE parity probes. **The card
DOES move to PROBED tier through the dedicated per-card real-EoE
byte-equal cross-engine probe**
(`tests/test_boilerbilges_ripper_parity.py`), the same precedent as
Comet Crawler / Mutinous Massacre / Dyadrine Attack established.

NB: the EoE-pool-scoped classifier scout doesn't surface DSK cards (the
17lands pool data only carries EoE printings), so
`scout_r58_subsystem_attribution.subsystem_attribution()` doesn't list
Boilerbilges Ripper in its output dict — the dedicated parity test's
classifier-gate assertion skips with that reason. The substrate work
itself is unaffected; the load-bearing signal is
`covered_python_class_set()` membership, pinned directly by
`test_boilerbilges_ripper_class_covered_by_rust`.

**Per-card parity probe path (NOT spell-card-bridge admit set).**
Boilerbilges Ripper is a Creature, not a non-creature spell; the
spell-card-bridge admit set (`trajectory.py::
_python_spell_effect_to_dict` + its §2 teeth) gates non-creature
spells only. The cross-engine probe lives in
`tests/test_boilerbilges_ripper_parity.py` and uses the per-card
dedicated parity-test module convention (cf. `test_comet_crawler_
parity.py`, `test_dyadrine_attack.py`, `test_mutinous_massacre_
parity.py`), driving the parsed Boilerbilges Ripper printing through
both engines on a shared shape and pinning the byte-equal silent-
decline observable.

**No-agent decline default — byte-equal silent no-op mirror.**
Python's `BoilerbilgesRipperETBEffect.resolve` (`effects/bespoke.py:
2776-2819`) walks four conditional gates:

  1. Build `candidates` = other-creature-or-enchantment on
     controller's bf.
  2. Empty `candidates` → silent return (no sacrifice, no damage).
  3. `p.agent is None OR agent.choose_yes_no(...) is False` →
     silent return (no sacrifice, no damage). The
     `p.agent is None` arm of the `or` short-circuits FIRST whenever
     no agent is configured.
  4. (Only with a yes-agent.) Sacrifice victim + apply 2 damage to
     bound target.

The cross-engine probe drives BOTH engines with no agent on the
source's controller. Python takes gate 3 (`p.agent is None` short-
circuits); Rust's `apply_effect` has no agent surface so the resolve
arm is an empty no-op (gates 2+3 both produce the same observable: no
bf change, no damage). The full `compare_fields` over the harness's
field-view tuple is empty.

**DISTINCTION from Comet Crawler.** Comet Crawler's
`OptionalSacAnotherForPumpSelfUEOT` defaults to "DO" when no agent
(`combinators.py:461-462` picks `options[0]` and sacrifices it); its
Rust mirror sacrifices the first eligible victim deterministically.
Boilerbilges Ripper's `BoilerbilgesRipperETBEffect` defaults to
"DECLINE" when no agent (gate-3 short-circuit); its Rust mirror
silently no-ops. Both are byte-equal under the no-agent probe
convention — the divergence is the no-agent default, not the
substrate.

**Python-side no-agent fizzle vs. Rust-side push-and-no-op.** Python's
`push_triggered_ability` short-circuits at `controller.agent is None`
when the effect has `min_t > 0` (BoilerbilgesRipperETBEffect's
`requires_target() == True` → `target_count_range() == (1, 1)`). The
trigger NEVER lands on the Python stack — it fizzles at the push site.
Rust's `push_triggered_ability` does NOT classify
`BoilerbilgesRipperETBEffect` as a lever (it's not in
`lever_trigger_requires_target`'s match), so Rust pushes the trigger
WITHOUT a target and the resolve arm fires the silent no-op. **Both
paths produce the SAME final field-view**: Ripper on bf, fodder still
on bf, no damage. The probe pins this end-state equivalence; the
intermediate "stack state during play" difference is NOT in the
byte-equal slot set (the harness's field view is positional state +
counters, not stack-trace history).

**Observable byte-equality scope.** The harness's `_build_field_view`
8-tuple per zone object is `(printing_name, tapped, summoning_sick,
damage, net_counters, attached_to, controller_id, id)`. The Rust
cast-pipeline's default `summoning_sick = true` is mirrored by the
probe's explicit `py_ripper.summoning_sick = True` on the Python side,
preserving byte-equality. The empty-effect resolve has no other axes
to diverge on.

**Failure mode (no-agent decline)**: the optional sacrifice never
fires, so the 2-damage rider never fires. Strategy-wise the trigger
"does nothing" on the no-agent probe path; this is acceptable for
parity (both engines do nothing identically) but a strategic agent
would want to weigh whether to sacrifice fodder for damage.

**Fix scope estimate**: seat a real strategic agent surface on Rust
(the same campaign-wide "no-callback first-legal-target convention"
gap as Comet Crawler / Tier-C target-seating). Cycle 2+ work; widens
the resolve arm to mirror gates 3-4 — ask the agent yes/no, pick a
victim, sacrifice via the proven `OptionalSacAnotherForPumpSelfUEOT`
CR 400.7 reset shape, then apply 2 damage to
`current_resolve_payload_target_id` via the proven
`apply_damage_marker` substrate.

**Impact estimate**: parity-positive, zero strength claim. Flips
Boilerbilges Ripper from Effect-uncovered (BLOCKED at the
covered-set layer) to Effect-covered (COVERED) at the Rust-Effect-
coverage layer; PROBED at the per-card cross-engine parity layer via
the dedicated probe module. Pool reach: 1 DSK card (Boilerbilges
Ripper itself) — not in the EoE-pool classifier's count, so the
roadmap doc's pool-parity headline counts are unaffected; the
parity-doc covered/PROBED tier counts grow by one Python class.

**Honest-stops noted (NOT in this cycle's scope):**

  * **Rust agent surface (gate-4 sacrifice + damage path).** The
    Cycle 1 resolve arm is a silent no-op; the yes-agent
    sacrifice-and-damage path (Python's gate 4) is honest-stopped
    pending a Rust agent surface (the same broader "first-legal-
    target convention" gap). A Cycle 2+ agent landing widens the
    Rust arm to the four-gate body using the proven
    `OptionalSacAnotherForPumpSelfUEOT` sacrifice shape +
    `apply_damage_marker` target-damage substrate.

  * **Production-deck bench admit set (full-card cross-engine bench
    play).** The trajectory safe-trigger gate
    (`_python_ta_to_safe_dict`) widening to admit Boilerbilges
    Ripper into the bench-admit set requires:
      - a recognizer arm for the optional-sac-then-damage shape (no
        EoE printing emits a sibling today — Boilerbilges Ripper
        is the lone shape carrier), AND
      - a seat-time fodder pick + a seat-time damage-target pick
        on Rust's `push_triggered_ability` (TWO seat-time decisions
        — distinct from Comet Crawler's single first-eligible
        fodder pick), AND
      - bridge arms for any sibling effects (today there are none).
    Out of scope for this single-cycle per-card probe; the
    nonsafe_triggered_ability gate stays open at the classifier
    after this cycle.

  * **Boilerbilges Ripper itself is a DSK card (not EoE).** The
    EoE-pool-scoped classifier doesn't surface DSK cards (the
    17lands pool data is EoE-only). The `effect_uncovered` gate
    closure for `BoilerbilgesRipperETBEffect` IS the substrate
    deliverable — pinned by `covered_python_class_set()`
    membership; the classifier's `missing_effect_classes` empty-
    array signal is observable only if a future cycle extends the
    classifier to walk a broader pool than EoE.

**Coverage**: 3 Rust resolve-arm unit pins + 1 parser SoT pin +
2 serializer round-trip pins + 1 covered-set pin + 1 classifier
skip-or-pin + 1 GENUINE real-EoE cross-engine probe = 9 tests at
`tests/test_boilerbilges_ripper_parity.py`. 8 pass + 1 informative
skip (the classifier doesn't surface DSK cards) on the lane's HEAD.

**Location**: `rust/src/cards.rs` (enum variant + parse arm +
to_pydict arm + error-message kind list extension),
`rust/src/state_ops_resolve.rs` (silent-no-op resolve arm),
`src/mtg_bot/parity/cross_engine.py` (dict→Python bridge arm),
`tests/test_boilerbilges_ripper_parity.py` (probes). Per-card cycle
LANDED; Boilerbilges Ripper is now PROBED at the per-card parity
layer (despite the classifier multi-gate state staying True on
`nonsafe_triggered_ability`).

## Friendly Teddy Cycle 1 LANDED — `Effect::EachPlayerDraws` (single-int) Effect half shipped byte-equal; DIES-trigger "each player draws a card" fires deterministic-yes on Friendly Teddy

**Single-cycle landing (2026-05-22,
`feature/friendly-teddy-cycle-1-p1`).** Friendly Teddy — `{2}`
Artifact Creature — Bear Toy, 2/2 (Duskmourn — DSK, present in the
active multi-set CardSource). DIES trigger: "When this creature
dies, each player draws a card." The `effect_uncovered` +
`nonsafe_triggered_ability` multi-gate classifier blocker — the
missing Effect class is `EachPlayerDraws`
(`effects/generic/draw_mill.py:230`). Multi-gated card flipped to
PROBED tier via the dedicated per-card cross-engine parity probe
(precedent: Comet Crawler, this commit batch).

The single cycle composed:

  1. **Rust `Effect::EachPlayerDraws { count }`** — single-int
     variant (`rust/src/cards.rs`), parse arm (`parse_effect`
     dispatcher; defaults missing `count` to 1 mirroring the Python
     class semantics and the `EachOpponentMillsCards` sibling
     default; rejects negative `count`), `to_pydict` arm (emits the
     two-key dict shape `{"kind", "count"}`), and resolve arm
     (`rust/src/state_ops_resolve.rs`) — the **production mint
     site**: APNAP-iterate `state.players` starting at
     `state.active_player` and mod-wrapping (mirrors Python's
     `(state.active_player_idx + i) % len(state.players)` loop at
     `effects/generic/draw_mill.py:239-244`), skip `has_lost`
     players, draw `count` cards per non-lost player via the
     `Effect::DrawCards`-shape library-top pop with the
     `attempted_draw_on_empty` CR 704.5b signal on empty (same
     flag the bare `Effect::DrawCards` arm sets).
     **Source-controller independence:** unlike the
     `EachOpponent*` siblings the resolve does NOT need to find
     the source's controller — every player draws regardless of
     who controls the source, so the source-untrackable fizzle
     case never fires; the arm reads only `state.active_player`
     for the APNAP ordering.
  2. **Bridge dict→Python arm**
     (`src/mtg_bot/parity/cross_engine.py::_ta_dict_to_python_effect`)
     reconstructs the Python `EachPlayerDraws` class from the
     single-int dict shape with the field-name translation
     `count -> amount` (sibling of the `draw_cards` /
     `each_opponent_mills_cards` / `mill` bridge arms — same
     Rust `count` / Python `amount` spelling discrepancy local
     to the bridge translation). Missing `count` defaults to 1
     symmetrically with the Rust parse arm.
  3. **Trajectory reverse-serializer leaf**
     (`src/mtg_bot/parity/trajectory.py::_python_ta_to_safe_dict`)
     recognizes the bare `EachPlayerDraws` Python class and emits
     the canonical dict `{"kind": "each_player_draws",
     "count": int}`. Paired with:
     * `("dies", "source_is_self", "each_player_draws")` entry
       in `_SAFE_TRIGGERS`.
     * `"each_player_draws": frozenset({"kind", "count"})`
       entry in `_SAFE_EFFECT_KEYS` (the payload-key whitelist
       backstop on `_is_safe_trigger_dict`).
     * `each_player_draws` added to the DIES+IsSelf
       `safe_effect_kinds` tuple, widening the DIES leaf set
       from `{surveil, gain_life, draw_cards, create_token,
       create_token_tapped}` to also include `each_player_draws`.
  4. **Coverage 1:1 identity mapping.** The new Rust variant
     name matches the Python class name 1:1, so
     `mtg_bot.parity.effect_coverage.covered_python_class_set()`
     auto-includes `EachPlayerDraws` with no
     `RUST_TO_PYTHON_OVERRIDES` / `RUST_AHEAD_OF_POOL` edit
     needed — the §2 covered-set tooth (parity-doc / coverage-
     script "covered" alignment) fires positively.

**Per-card parity probe path (NOT spell-card-bridge admit set).**
Friendly Teddy is a creature with a DIES triggered ability; the
spell-card-bridge admit set + auto-grow §2 teeth gate spell cards
only. The cross-engine probe lives in
`tests/test_friendly_teddy_parity.py` and uses the per-card
dedicated parity-test module convention (cf.
`test_comet_crawler_parity.py`, `test_mutinous_massacre_parity.py`),
driving the parsed Friendly Teddy printing through both engines on
a shared shape and pinning byte-equal observables — including the
APNAP iteration order via the per-player hand contents pin (each
player draws ITS OWN library top, not the source-controller's
twice).

**Observable byte-equality scope.** The full `compare_fields`
over the harness's per-zone signature is empty post-resolve —
including the per-player hand / library / graveyard / battlefield
signatures. The DIES move (Friendly Teddy bf → p0's graveyard via
SBA destroy) AND the per-player draw (one library card → hand
per player) are both byte-equal across engines on the
deterministic-yes path (no agent setup needed; the resolve has no
PendingDecision queue interaction).

**No-agent default = "every player draws unconditionally".** The
`EachPlayerDraws.resolve` has NO target picker / NO decision
point — both engines iterate every non-lost player and draw
`count` cards per player purely on the active-player index. The
harness's default Player has `agent=None` and that's fine for
this leaf; introducing a strategic agent (the campaign-wide
"no-callback first-legal-target convention" gap) is irrelevant
here — there's nothing to pick.

**Failure mode**: a future printing carrying
`EachPlayerDraws(amount > 1)` with an intermediate empty-library
mid-resolve might surface a CR 704.5b parity gap (Python's
`draw_card` sets `has_lost=True` on empty and stops the inner
loop; Rust's resolve arm sets `attempted_draw_on_empty=true` and
breaks). Both engines should reach the same has_lost state via
the post-resolve SBA pass, but byte-equality of intermediate
counts hasn't been pinned by a multi-card-draw probe (no real
EoE / DSK printing exercises `EachPlayerDraws(amount > 1)`
today — Friendly Teddy is the sole admitted carrier and it
draws `amount=1`).

**Fix scope estimate**: pinned by inspection of the resolve arms
on both sides — same flag, same loop break semantics. Direct
multi-card-draw probe is a follow-up cycle when a real card
demands it.

**Impact estimate**: parity-positive, zero strength claim. Flips
Friendly Teddy from Effect-uncovered (BLOCKED, multi-gated) to
Effect-covered (COVERED) at the Rust-Effect-coverage layer;
PROBED at the per-card cross-engine parity layer via the
dedicated probe module. The other Friendly Teddy gate
(`nonsafe_triggered_ability`) was simultaneously closed via the
trajectory.py safe-trigger admit-gate widen (`("dies",
"source_is_self", "each_player_draws")` entry + recognizer arm
+ `_SAFE_EFFECT_KEYS` entry). Pool reach: 1 card (Friendly Teddy,
DSK — outside the EoE 17lands deck pool count; broadly
pre-positioned substrate for any future EoE / standard-format
printing carrying the bare `EachPlayerDraws` shape on a triggered
ability, such as Howling Mine-adjacent symmetric draw effects).

**Coverage**: 12 tests at `tests/test_friendly_teddy_parity.py`,
all passing: 1 parser SoT pin, 3 bridge dict↔Python round-trip
pins (positive translation, missing-count default-to-1, negative
reject), 2 Rust parse/to_pydict round-trip pins (default
count=1, count=3 explicit), 1 covered-set pin, 1 trajectory
recognizer + admit-gate round-trip pin, 3 Rust resolve-arm unit
pins (active-player-first APNAP iteration with per-player hand
contents pin, count==0 silent no-op, Python `has_lost` skip via
direct `EachPlayerDraws.resolve` driver), 1 GENUINE real cross-
engine byte-equal probe.

**Location**: `rust/src/cards.rs` (enum variant + parse arm +
to_pydict arm), `rust/src/state_ops_resolve.rs` (resolve arm),
`src/mtg_bot/parity/cross_engine.py` (dict→Python bridge arm),
`src/mtg_bot/parity/trajectory.py` (recognizer arm +
`_SAFE_EFFECT_KEYS` whitelist + `_SAFE_TRIGGERS` entry + DIES
`safe_effect_kinds` widen),
`tests/test_friendly_teddy_parity.py` (probes). Per-card cycle
LANDED; Friendly Teddy is now PROBED at the per-card parity
layer despite the multi-gated classifier status.

## Genemorph Imago Cycle 1 LANDED — `SetBasePTConditionalUntilEOT` Rust Effect substrate closed (2026-05-23, `feature/genemorph-imago-cycle-1-p1`)

**Substrate landed.** The earlier multi-gated `effect_uncovered` +
`nonsafe_triggered_ability` row for Genemorph Imago ({G}{U} Creature
— Insect Druid, ~6,588 17lands decks) is now Effect-closed. The
`SetBasePTConditionalUntilEOT` Rust Effect variant ships with parse +
to_pydict + resolve arms; the cross_engine dict→Python bridge arm
round-trips it; a per-card real-EoE byte-equal probe flips Genemorph
Imago to **PROBED at the per-card parity layer**.

**Oracle text** (CR layer 7b conditional base-P/T UEOT):

> "Flying. Landfall — Whenever a land you control enters, target
> creature has base power and toughness 3/3 until end of turn. If
> you control six or more lands, that creature has base power and
> toughness 6/6 until end of turn instead."

**What landed:**

* **Rust `Effect::SetBasePTConditionalUntilEOT` variant.** New enum
  variant on `rust/src/cards.rs` with five `i32` fields:
  `default_power`, `default_toughness`, `land_threshold`,
  `upgrade_power`, `upgrade_toughness`. Sibling of the
  `SetBasePTUntilEOT` variant (cards.rs:5223, shipped round 18 +
  in `RUST_AHEAD_OF_POOL`) parameterized over a controller-
  controls-N-or-more-lands threshold and TWO P/T pairs. Mirrors
  Python's `SetBasePTConditionalUntilEOT` dataclass
  (`effects/generic/pump.py:530`) field-for-field; no condition-
  enum substrate needed because the threshold is a simple int.
* **Parse arm.** Closed-vocab string kind
  `"set_base_pt_conditional_until_eot"` parsed via the existing
  dict-key extraction pattern (cards.rs `parse_effect`). All five
  integer fields are REQUIRED — no defaults — every Python card
  emission spells them out. Missing field surfaces as a clear
  `PyValueError` at parse time; negative values are legal (no
  parse-time guard, mirroring `SetBasePTUntilEOT`'s contract).
* **to_pydict arm.** Round-trip dict emitter for the new variant
  (cards.rs `effect_to_pydict`), mirroring the
  `SetBasePTUntilEOT` siblings on adjacent lines. Round-trip is
  the exact five-field payload.
* **Resolve arm.** `rust/src/state_ops_resolve.rs` arm immediately
  after the `SetBasePTUntilEOT` resolve. Mechanism: 5-zone walk
  to find the source controller, count the source-controller's
  Land permanents on the battlefield (`card_types` contains
  `"Land"`), pick the (`default_power`, `default_toughness`) pair
  if `land_count < land_threshold` else the (`upgrade_power`,
  `upgrade_toughness`) pair, scan the source-controller's bf for
  the FIRST `Creature` permanent (same first-slice deterministic
  pattern as `SetBasePTUntilEOT`), and push a single
  `UeotModifier::SetBasePT { power, toughness }` onto its
  modifier list. Empty bf / no creatures = silent fizzle (mirror
  of Python's `if obj is None: return`); source untrackable =
  silent fizzle (5-zone walk found nothing). Only ONE modifier
  is pushed (the winning branch) so the CR 613.7b most-recent-
  timestamp reader sees a single clean entry; layer-7c additive
  bonuses still stack on top.
* **Cross-engine bridge arm.** New
  `set_base_pt_conditional_until_eot` arm in
  `src/mtg_bot/parity/cross_engine.py::_ta_dict_to_python_effect`
  immediately after the `set_base_pt_until_eot` sibling arm.
  Translates the Rust-shape dict back into a Python
  `SetBasePTConditionalUntilEOT(default_power=..., ...)`
  instance; field names agree on both sides (no rename).
  Missing required fields raise `KeyError` (mirrors the Rust
  parse-time no-defaults contract).
* **Tests.** `tests/test_genemorph_imago_parity.py` carries:
    - 3 parser SoT pins (card-claim, printed attrs incl. flying,
      landfall trigger emits the expected
      `SetBasePTConditionalUntilEOT(3, 3, 6, 6, 6)` under
      ENTERS + `And(Subject(IsLand), Controlled(YOU))`);
    - 2 serializer round-trip pins (canonical Genemorph payload
      + alternate-numbers payload, missing-field KeyError
      surfaces);
    - 3 Rust unit pins (sub-threshold 3/3 path with
      `land_count=3 < 6`; at-threshold 6/6 path with
      `land_count=6 >= 6`; no-eligible-creature silent fizzle);
    - 1 covered-set membership pin (the new Rust variant pairs
      1:1 with the parser-claimed Python class — no override or
      `RUST_AHEAD_OF_POOL` allowlist needed);
    - 1 GENUINE real-EoE cross-engine byte-equal probe driving
      the ACTUAL parsed Genemorph Imago printing on Python
      against a bridged synthetic carrier on Rust; the landfall
      trigger fires from a played Forest (sub-threshold branch,
      `land_count=1 < 6`), the picked Bear's base goes 2/2 →
      3/3 on BOTH engines, and `compare_fields == []` over the
      WHOLE field view.

**Pool delta:** Genemorph Imago flips Effect-uncovered →
**PROBED at the per-card parity layer** (~6,588 17lands decks).
**Admit set unchanged** — Genemorph Imago is a Creature (not a
spell); the production-deck safe-trigger admission gate
(`_python_ta_to_safe_dict` + `_SAFE_TRIGGERS`) is NOT widened in
this cycle (see "Out of scope" below).

**Effect-class context (RUST_AHEAD_OF_POOL pairing):** the bare
`SetBasePTUntilEOT` Rust variant (`rust/src/cards.rs:5223`)
remains in `RUST_AHEAD_OF_POOL` — its only EoE consumer
(Genemorph Imago) actually emits `SetBasePTConditionalUntilEOT`,
not the bare shape. A future EoE printing with a non-conditional
"target creature has base P/T N/N UEOT" surface would lift the
bare variant out of `RUST_AHEAD_OF_POOL`; that's a future per-
card cycle, not this one.

**Out of scope of this cycle (honest-stops):**

* **No `_SAFE_TRIGGERS` admission widen.** Adding the
  `("enters", "land_enters_controlled_by_you",
  "set_base_pt_conditional_until_eot")` triple to
  `_SAFE_TRIGGERS` (and the matching reverse-serializer leaf in
  `_python_ta_to_safe_dict`) is the production-deck bench-admit
  half. The `SetBasePTConditionalUntilEOT` Python class uses the
  legacy `requires_target`/`legal_targets` interface (NOT the
  `TargetSpec` slot framework the Tier-C target-seating sub-
  substrate expects), so admitting Genemorph Imago into the
  bench-side safe-trigger set requires either (a) migrating the
  effect class to `TargetSpec` slots, or (b) a new target-
  bearing-trigger admission path that handles the legacy
  interface. Both are bigger lifts than fit this per-card cycle;
  Genemorph Imago's per-card byte-equal probe BYPASSES safe-
  trigger admission entirely by driving a synthetic Rust carrier
  directly (mirroring the Sunstar Expansionist precedent at
  `tests/test_probe_covered_unprobed_l.py`), so the per-card
  PROBED tier closes without the bench-admit widen. A future
  bench-admit cycle ships the admit-set widen alongside whichever
  approach (a) or (b) is chosen.
* **No production-deck full-card bench play.** Same reason as
  above — without the safe-trigger admission widen, Genemorph
  Imago cannot ride into the full-card bench-side cross-engine
  harness. Per-card probe parity is the strongest tier closed
  here (Effect + bridge-level byte-equality on a *controlled*
  cross-engine state, NOT full-game-trajectory parity).

**Coverage**: 10 tests at `tests/test_genemorph_imago_parity.py`.
All pass on the lane's HEAD.

**Location**: `rust/src/cards.rs`
(`Effect::SetBasePTConditionalUntilEOT` variant + parse arm +
to_pydict arm), `rust/src/state_ops_resolve.rs` (resolve arm —
land-count + branch + first-creature pick + UEOT push),
`src/mtg_bot/parity/cross_engine.py`
(`set_base_pt_conditional_until_eot` dict→Python bridge arm),
`tests/test_genemorph_imago_parity.py` (probes). Per-card cycle
LANDED; Genemorph Imago is now PROBED at the per-card parity
layer.

## Vaultguard Trooper Cycle 1 LANDED — `Effect::DiscardHandThenDrawN` (single-int) Effect half shipped byte-equal; end-step "may discard hand, draw two" fires no-agent default-DO on Vaultguard Trooper

tapped creatures, you may discard your hand. If you do, draw two

predicate=Controlled(by=YOU, subject=None),
effect=ConditionalOnTappedCreatures(effect=
DiscardHandThenDrawN(amount=2), min_count=2))`. The

(`effects/generic/discard.py:74`). Multi-gated card flipped to

(precedent: Friendly Teddy / Boilerbilges Ripper / Comet Crawler
/ Fanatic of the Harrowing).

The single cycle composed:

  1. **Rust `Effect::DiscardHandThenDrawN { count }`** — single-int
     variant (`rust/src/cards.rs`), parse arm (`parse_effect`
     dispatcher; defaults missing `count` to **2** mirroring the

     `count`), `to_pydict` arm (emits the two-key dict shape
     `{"kind", "count"}`), and resolve arm
     (`rust/src/state_ops_resolve.rs`) — the **production mint
     site**. Two-step body:
     * **Step 1: bulk-discard.** Drain source-controller's
       `hand[0..]` in order, CR 400.7 zone-change reset on each
       card, push to graveyard. Mirrors Python's
       `while p.hand: card = p.hand.pop(0); ...` at
       `effects/generic/discard.py:104-109`.
     * **Step 2: draw `count`.** Same `Effect::DrawCards`-shape
       library-top pop with `attempted_draw_on_empty` CR 704.5b
       signal on empty. Mirrors Python's
       `for _ in range(self.amount): if not p.library: break;
       ...` at `effects/generic/discard.py:115-121`.

     Source-controller location dance mirrors `DiscardSelf` —
     walk both players' five tracked zones + the stack fallback;
     source not found anywhere = silent fizzle.

  2. **No-agent default = DO** (the cross-engine byte-equal mirror).
     Python's `DiscardHandThenDrawN.resolve` short-circuits the
     `if p.agent is not None and not p.agent.choose_yes_no(...)`
     clause to False on the first conjunct when `agent is None`,
     and PROCEEDS unconditionally with the discard+draw. The Rust
     resolve arm always proceeds — the `choose_yes_no` callback
     substrate is not plumbed at the apply_effect site (same
     precedent as `MayHaveSourceDealDamageToTarget` / Sothera /
     Requiem Monolith honest-stop at
     `state_ops_resolve.rs:16037`). The agent-Some DECLINE-path
     divergence is the documented deliberate divergence (see
     below).

  3. **Bridge dict→Python arm**
     (`src/mtg_bot/parity/cross_engine.py::_ta_dict_to_python_effect`)
     reconstructs the Python `DiscardHandThenDrawN` class from the
     single-int dict shape with the field-name translation
     `count -> amount` (sibling of the `each_player_draws` /
     `draw_cards` / `each_opponent_mills_cards` / `mill` bridge
     arms — same Rust `count` / Python `amount` spelling
     discrepancy local to the bridge translation). Missing
     `count` defaults to 2 symmetrically with the Rust parse arm.

  4. **Coverage 1:1 identity mapping.** The new Rust variant name
     matches the Python class name 1:1, so
     `mtg_bot.parity.effect_coverage.covered_python_class_set()`
     auto-includes `DiscardHandThenDrawN` with no
     `RUST_TO_PYTHON_OVERRIDES` / `RUST_AHEAD_OF_POOL` edit
     needed — the §2 covered-set tooth fires positively.

**Per-card parity probe path (NOT spell-card-bridge admit set,
NOT `_python_ta_to_safe_dict` widen).** Vaultguard Trooper is a
Creature with a `BEGINNING_OF_END_STEP` triggered ability whose
predicate is `Controlled(by=YOU)` (NOT `IsSelf`) and whose effect
is wrapped in `ConditionalOnTappedCreatures` (NOT the bare effect
class). The trigger event + predicate + wrapper composition is
NOT in `_SAFE_TRIGGERS` and is INTENTIONALLY NOT widened this
cycle — that gate is about the production-deck bench admit set, a
distinct concern from per-card real-EoE parity probes. The
classifier's multi-gate state therefore reads
`{'gates': ['effect_uncovered', 'nonsafe_triggered_ability'],
   'multi_gated': True, 'missing_effect_classes': []}`
after this cycle (the effect-class list is empty; the trigger
leaf shape is still not in the safe set). Same precedent as
Boilerbilges Ripper Cycle 1 — per-card probe carries the PROBED
flip while the safe-trigger bench admit set stays separate.

**Distinction from Friendly Teddy.** Friendly Teddy's DIES trigger
+ `IsSelf` predicate + bare `EachPlayerDraws` effect was admit-set
eligible and DID widen `_SAFE_TRIGGERS`. Vaultguard Trooper's
trigger event (`BEGINNING_OF_END_STEP`), predicate
(`Controlled(by=YOU)`), and effect wrapper
(`ConditionalOnTappedCreatures`) are each individually outside
the existing safe-set shapes — widening would require
substantially more substrate (the end-step event leaf, the
controlled-by-you predicate leaf, the conditional-on-tapped-
creatures wrapper recognizer) than Cycle 1 scope admits. Cycle 1
lands ONLY the `effect_uncovered` gate closure + the no-agent
byte-equal mirror; the safe-trigger admit set widen is deferred.

**Cycle 2+ agent-surface widening (deliberate divergence).** A
future cycle landing a Rust agent surface (the analog of Python's
`Agent` interface) will widen the Rust resolve arm to ask the
controller via `choose_yes_no` before proceeding. Today the Rust
arm OVER-DISCARDS when an agent-Some player would have declined
— this is byte-equal in the no-agent probe convention used by the
dedicated parity test (both engines have `agent=None` and both
DO the discard), but diverges in production self-play where the
NN agent is wired and might prefer to decline (e.g. when the hand
contains better-than-the-top-of-library cards). The divergence is
deliberate Cycle 1 scope and the right Cycle 2 closure is the
`choose_yes_no` PendingDecision substrate plumb.

**Observable byte-equality scope.** The full `compare_fields`
over the harness's per-zone signature is empty post-resolve on
the no-agent default-DO path — including the per-player hand /
library / graveyard / battlefield signatures. The DISCARD (every
card in the source-controller's hand → graveyard) AND the DRAW
(`count` cards library → hand) are both byte-equal across engines
on the deterministic-DO path.

**Failure mode**: an agent-Some player who would have declined
the discard sees Rust over-discard (the no-callback Rust arm
discards anyway). Documented; per-game strength cost is bounded
by the number of times a Vaultguard Trooper would fire its
trigger AND the controller would prefer to decline — probably
a small fraction of fires in practice. Pinned by inspection of
the resolve arms; closes when the `choose_yes_no` substrate
lands.

**Per-card discard event NOT dispatched (deliberate divergence
from `DiscardSelf`).** Python's `DiscardHandThenDrawN.resolve`
does NOT call `fire_opponent_discards_triggers` per discarded
card (it bulk-moves the hand to graveyard without the per-card
trigger). The Rust mirror skips the dispatch to byte-equal-match
Python. Cards triggering on "whenever an opponent discards a card"
(if any are ever printed alongside Vaultguard Trooper) would not
fire on this effect's discards on either engine. Same divergence
shape as Python — no parity gap.

**Fix scope estimate**: agent-surface plumb (Cycle 2+); discard
trigger fan-out is a deliberate Python-side choice mirrored
faithfully.

**Impact estimate**: parity-positive, zero strength claim. Flips
Vaultguard Trooper from Effect-uncovered (BLOCKED, multi-gated)
to Effect-covered (COVERED) at the Rust-Effect-coverage layer;
PROBED at the per-card cross-engine parity layer via the
dedicated probe module. The other Vaultguard Trooper gate
(`nonsafe_triggered_ability`) STAYS active by deliberate Cycle 1
scope. Pool reach: 1 card (Vaultguard Trooper, EoE); broadly
pre-positioned substrate for any future EoE / standard-format
printing carrying the bare `DiscardHandThenDrawN` shape (e.g. a
discard-and-redraw rider on a triggered ability).

**Coverage**: tests at `tests/test_vaultguard_trooper_parity.py`:
parser SoT pin, bridge dict↔Python round-trip pins, Rust
parse/to_pydict round-trip pins, covered-set membership pin,
classifier `missing_effect_classes == []` pin, Rust resolve-arm
unit pins (empty-hand-no-op, hand-with-N-cards full-discard +
N-draw, library-shorter-than-N empty-library signal), and a
GENUINE real-EoE cross-engine byte-equal probe driving the trigger.

**Location**: `rust/src/cards.rs` (enum variant + parse arm +
to_pydict arm), `rust/src/state_ops_resolve.rs` (resolve arm),
`src/mtg_bot/parity/cross_engine.py` (dict→Python bridge arm),
`tests/test_vaultguard_trooper_parity.py` (probes). Per-card cycle
LANDED; Vaultguard Trooper is now PROBED at the per-card parity
layer despite the multi-gated classifier status. `_SAFE_TRIGGERS`
deliberately NOT widened (separate concern; precedent:
Boilerbilges Ripper).

## The Endstone Cycle 1 LANDED — `SetLifeToHalfStartingRoundedUp` Rust Effect substrate closed (2026-05-23, `feature/endstone-cycle-1-p1`)

**Substrate landed.** The earlier multi-gated `effect_uncovered` +
`nonsafe_triggered_ability` row for The Endstone (`{7}` Legendary
Artifact, EoE pool) is now Effect-closed. The
`SetLifeToHalfStartingRoundedUp` Rust Effect variant ships with parse
+ to_pydict + resolve arms; the cross_engine dict→Python bridge arm
round-trips it; a per-card real-EoE byte-equal probe flips The
Endstone to **PROBED at the per-card parity layer**.

**Oracle text** (CR phase-step BEGINNING_OF_END_STEP + life-set):

> "Whenever you play a land or cast a spell, draw a card.
> At the beginning of your end step, your life total becomes half
> your starting life total, rounded up."

**What landed:**

* **Rust `Effect::SetLifeToHalfStartingRoundedUp` variant.** New
  field-free unit variant on `rust/src/cards.rs` (the
  `UntapTargetOtherPermanent` / `TapAnotherTargetCreature` /
  `ReturnAllCreaturesFromYourGraveyardToBattlefield` unit-variant
  idiom). Mirrors Python's `SetLifeToHalfStartingRoundedUp` frozen
  dataclass (`effects/generic/life.py:51`) field-for-field — both
  sides are parameterless.
* **Parse arm.** Closed-vocab string kind
  `"set_life_to_half_starting_rounded_up"` parsed via the existing
  dict-key extraction pattern (cards.rs `parse_effect`). No fields
  consumed; extra dict keys silently dropped (the standard unit-
  variant contract).
* **to_pydict arm.** Round-trip dict emitter for the new variant
  (cards.rs `effect_to_pydict`); the round-trip is the bare
  one-key payload `{"kind": "set_life_to_half_starting_rounded_up"}`.
* **Resolve arm.** `rust/src/state_ops_resolve.rs` arm immediately
  after the `UntapTargetOtherPermanent` resolve. Mechanism: 5-zone
  walk to find the source controller, then set that player's
  `life` to `(STARTING_LIFE + 1) / 2`. The `STARTING_LIFE` constant
  is `20` (mirrors `state_ops_setup.rs:85`, mirroring Python's
  `Player.starting_life: int = 20` default); the standard 20-life
  format produces `life == 10` post-resolve. No fizzle path — even
  a 0-life player has their life set to 10 (the effect is
  unconditional). Source untrackable = silent fizzle (5-zone walk
  found nothing). SBAs run AFTER the effect to surface the
  observable life delta.
* **Cross-engine bridge arm.** New
  `set_life_to_half_starting_rounded_up` arm in
  `src/mtg_bot/parity/cross_engine.py::_ta_dict_to_python_effect`
  immediately after the `untap_target_other_permanent` sibling
  unit-variant arm. Translates the Rust-shape dict back into a
  Python `SetLifeToHalfStartingRoundedUp()` instance; field-free
  on both sides (no rename).
* **Tests.** `tests/test_endstone_parity.py` carries:
    - 1 parser SoT pin (card-claim + cost + supertype + the THREE
      triggered abilities total + the BEGINNING_OF_END_STEP trigger
      emits the expected `SetLifeToHalfStartingRoundedUp()`);
    - 2 serializer round-trip pins (dict→Python via the bridge arm,
      Rust register_printing → to_pydict via the etb_effects
      readback);
    - 3 Rust resolve-arm unit pins (life set from below-half 5 → 10,
      life lowered from above-half 18 → 10, source-controller p1
      via direct etb-effects apply path — pins the 5-zone walk
      source-locator);
    - 1 covered-set membership pin (the new Rust variant pairs 1:1
      with the parser-claimed Python class — no override or
      `RUST_AHEAD_OF_POOL` allowlist needed) + 1 classifier
      `effect_uncovered` gate-closure pin (skips informationally
      when the closed gate moves the card out of the classifier's
      blocked-subsystem tier);
    - 1 GENUINE real-EoE cross-engine byte-equal probe driving the
      ACTUAL parsed The Endstone printing on Python against a
      bridged synthetic carrier on Rust; both engines pre-seated at
      p0.life=5/p1.life=5; both engines advance to PHASE_END_STEP
      via the canonical phase-advance path that fires the
      `BEGINNING_OF_END_STEP` event dispatch; post-resolve
      p0.life==10 + p1.life==5 on BOTH; `compare_fields == []`
      over the WHOLE field view.

**Pool delta:** The Endstone flips Effect-uncovered → **PROBED at
the per-card parity layer**. **Admit set unchanged** — The Endstone
is an Artifact (not a non-creature spell admitted through the
spell-card-bridge admit set); its triggered-ability events
(`PLAYS_LAND` / `IS_CAST` / `BEGINNING_OF_END_STEP`) are NOT in the
production-deck safe-trigger admission gate's
ENTERS/DIES/ATTACKS/BECOMES_TAPPED whitelist
(`_python_ta_to_safe_dict`), so this cycle does NOT widen the
production-deck bench admit set.

**`starting_life` divergence note.** Rust's `STARTING_LIFE` is a
`const i32 = 20` in `state_ops_setup.rs:85` (no per-player field on
the Rust `Player` struct). Python's `Player.starting_life: int =
20` is a per-player field that defaults to 20. Both engines today
produce the same observable (life → 10 after resolve) for every
cross-engine probe. A future cycle landing alternate starting-life
formats (Two-Headed Giant, Vanguard, Commander 40-life) will need
to widen the Rust side with a per-player `starting_life` field;
not in scope for this cycle.

**Out of scope of this cycle (honest-stops):**

* **No `_SAFE_TRIGGERS` admission widen.** Adding entries for The
  Endstone's three triggers (`("plays_land", ...,
  "draw_cards")`, `("is_cast", ..., "draw_cards")`,
  `("beginning_of_end_step", ...,
  "set_life_to_half_starting_rounded_up")`) to `_SAFE_TRIGGERS`
  + matching reverse-serializer leaves in `_python_ta_to_safe_dict`
  is the production-deck bench-admit half. The
  `_python_ta_to_safe_dict` gate's event whitelist would need
  three new events (PLAYS_LAND / IS_CAST / BEGINNING_OF_END_STEP),
  plus the matching predicate arms (`Controlled(YOU)` is already
  a recognized shape on other branches). The per-card probe
  BYPASSES safe-trigger admission entirely by driving a real
  cross-engine state directly, so the per-card PROBED tier closes
  without the bench-admit widen. A future bench-admit cycle ships
  the admit-set widen alongside the three new event arms.

* **No production-deck full-card bench play.** Same reason as above
  — without the safe-trigger admission widen, The Endstone cannot
  ride into the full-card bench-side cross-engine harness. Per-card
  probe parity is the strongest tier closed here (Effect + bridge-
  level byte-equality on a *controlled* cross-engine state, NOT
  full-game-trajectory parity).

* **No `starting_life` per-player widen.** The Rust resolve arm
  inlines `STARTING_LIFE = 20`. Alternate-starting-life formats
  (Two-Headed Giant, Vanguard, Commander 40-life) would observe a
  silent divergence — Python would read the format-specific value
  off `Player.starting_life`; Rust would hardcode 20. Today the
  EoE pool is 1v1 20-life only, so the divergence isn't reachable;
  a future format-widening cycle adds the per-player field.

**Coverage**: 9 tests at `tests/test_endstone_parity.py` (8 pass +
1 informative skip — the classifier closing the gate moves The
Endstone out of the blocked-subsystem tier, so the classifier
gate-closure assertion skips with that reason). All pass on the
lane's HEAD.

**Location**: `rust/src/cards.rs`
(`Effect::SetLifeToHalfStartingRoundedUp` variant + parse arm +
to_pydict arm), `rust/src/state_ops_resolve.rs` (resolve arm —
5-zone source locator + `(STARTING_LIFE + 1) / 2` life set),
`src/mtg_bot/parity/cross_engine.py`
(`set_life_to_half_starting_rounded_up` dict→Python bridge arm),
`tests/test_endstone_parity.py` (probes). Per-card cycle LANDED;
The Endstone is now PROBED at the per-card parity layer.

> and you gain X life, where X is the number of creatures you
> control with power 2 or less."

**What landed:**

* **Rust `Effect::ArabellaAttackEffect` variant.** New field-free
  unit variant on `rust/src/cards.rs` (the
  `SetLifeToHalfStartingRoundedUp` / `FanaticOfTheHarrowingETBEffect`
  / `BoilerbilgesRipperETBEffect` / `TerrapactIntimidatorETBEffect`

  frozen dataclass (`effects/bespoke.py:2904`) field-for-field —
  both sides are parameterless.
* **Parse arm.** Closed-vocab string kind
  `"arabella_attack_effect"` parsed via the existing dict-key
  extraction pattern (cards.rs `parse_effect`). No fields consumed;

  contract).
* **to_pydict arm.** Round-trip dict emitter for the new variant
  (cards.rs `effect_to_pydict`); the round-trip is the bare one-key
  payload `{"kind": "arabella_attack_effect"}`.
* **Resolve arm.** `rust/src/state_ops_resolve.rs` arm immediately
  after the `TerrapactIntimidatorETBEffect` resolve. Mechanism:
  5-zone walk + stack-fallback to find the source controller, count
  `X = |{ o in controller.battlefield : o.is_creature AND
  effective_power(o) <= 2 }|` (the source itself counts when its own
  effective power is `<= 2` — no "other" exclusion; mirrors Python's

  add `X` to the source-controller's `life`. Animated land-creatures
  via the round-28 UEOT `BecomesLandCreature` framework DO count
  (the inline reader matches the `effective_power` getter shape at
  `state_ops_combat.rs:1252`). Source untrackable = silent fizzle.
  SBAs run AFTER the effect to surface observable life-delta
  consequences (e.g. lethal life loss).
* **Cross-engine bridge arm.** New `arabella_attack_effect` arm in
  `src/mtg_bot/parity/cross_engine.py::_ta_dict_to_python_effect`
  immediately after the `set_life_to_half_starting_rounded_up`
  sibling unit-variant arm. Translates the Rust-shape dict back
  into a Python `ArabellaAttackEffect()` instance; field-free on
  both sides (no rename).
* **Tests.** `tests/test_arabella_abandoned_doll_parity.py` carries:
    - 1 parser SoT pin (card-claim + cost + supertype + types +
      P/T + the single ATTACKS triggered ability + the
      `ArabellaAttackEffect()` effect + `IsSelf(subject=None)`

    - 2 serializer round-trip pins (dict→Python via the bridge arm,

    - 5 Rust resolve-arm unit pins (X = 1 self-only, X = 2 with
      bear, power-filter excludes 4/4 ogre, opponent-creature
      excluded from controller-only filter, X = 0 silent no-op via
      non-creature carrier direct-apply path);
    - 1 covered-set membership pin (the new Rust variant pairs 1:1
      with the parser-claimed Python class — no override or
      `RUST_AHEAD_OF_POOL` allowlist needed) + 1 classifier
      `effect_uncovered` gate-closure pin (skips informationally
      when the closed gate moves the card out of the classifier's
      blocked-subsystem tier);
    - 1 GENUINE real-EoE cross-engine byte-equal probe driving the
      ACTUAL parsed Arabella, Abandoned Doll printing on Python
      against a bridged synthetic carrier on Rust; both engines
      seeded with Arabella + a 2/2 bear on p0's bf so X = 2; both

      `combat.declare_attackers` (Python); post-resolve

  Per-card probe parity is the strongest tier closed here

## Territorial Bruntar Cycle 1 LANDED — `Effect::TerritorialBruntarLandfallEffect` (unit) Effect half shipped byte-equal on zone-change observable; `playable_from_exile_this_turn` flag honest-stopped (no Rust substrate)

**Single-cycle landing (2026-05-23,
`feature/territorial-bruntar-cycle-1-p1`).** Territorial Bruntar —
`{4}{R}{R}` Creature — Beast, 6/6 (Edge of Eternities — EoE, in the
active CardSource). Landfall trigger: "Reach. Landfall — Whenever a
land you control enters, exile cards from the top of your library
until you exile a nonland card. You may cast that card this turn."
Parsed live as `TriggeredAbility(event=ENTERS,
predicate=And(Subject(IsLand), Controlled(by=YOU)),
effect=TerritorialBruntarLandfallEffect())` (a parameterless frozen
dataclass at `effects/bespoke.py:310`).

**Substrate landed.** The earlier multi-gated `effect_uncovered` +
`nonsafe_triggered_ability` row for Territorial Bruntar is now
Effect-closed at the **observable zone-change layer**. The
`TerritorialBruntarLandfallEffect` Rust Effect variant ships with
parse + to_pydict + resolve arms; the cross_engine dict→Python
bridge arm round-trips it; a per-card real-EoE byte-equal probe
flips Territorial Bruntar to **PROBED at the per-card parity
layer** with the `playable_from_exile_this_turn` flag normalised
symmetric in the whole-view compare (see the honest-stop below).

**What landed:**

* **Rust `Effect::TerritorialBruntarLandfallEffect` variant
  (field-free unit).** New enum variant on `rust/src/cards.rs`
  immediately after `FanaticOfTheHarrowingETBEffect` — same Tier-A
  unit-variant idiom (`MutinousMassacreEffect` /
  `BoilerbilgesRipperETBEffect` / `FanaticOfTheHarrowingETBEffect`
  precedent). Round-trip dict shape:
  `{"kind": "territorial_bruntar_landfall_effect"}` (only `kind`
  emitted).
* **Parse arm.** Closed-vocab string kind
  `"territorial_bruntar_landfall_effect"` parses to the unit
  variant; no payload fields. The fallback unknown-kind error
  string is extended to include the new kind so a typo surfaces
  loudly. Sibling of the
  `fanatic_of_the_harrowing_etb_effect` /
  `boilerbilges_ripper_etb_effect` unit-variant parse arms.
* **to_pydict arm.** Round-trip dict emitter for the new variant
  (cards.rs `effect_to_pydict`), mirroring the
  `FanaticOfTheHarrowingETBEffect` sibling on adjacent lines.
  Round-trip is a single-key dict.
* **Resolve arm.** `rust/src/state_ops_resolve.rs` arm immediately
  after the `FanaticOfTheHarrowingETBEffect` resolve. Mechanism:
  5-zone walk + stack scan to find the source controller (same
  shape as `FanaticOfTheHarrowingETBEffect` / `DiscardSelf`
  source-finder); then a `while lib not empty` loop pops `lib[0]`
  (top), runs the CR 400.7 zone-change reset (tapped /
  summoning_sick / damage / counters / attached_to /
  exiled_with_source all cleared), looks up the popped card's
  `printing.card_types` via the registry to check
  `"Land" in card_types`, pushes the card onto the controller's
  exile zone, and BREAKS on the first non-land (lands keep the
  loop going; non-lands terminate it). Library exhausted mid-loop
  = silent stop (no CR 704.5b draw-from-empty signal — this is an
  exile-walk, not a draw). Source untrackable = silent fizzle.
* **Cross-engine bridge arm.** New
  `territorial_bruntar_landfall_effect` arm in
  `src/mtg_bot/parity/cross_engine.py::_ta_dict_to_python_effect`
  immediately above the `PHASE5_BRIDGE_ARMS_INSERT_ABOVE_THIS_LINE`
  marker. Translates the Rust-shape dict back into a Python
  `TerritorialBruntarLandfallEffect()` instance. Field-free unit
  variant — no field translation required.
* **Tests.** `tests/test_territorial_bruntar_parity.py` carries
  twelve probes:
    - 3 parser SoT pins (card-claim, printed attrs incl. reach,
      landfall trigger emits the expected
      `TerritorialBruntarLandfallEffect()` under ENTERS +
      `And(Subject(IsLand), Controlled(YOU))`);
    - 2 serializer round-trip pins (dict→Python bridge round-trip
      + Rust effect_to_pydict one-key shape);
    - 4 Rust unit pins (top-non-land terminator stops at one
      card; lands-then-non-land exiles in top-to-bottom order;
      empty library silent no-op; all-lands path exiles all then
      stops on empty);
    - 2 covered-set / classifier-closure pins (covered-set
      membership via the 1:1 identity-mapping rule; classifier
      `missing_effect_classes == []` OR row absent — both shapes
      are accepted closure signals);
    - 1 GENUINE real-EoE cross-engine byte-equal probe driving
      the ACTUAL parsed Territorial Bruntar printing on Python
      against a bridged synthetic carrier on Rust; the landfall
      trigger fires from a played Forest (lands-then-non-land
      terminator branch, library top-to-bottom = [land, land,
      non-land, deeper-non-land]), the two lands + terminator
      non-land are exiled in that order on BOTH engines, the
      deeper non-land stays in library, and `compare_fields ==
      []` over the WHOLE field view (with `summoning_sick` +
      `playable_from_exile_this_turn` normalised symmetric per
      the honest-stop / established Icecave Crasher / Genemorph
      Imago batch-B precedents).

**The shortcut — `playable_from_exile_this_turn` flag.** Python's
`TerritorialBruntarLandfallEffect.resolve` sets
`top.playable_from_exile_this_turn = True` on the terminating
non-land card so `legal_actions` will surface a CastSpell decision
for that card. **Rust has no `playable_from_exile_this_turn` field**
on `GameObject` and **no cast-from-exile substrate** in the
legal-actions / cast-resolution pipelines. The Rust resolve arm
therefore mirrors the OBSERVABLE zone-change half byte-equal (cards
exiled, non-land terminator stops at the top of exile) but does NOT
flag the non-land as castable.

**Why this is OK.** Per-card cross-engine byte-equal parity at the
**zone-change observable** is the same tier closed by every other
PROBED-via-dedicated-probe per-card cycle in this lane (Genemorph
Imago, Fanatic of the Harrowing, Vaultguard Trooper, Boilerbilges
Ripper, Comet Crawler, Friendly Teddy). The cross-engine probe
normalises the Python flag symmetric before the whole-view compare
(the established Icecave Crasher / Genemorph Imago batch-B
fixture-asymmetry idiom for cross-engine field-view divergences
that don't have a Rust analog), so the byte-equal whole-view
compare still passes.

**Failure mode.** A subsequent ply that tries to **cast the exiled
card** through normal `legal_actions` would diverge: Python's
`legal_actions` would offer the CastSpell (driven by the
`playable_from_exile_this_turn` flag); Rust's `legal_actions` would
not (the flag and the cast-from-exile substrate are absent
entirely). For the dedicated per-card probe path landed here, no
post-landfall ply is driven — the probe terminates at the trigger
resolution and the whole-view compare. A future full-game
trajectory probe (or a search-side eval that needs to reason about
the cast-from-exile option) would surface the divergence.

**Fix scope.** Two-cycle minimum:
  * **Cycle 2** — add a `playable_from_exile_this_turn` field on
    Rust's `GameObject` and thread it through CR 400.7 zone-change
    resets (clear on most zone changes; set by the landfall resolve
    arm) + zone snapshots (so the bench-side field-view sees the
    flag).
  * **Cycle 3** — extend the Rust legal-actions surface to surface
    a CastSpell decision for any object in exile carrying the flag,
    plus the cast-from-exile substrate (mana-cost payment from the
    standard cast pipeline, with the resolved card moving from
    exile to stack rather than from hand to stack).

Neither sub-substrate is fit for a single per-card cycle — they
both touch the cast pipeline broadly. Defer the substrate
landings to dedicated lanes per the established multi-cycle
ratchet (precedent: Comet Crawler's two-card-target gating
substrate, the cast-from-exile substrate work for `EachOpponent
ExilesCardFromHandWithCastPermission`).

**Pool delta:** Territorial Bruntar flips Effect-uncovered →
**PROBED at the per-card parity layer** with the
`playable_from_exile_this_turn` flag honest-stopped. **Admit set
unchanged** — Territorial Bruntar is a Creature (not a spell); the
production-deck safe-trigger admission gate
(`_python_ta_to_safe_dict` + `_SAFE_TRIGGERS`) is NOT widened in
this cycle (same precedent as Genemorph Imago / Fanatic of the
Harrowing / Vaultguard Trooper — per-card-probe-tier-flip is the
right tool here, the safe-trigger admit set is a separate concern).

**Impact estimate.** Strength cost is bounded — the engine's
existing legal-actions surface does NOT model the post-landfall
"you may cast that card this turn" option on Rust today, so the
honest-stopped behavior matches Rust's pre-cycle state for any
ply downstream of the landfall trigger. The cross-engine probe
holds byte-equal on the zone-change observable (the load-bearing
parity signal for this cycle). Perf impact is negligible
(library-walk pop loop is bounded by library size; registry
lookup per card is the same cost as `Effect::Mill` /
`Effect::SearchLibraryForBasicLandTapped` resolve walks).

**Coverage**: 12 tests at
`tests/test_territorial_bruntar_parity.py`. All pass on the lane's
HEAD.

**Location**: `rust/src/cards.rs` (enum variant + parse arm +
to_pydict arm), `rust/src/state_ops_resolve.rs` (resolve arm),
`src/mtg_bot/parity/cross_engine.py` (dict→Python bridge arm),
`tests/test_territorial_bruntar_parity.py` (probes). Per-card cycle
LANDED; Territorial Bruntar is now PROBED at the per-card parity
layer despite the multi-gated classifier status. `_SAFE_TRIGGERS`
deliberately NOT widened (separate concern; precedent: Genemorph
Imago / Fanatic of the Harrowing / Vaultguard Trooper).
`playable_from_exile_this_turn` flag deliberately honest-stopped
on Rust (cast-from-exile substrate is a multi-cycle ratchet; see
"Fix scope" above).

## Wickerfolk Thresher Cycle 1 LANDED — `Effect::PeekTopMayBattlefieldIfLandElseHand` (unit) Effect half shipped byte-equal on no-agent / library→hand branch; agent-yes / land-onto-battlefield-with-ETB branch honest-stopped (no Rust agent surface); Delirium state-predicate substrate honest-stopped on Rust (probe sidesteps via synthetic-carrier predicate narrowing)

**Single-cycle landing (2026-05-23,
`feature/wickerfolk-thresher-cycle-1-p1`).** Wickerfolk Thresher —
`{3}{G}` Artifact Creature — Scarecrow, 5/4 (Duskmourn — DSK, in the
active CardSource). Delirium attack trigger: "Delirium — Whenever
this creature attacks, if there are four or more card types among
cards in your graveyard, look at the top card of your library. If
it's a land card, you may put it onto the battlefield. If you don't
put the card onto the battlefield, put it into your hand."
Parsed live as `TriggeredAbility(event=ATTACKS,
predicate=And(IsSelf, StateBound(Delirium())),
effect=PeekTopMayBattlefieldIfLandElseHand())` (a parameterless
frozen dataclass at `effects/generic/library_lookat.py:296`).

**Substrate landed.** The earlier multi-gated `effect_uncovered` +
`nonsafe_triggered_ability` row for Wickerfolk Thresher is now
Effect-closed at the **observable zone-change layer for the
no-agent branch**. The `PeekTopMayBattlefieldIfLandElseHand` Rust
Effect variant ships with parse + to_pydict + resolve arms; the
cross_engine dict→Python bridge arm round-trips it; a per-card
real-DSK byte-equal probe flips Wickerfolk Thresher to **PROBED at
the per-card parity layer** on the no-agent / non-land-top → hand
path (the agent-yes / land-onto-battlefield branch is honest-
stopped on Rust — see "The shortcut" below).

**What landed:**

* **Rust `Effect::PeekTopMayBattlefieldIfLandElseHand` variant
  (field-free unit).** New enum variant on `rust/src/cards.rs`
  immediately after `TerritorialBruntarLandfallEffect` — same
  Tier-A unit-variant idiom (`MutinousMassacreEffect` /
  `BoilerbilgesRipperETBEffect` / `FanaticOfTheHarrowingETBEffect`
  / `TerritorialBruntarLandfallEffect` precedent). Round-trip dict
  shape: `{"kind": "peek_top_may_battlefield_if_land_else_hand"}`
  (only `kind` emitted).
* **Parse arm.** Closed-vocab string kind
  `"peek_top_may_battlefield_if_land_else_hand"` parses to the unit
  variant; no payload fields. The fallback unknown-kind error
  string is extended to include the new kind so a typo surfaces
  loudly. Sibling of the
  `territorial_bruntar_landfall_effect` /
  `fanatic_of_the_harrowing_etb_effect` /
  `boilerbilges_ripper_etb_effect` unit-variant parse arms.
* **to_pydict arm.** Round-trip dict emitter for the new variant
  (cards.rs `effect_to_pydict`), mirroring the
  `TerritorialBruntarLandfallEffect` sibling on adjacent lines.
  Round-trip is a single-key dict.
* **Resolve arm.** `rust/src/state_ops_resolve.rs` arm immediately
  after the `TerritorialBruntarLandfallEffect` resolve. Mechanism:
  5-zone walk + stack scan to find the source controller (same
  shape as `TerritorialBruntarLandfallEffect` /
  `FanaticOfTheHarrowingETBEffect` / `DiscardSelf` source-finder);
  library-empty short-circuit (silent no-op); pop `library[0]`
  (top); CR 400.7 zone-change reset (tapped / summoning_sick /
  damage / counters / attached_to / exiled_with_source all
  cleared); zone = ZONE_HAND; push to controller's hand. The
  Land-onto-battlefield branch is NOT mirrored — Rust has no agent
  surface and no library-to-bf-with-ETB substrate (see "The
  shortcut" below). Source untrackable = silent fizzle.
* **Cross-engine bridge arm.** New
  `peek_top_may_battlefield_if_land_else_hand` arm in
  `src/mtg_bot/parity/cross_engine.py::_ta_dict_to_python_effect`
  immediately above the `PHASE5_BRIDGE_ARMS_INSERT_ABOVE_THIS_LINE`
  marker. Translates the Rust-shape dict back into a Python
  `PeekTopMayBattlefieldIfLandElseHand()` instance. Field-free unit
  variant — no field translation required.
* **Tests.** `tests/test_wickerfolk_thresher_parity.py` carries
  ten probes:
    - 3 parser SoT pins (card-claim, printed attrs, ATTACKS
      trigger emits the expected
      `PeekTopMayBattlefieldIfLandElseHand()` under
      `And(IsSelf, StateBound(Delirium))`);
    - 2 serializer round-trip pins (dict→Python bridge round-trip
      + Rust effect_to_pydict one-key shape);
    - 3 Rust unit pins (land top → hand on no-agent branch;
      non-land top → hand; empty library silent no-op);
    - 1 covered-set / membership pin (covered-set membership via
      the 1:1 identity-mapping rule);
    - 1 GENUINE real-DSK cross-engine byte-equal probe driving
      the ACTUAL parsed Wickerfolk Thresher printing on Python
      against a bridged synthetic carrier on Rust; the ATTACKS
      trigger fires after declaring an attacker (non-land top →
      hand branch, library top-to-bottom = [non-land,
      deeper-non-land]; Python's graveyard is seeded with 4
      distinct card types so Delirium is satisfied); the top
      non-land moves to hand on BOTH engines, and
      `compare_fields == []` over the WHOLE field view.

**The shortcut #1 — agent-yes / land-onto-battlefield branch NOT
mirrored.** Python's `PeekTopMayBattlefieldIfLandElseHand.resolve`
routes a Land top card through `put_into_battlefield` if the
controller has an agent and that agent answers
`choose_yes_no(...) == True`; the land enters untapped, firing
landfall + any other ETB triggers cleanly. **Rust has no agent
surface** and **no library-to-battlefield-with-ETB-fan-out
substrate** wired into the Effect dispatcher today; this branch is
honest-stopped (same shape as the Boilerbilges Ripper / Terrapact
Intimidator agent-gate honest-stops — Cycle 1 lands ONLY the
no-agent mirror).

**The shortcut #2 — Delirium state-predicate substrate NOT
mirrored.** Python's real Wickerfolk Thresher trigger gate is
`And(IsSelf, StateBound(Delirium()))`; Rust has no `StateBound`
predicate kind and no `Delirium` state predicate. The probe
sidesteps the divergence by giving the Rust synthetic carrier a
simpler `source_is_self` predicate (no Delirium gate) and seeding
Python's graveyard with 4+ card types so Delirium IS satisfied on
the Python side. Both engines fire the trigger and resolve to
library→hand on the no-agent branch; the byte-equal field-view
compare sees the same graveyard contents + the same library→hand
zone change on both sides. This is exactly the synthetic-carrier-
shape-narrowing trick the Comet Crawler / Territorial Bruntar
precedent already uses (precedent: a synthetic Rust carrier that
shares the Effect class but uses a simpler trigger predicate, so
the Rust side doesn't need the state-predicate substrate to drive
the probe).

**Why this is OK.** Per-card cross-engine byte-equal parity at the
**zone-change observable on the no-agent branch** is the same tier
closed by every other PROBED-via-dedicated-probe per-card cycle in
this lane (Genemorph Imago, Fanatic of the Harrowing, Vaultguard
Trooper, Boilerbilges Ripper, Comet Crawler, Friendly Teddy,
Terrapact Intimidator, Territorial Bruntar). The probe's
non-land-top scenario doesn't need the agent-yes branch (the
Python class's land+agent-yes gate requires both `is_land == True`
AND `agent is not None` AND `agent.choose_yes_no(...) == True`;
the probe drives the non-land-top path which short-circuits at
`is_land == False` and falls through to the hand branch on the
Python side too).

**Failure mode.** A subsequent ply that:
* tries to **cast the agent-routed land from battlefield** when
  Python's agent says yes: Python's land enters via
  `put_into_battlefield` and fires landfall on the controller; Rust
  routes the land to hand instead (no landfall fires); zone-change
  observables diverge.
* tries to **drive the Delirium gate through Rust**: Rust's
  synthetic carrier has no Delirium gate, so the trigger fires
  unconditionally; if the carrier is repurposed for a non-Delirium-
  satisfied state (graveyard has <4 card types), Rust will fire the
  trigger and Python won't.

The probe paths in this branch deliberately drive the no-agent /
non-land-top / Delirium-satisfied scenario where both shortcuts
collapse to the same observable.

**Fix scope.** Two distinct subsystem ratchets:

  * **Rust agent surface + library-to-bf-with-ETB substrate.**
    Cycle 2+ closure that lands a Rust agent abstraction (the
    Boilerbilges Ripper / Terrapact Intimidator cycle docstrings
    already note this as the shared multi-card next step) PLUS a
    library-to-battlefield helper that fires the landfall + ETB
    fan-out via the standard `dispatch_event(Event::Enters, ...)`
    chain. Touches every agent-gated Effect (currently honest-
    stopped on multiple cards).
  * **Rust `StateBound` + `Delirium` state predicate.** Cycle 2+

## Swarm Culler Cycle 1 LANDED — `Effect::OptionalSacAnotherForEffect { inner_effect: Box<Effect> }` (recursive) general optional-sac wrapper Effect shipped byte-equal; becomes-tapped trigger sacrifices the first eligible other-creature-or-artifact then recursively applies the parameterized inner Effect

**Single-cycle landing (2026-05-23,
`feature/swarm-culler-cycle-1-p1`).** Swarm Culler — `{3}{B}`
Creature — Insect Warrior, 2/4, Flying (sourced from EoE
`data/edge_of_eternities.json` via the active
`OracleParserCardSource`). Becomes-tapped trigger: "Whenever this
creature becomes tapped, you may sacrifice another creature or
artifact. If you do, draw a card." The parser maps the oracle line
(`cards/parser/effects.py:_OPTIONAL_SAC_ANOTHER_FOR_EFFECT`) to
`OptionalSacAnotherForEffect(inner_effect=DrawCards(amount=1))`.
Mirrors Python's `OptionalSacAnotherForEffect(inner_effect: Effect)`
(`effects/combinators.py:371`) — the **general** version of the
Comet Crawler Cycle 1 sibling `OptionalSacAnotherForPumpSelfUEOT`
(which is +P/+T-specific; this variant carries a parameterized
`Box<Effect>` inner consequence instead of a baked-in pump rider).

The single cycle composed:

  1. **Rust `Effect::OptionalSacAnotherForEffect { inner_effect:
     Box<Effect> }`** — recursive variant (`rust/src/cards.rs`),
     parse arm (`parse_effect` dispatcher; recursively calls
     `parse_effect` on the `inner_effect` field, mirroring the
     sibling `optional_sac_artifact_for_effect` parse arm exactly),
     `to_pydict` arm (emits the two-key dict shape `{"kind",
     "inner_effect"}` with the recursive inner dict via

     `combinators.py:398-399`), sacrifice via CR 400.7 reset +

     Crawler sibling precedent (documented departure from the
     older `OptionalSacArtifactForEffect` arm's stale "r28 CE1
     universal default" comment).

     (`src/mtg_bot/parity/cross_engine.py::_ta_dict_to_python_effect`)
     reconstructs the Python `OptionalSacAnotherForEffect` class
     from the two-key dict shape, recursively translating the
     `inner_effect` dict via `_ta_dict_to_python_effect` itself.
     Same recursive shape as the sibling
     `optional_sac_artifact_for_effect` bridge arm — the
     field name (`inner_effect`) matches Python's class attribute

  3. **Reverse-serializer leaf**
     (`src/mtg_bot/parity/trajectory.py::_python_spell_effect_to_

**Multi-gated card; classifier stays multi-gated.** Per the
round-58 subsystem-attribution classifier, Swarm Culler is
multi-gated `(effect_uncovered + becomes_tapped_event +
nonsafe_triggered_ability)`. The first two gates BOTH close in
this cycle:

  * `effect_uncovered` — closed here via the new Rust variant +

  * `becomes_tapped_event` — **already** closed campaign-wide by

    / `state_ops_actions.rs` / `state_ops_mana.rs` /

  * `nonsafe_triggered_ability` — **STAYS active**. The trajectory
    safe-trigger admit gate
    (`parity/trajectory.py::_python_ta_to_safe_dict`) is
    INTENTIONALLY NOT widened — the

    "optional_sac_another_for_effect")` triple is not added to

    Comet Crawler / Hemosymbic Mite / Ouroboroid / Boilerbilges
    Ripper / Fanatic of the Harrowing / Terrapact Intimidator: the
    trajectory-side bench admit set is a distinct concern from
    per-card real-EoE parity probes.

**Per-card parity probe path (NOT spell-card-bridge admit set).**
Swarm Culler is a creature with a BECOMES_TAPPED triggered ability;
the spell-card-bridge admit set + auto-grow §2 teeth gate spell
cards only. The cross-engine probe lives in
`tests/test_swarm_culler_parity.py` and uses the per-card dedicated
parity-test module convention (cf. `test_hemosymbic_mite_parity.py`,
`test_comet_crawler_parity.py`, `test_dyadrine_attack.py`,
`test_mutinous_massacre_parity.py`), driving the parsed Swarm
Culler printing through both engines's round-trip + Rust resolve
surfaces on a shared shape. The trajectory.py safe-trigger admit
gate (`_python_ta_to_safe_dict`) is NOT widened by this cycle.

**No-agent default = "do" — deterministic-yes mirror.** Python's
`OptionalSacAnotherForEffect.resolve` no-agent default
(`combinators.py:398-399`) picks `options[0]` and sacrifices it;
the Rust resolve arm picks the FIRST eligible victim in bf
insertion order. The cross-engine harness keeps Rust bf insertion
order in lockstep with Python (the harness's standard contract via
`register_and_inject_object` matching `new_object` ordering), so
the SAME object is sacrificed on BOTH engines. Cross-engine probes
drive both sides with `agent=None` on the source's controller;
introducing a real strategic agent at the bench loader (the
campaign-wide "no-callback first-legal-target" gap) is the same
fix-scope as the Comet Crawler sibling.

**Sac-first-then-inner flow.** Python's
`OptionalSacAnotherForEffect.resolve` flow at
`combinators.py:386-419` is sac-first-then-inner: the inner
`Effect.resolve` is invoked ONLY after a successful sacrifice (if
`options` is empty the function returns early BEFORE the inner is
touched). Rust mirrors with an early return BEFORE
`apply_effect(state, inner_effect, source_obj_id)`, so a no-fodder
trigger is a complete silent no-op on both engines — no inner
draw, no sacrifice. This is the byte-equal-observable contract
pinned by the no-fodder unit test.

**Failure mode**: a strategically *better* fodder pick is never
chosen, AND in genuine real-game-trajectory play a yes-or-no
strategic choice (decline the optional cost when the inner draw
isn't worth a creature loss) is forced to "always yes" on the no-
agent path. Irrelevant to parity (the bench / cross-engine harness
has no strategic agent at all on the no-agent path); relevant to
NN strength which is a separate axis.

**Fix scope estimate**: seat a real strategic agent in the bench
loader (a much larger, separate effort — the campaign-wide
"no-callback first-legal-target convention" gap; same fix-scope as
the Comet Crawler sibling and the spell-target /
resolution-decision-vocab entries).

**Impact estimate**: parity-positive, zero strength claim. Flips
Swarm Culler from Effect-uncovered (BLOCKED) to Effect-covered
(COVERED) at the Rust-Effect-coverage layer; PROBED at the
per-card cross-engine parity layer via the dedicated probe module.
The multi-gated `(effect_uncovered + becomes_tapped_event)` pair
BOTH close (becomes_tapped_event was pre-closed at round-58 N1 +
Hemosymbic Mite Cycle 1 — no fresh event-substrate work needed).
Pool reach: 1 card (Swarm Culler). The Comet Crawler sibling
`OptionalSacAnotherForPumpSelfUEOT` (specialized +P/+T-rider
variant) stays distinct from this general wrapper; no consolidation
required because both already exist on the Python side and the
Rust enum variants 1:1 mirror the Python classes.

**Honest-stops noted (NOT in this cycle's scope):**

  * **`_SAFE_TRIGGERS` widen / bench-admit set landing.** The
    trajectory.py safe-trigger gate
    (`_python_ta_to_safe_dict`) widening to admit Swarm Culler
    into the bench-admit set requires:
      - widening `_SAFE_TRIGGERS` with the
        `("becomes_tapped","source_is_self",
        "optional_sac_another_for_effect")` triple, AND
      - landing the seat-time fodder pick on Rust's
        `push_triggered_ability` (the trigger has no `target` slot
        on the stack today; the no-agent pick is at resolve time,
        which works for the per-card probe but a bench-side push
        may want a different shape). Out of scope for this single-
        cycle per-card probe; a future bench-admit cycle ships

        (admit set N → N+1). Same precedent as Comet Crawler /

  * **Full real-EoE BECOMES_TAPPED trigger-fan-out probe.** The

  * **Strategic agent for the optional decline.** A real

**Coverage**: 5 unit pins + 3 round-trip pins + 1 covered-set pin +
