## Weftwalking Cycle 1 LANDED — `Effect::ConditionalIfCastFromHand` (recursive `inner: Box<Effect>`) combinator + `Effect::ShuffleZonesIntoLibrary` (`zones: Vec<String>`) leaf Effect substrates shipped byte-equal on the ETB trigger body "if you cast it, shuffle your hand and graveyard into your library, then draw seven cards"

**Single-cycle landing (2026-05-23,
`feature/weftwalking-cycle-1-p1`).** Weftwalking — `{4}{U}{U}`
Enchantment (sourced from EoE `data/edge_of_eternities.json` via the
active `OracleParserCardSource`). The ETB trigger body the cycle
closes: "When this enchantment enters, if you cast it, shuffle your
hand and graveyard into your library, then draw seven cards." (The
card also carries a static cost-reduction line about the first spell
each turn — out of scope for this cycle's parity probe; the focus
here is the ETB trigger body.) Parsed shape:
`ConditionalIfCastFromHand(inner_effect=Sequence((
ShuffleZonesIntoLibrary(zones=("hand", "graveyard")),
DrawCards(amount=7))))`. Mirrors Python's two classes at
`effects/combinators.py:1513` and
`effects/generic/zone_moves.py:405`.

The single cycle composed:

  1. **Rust `Effect::ConditionalIfCastFromHand` combinator variant**
     (`rust/src/cards.rs`) with the `{inner: Box<Effect>}` payload —
     a recursive combinator whose inner Effect is fired
     unconditionally at resolve time per the documented engine
     simplification (the ephemeral `cast_via_hand` flag is cleared
     by `put_into_battlefield` BEFORE ETB triggers fire, so neither
     engine has a persistent provenance flag to consult at resolve
     time). The wrapper is preserved (rather than dropped at parse
     time) so the printed gate isn't silently dropped — a future
     engine that adds a non-cast ETB path for enchantments + a
     persistent provenance flag would land the conditional check
     here without re-touching the parser or the bridge. Same
     fidelity discipline as Python's documented simplification at
     `combinators.py:1518-1536`. Parse arm + `to_pydict` arm in
     `cards.rs`; resolve arm in `state_ops_resolve.rs`.
  2. **Rust `Effect::ShuffleZonesIntoLibrary` Effect variant**
     (`rust/src/cards.rs`) with the `{zones: Vec<String>}` payload —
     moves each named owned zone's contents to the source's
     controller's library, stamps `ZONE_LIBRARY`, clears the source
     zones, then shuffles the library via the shared dual-Python-
     `random.Random` / xorshift64 fallback (same shape as
     `FamishedWorldsireLookTopXByPowerPutLandsTapped` /
     `SearchLibraryForBasicLandTapped`). Recognized zones: `"hand"`
     and `"graveyard"`; other names silently skipped at resolve time
     (matches Python class semantics at `zone_moves.py:431-442`).
     Controller resolution reuses the
     `current_resolve_source_controller` transient + 5-zone source-
     finder + stack fallback shape that `IfNot` / `DiscardSelf` /
     `Mill` use.
  3. **Cross-engine bridge dict→Python arms**
     (`src/mtg_bot/parity/cross_engine.py::_ta_dict_to_python_effect`)
     reconstruct the Python `ConditionalIfCastFromHand(inner_effect=
     ...)` (recursive on `inner`) and the flat-leaf
     `ShuffleZonesIntoLibrary(zones=(...))` (zones tuple) from their
     dict shapes. **Field-name translation seam:** Rust's `inner`
     ↔ Python's `inner_effect` (the bridge does the rename).
  4. **Per-leaf Python→dict serializers**
     (`src/mtg_bot/parity/trajectory.py::_python_spell_effect_to_dict`)
     emit `{"kind": "conditional_if_cast_from_hand",
     "inner": <eff_dict>}` and `{"kind": "shuffle_zones_into_
     library", "zones": [<str>, ...]}`. The
     `ConditionalIfCastFromHand` leaf recurses on `inner_effect`
     (recurse-or-bail, no-fallback-hybrid teeth preserved). A
     **nested-`Sequence`-as-leaf** arm was added in the same module
     so a Sequence appearing as a child of another composer (e.g.
     inside `ConditionalIfCastFromHand.inner_effect` for
     Weftwalking's ETB body) round-trips correctly — without this
     arm a Sequence nested inside a composer would bail with `None`,
     blocking round-trip of any composer-wrapping-Sequence shape.
  5. **Coverage 1:1 identity mapping.** The new Rust variant names
     `ConditionalIfCastFromHand` and `ShuffleZonesIntoLibrary`
     match the Python class names 1:1, so
     `mtg_bot.parity.effect_coverage.covered_python_class_set()`
     auto-includes both — closes the `effect_uncovered` classifier
     gate at the covered-set level.

**Multi-gated card; classifier multi-gate state stays True after the
cycle.** Per the round-58 subsystem-attribution classifier,
Weftwalking is multi-gated on `effect_uncovered +
nonsafe_triggered_ability`. The cycle closes the `effect_uncovered`
gate (both `ConditionalIfCastFromHand` and `ShuffleZonesIntoLibrary`
Python classes flip from `missing_effect_classes` to covered), but
the `nonsafe_triggered_ability` gate KEEPS the card multi-gated at
the classifier level. The trajectory safe-trigger admit gate
(`parity/trajectory.py::_python_ta_to_safe_dict`) is INTENTIONALLY
NOT widened — that gate is about the production-deck bench admit
set, a distinct concern from per-card real-EoE parity probes. **The
card DOES move to PROBED tier through the dedicated per-card real-
EoE byte-equal cross-engine probe** (`tests/test_weftwalking_
parity.py`), the same precedent as Splitskin Doll / Boilerbilges
Ripper / Possibility Technician / Friendly Teddy / Endstone /
Terrapact / Vaultguard / Arabella / Attack-in-the-Box / Wickerfolk
Thresher / Enduring Curiosity / Terrasymbiosis / Ouroboroid / Blade
of the Swarm established.

**Engine simplification — wrapper fires inner unconditionally.**
Both engines put enchantments onto the battlefield ONLY via the
cast-from-hand path today (no flicker-an-enchantment, no
enchantment-token creation), so every fire of
`ConditionalIfCastFromHand` is structurally a "cast happened" — the
gate degrades to "always run the inner effect". The wrapper is
preserved (not dropped at parse time) so the printed gate isn't
silently dropped; the day a future engine grows a non-cast ETB path
for enchantments + a persistent provenance flag, landing the actual
conditional check is a one-line resolve-arm change with no parser
or bridge churn.

  * **Failure mode**: zero today (no non-cast ETB path for
    enchantments exists in either engine). The future failure mode
    is "flicker-an-enchantment lands the inner effect anyway"; in
    that case the engine would need to ALSO add a persistent
    `cast_via_hand_provenance` flag, and this wrapper would gate on
    it.
  * **Fix scope**: ~1 day if/when the future need arises. Add a
    persistent flag on `GameObject`, set it in the cast pipeline,
    preserve it through `put_into_battlefield`, and add the
    conditional read in the resolve arm.
  * **Impact estimate**: zero today. Strength impact is whatever
    fraction of future flicker-an-enchantment effects need to
    suppress the inner — currently <1 card across EoE.

**Probe avoids the ETB-trigger-fan-out path.** The Cycle 1 scope
landed ONLY the two Effect substrates; the full real-EoE ETB-
trigger fan-out byte-equal probe through both engines's ETB-dispatch
machinery (the Python-side `dispatch_event(Event.ENTERS)` ↔ Rust-
side ETB-trigger-pushed-onto-stack timing coincidence) is honest-
stopped at Cycle 1. The Rust resolve-arm pins drive the wrapper +
inner through a synthetic carrier printing whose `effects` slot
mirrors the parser-emitted dict shape; the dedicated per-card probe
carries the byte-equal observable (hand → 7, graveyard → 0, library
delta = +hand_start + gy_start − 7) directly via push-to-stack +
resolve-top-of-stack on the synthetic carrier.

**NO admit-set change — Equipment-style precedent does NOT apply.**
Weftwalking is an Enchantment (not a non-creature instant /
sorcery); the spell-card-bridge admit set
(`trajectory.py::_python_spell_effect_to_dict` + its §2 teeth) gates
non-creature instant/sorcery shapes today, and the cross-engine
probe for Weftwalking lives in the dedicated per-card parity-test
module per the established classifier-bypass convention.

**Probe path location**: `rust/src/cards.rs::Effect::ConditionalIf
CastFromHand` + `Effect::ShuffleZonesIntoLibrary` (Effect-class
close + parse + to_pydict), `rust/src/state_ops_resolve.rs::
apply_effect` (resolve arms — `current_resolve_source_controller`
driven for the shuffle leaf; recursive `apply_effect` for the
wrapper), `src/mtg_bot/parity/cross_engine.py::_ta_dict_to_python_
effect` (bridge arms with field-name translation), `src/mtg_bot/
parity/trajectory.py::_python_spell_effect_to_dict` (per-leaf
Python→dict serializers + nested-`Sequence`-as-leaf arm + narrow
imports), `tests/test_weftwalking_parity.py` (probes — parser SoT
pin, per-Effect serializer round-trips, full-composite serializer
round-trip, Rust `effect_to_pydict` round-trip, covered-set
membership, Rust resolve `ShuffleZonesIntoLibrary` empty-hand-+-gy
pin, Rust resolve `ConditionalIfCastFromHand` fires-inner pin, Rust
resolve full Weftwalking-composite pin, real-EoE byte-equal cross-
engine probe). Per-card cycle LANDED; Weftwalking is now PROBED at
the per-card parity layer (despite the classifier multi-gate state
staying True on `nonsafe_triggered_ability`).

## Carrier-AA substrate Phase 1 Cycle 1 LANDED — non-token CardDef `activated_abilities` field + two new Rust Effect variants (`RegenerateTargetCreature`, `UntapTargetLand`) + `GameObject.regeneration_shield` field shipped substrate-only; admit predicate + per-card probes deferred to Cycle 2 / 3 / 4

**Where:**
- New CardDef field — `src/mtg_bot/parity/cross_engine.py` `CardDef.activated_abilities: tuple[dict, ...] = ()` (added immediately after `token_activated_abilities`).
- `build_rust_state` emit + mutual-exclusion guard — `cross_engine.py` (the registry-dict emit block).
- `_card_def_to_python_printing` reverse arm — `cross_engine.py` (appended after the `token_activated_abilities` reverse arm).
- `_ta_dict_to_python_effect` bridge arms for `"regenerate_target_creature"` + `"untap_target_land"` — `cross_engine.py` (just above the `PHASE5_BRIDGE_ARMS_INSERT_ABOVE_THIS_LINE` marker).
- Rust `Effect::RegenerateTargetCreature { allowed_subtypes: Vec<String> }` + `Effect::UntapTargetLand` (unit) — `rust/src/cards.rs` (Effect enum, parse_effect dispatch, to_pydict dispatch).
- Rust `state_ops_resolve.rs` resolve arms for both Effects.
- Rust `GameObject.regeneration_shield: bool` field — `rust/src/state.rs` (with default-`false` initialization at all 13 GameObject literal sites).
- Substrate-only invariant pins — `tests/test_carrier_aa_phase_1_substrate_cycle_1.py` (20 pins; 20/20 PASS on Cycle 1 landing).

**What the shortcut is:** Phase 1 Cycle 1 lands the **Rust + bridge substrate ONLY** — the new Effect variants are parseable / round-trippable on both engines, the new CardDef field carries non-token AA dicts, and the Rust GameObject carries a `regeneration_shield: bool` slot. But:

1. **No production-deck admit.** The Phase-1 admit predicate `_printing_is_bridge_simple_carrier_aa_land` (per design doc §6) is the **Cycle 2** deliverable; without it, **NO production-deck loader path admits Swarmyard or Deserted Temple**. The pilot pair STAYS DECLINED at the production-deck loader filter post-Cycle-1 — the substrate-only invariant pins (`test_swarmyard_stays_declined_post_cycle_1`, `test_deserted_temple_stays_declined_post_cycle_1`) enforce this contract.

2. **`Effect::RegenerateTargetCreature` resolve is set-only (no SBA consume).** The resolve arm SETS `regeneration_shield = true` on the chosen creature; Python's full CR 701.15 replacement check at `turn.py:1265-1272` ("the next time SOURCE would be destroyed this turn, instead remove all damage, tap, remove from combat") is **NOT wired on the Rust SBA pass**. A future cycle (alongside the real-EoE Swarmyard probe in Cycle 3+) wires the destroy-replacement check.

3. **No zone-change reset for `regeneration_shield`.** The Rust field is set-and-keep; Python's cleanup-step clear at `turn.py:1052` (clears `regeneration_shield = false` at end of turn if unused) has no Rust mirror in Cycle 1. Wired alongside the SBA consume in Cycle 3+.

4. **Pilot-pair cost-shape mismatch.** Verify-first against the live tree (main `4eed9554`) found Deserted Temple's printed cost is `{1}, {T}` (mana=ManaCost(generic=1), tap_self=True) — NOT the bare `{T}` cost-shape the design doc §2.3 admit gate requires (`cost.mana is None`). Swarmyard IS bare `{T}` cost; Swarmyard's effect carries an `allowed_subtypes` filter (`{Rat, Spider, Squirrel, Insect}`) which the Rust variant carries byte-equal via the sorted-unique `Vec<String>` shape. The Cycle-2 admit predicate must decide between (a) widening the cost-shape gate to accept `{1}, {T}` carriers, or (b) swapping the Deserted Temple pilot to a bare-`{T}` sibling per the design doc §10.3 escape (Terrain Generator's `PutBasicLandFromHandOntoBattlefieldTapped` or Thespian's Stage's `BecomesCopyOfTargetLand` — each needs its own Effect-class port). Cycle 1's Rust substrate is byte-equal for any of these outcomes.

**Why it's OK** (substrate-only landing discipline):
- Phase 1 Cycle 1 is **explicitly substrate-only** — the Rust + bridge plumbing lands as reusable infrastructure for Cycle 2's admit-predicate slice.
- The substrate-only invariant pins (`test_*_stays_declined_post_cycle_1`) prove that NO production-deck path drives the new Effect variants through the bench today — every existing `_printing_is_bridge_*` predicate's `if printing.activated_abilities: return False` guard at the 15 sibling sites (per the design doc §1.2 enumeration) keeps the pilot pair declined.
- The mutual-exclusion guard in `build_rust_state` raises loudly on a CardDef setting both `token_activated_abilities` AND `activated_abilities` — preventing silent double-register on the Rust side.
- The `regeneration_shield: bool` field is elided from the per-object fingerprint 8-tuple (same convention as `stun_counters`, `warp_exile_pending`, `warped`) — every pre-substrate pinned baseline stays byte-equal.

**Failure mode:**
- If a future cycle widens an existing admit predicate (e.g. `_printing_is_bridge_basic_land`) to admit `printing.activated_abilities` without ALSO landing the `_printing_is_bridge_simple_carrier_aa_land` predicate, Carrier-AA cards would silently land in the bench with a populated Python `printing.activated_abilities` tuple while the Rust mirror has an empty Vec (because the CardDef's `activated_abilities` field would not be set by the Cycle-2-pending builder). The mutual-exclusion guard does NOT cover this — it only catches simultaneous-set on the CardDef side. The substrate-only invariant pins are the regression guard.
- If a real card with `regeneration_shield = true` is somehow driven through the Rust SBA destroy pass (which can't happen via the production-deck loader pre-Cycle-2 — the admit predicate is the gate — but can happen via a direct `apply_effect_pub` synthetic test), the Rust side would destroy the creature normally while Python's mirror would skip the destroy + tap + remove from combat. This produces a cross-engine divergence at the destroyed-vs-shielded surface. Cycle 3+ wires the consume.

**Fix scope:**
- **Cycle 2** (Python-bridge agent, ~1 cycle): admit predicate `_printing_is_bridge_simple_carrier_aa_land` + `_aa_is_phase1_sub_shape_a` helper + `_carrier_aa_land_card_def` builder + `_python_aa_to_safe_dict` reverse helper + admit-set pin bump.
- **Cycle 3** (Bench agent, ~1 cycle): Swarmyard real-EoE probe + `regeneration_shield` Rust SBA-consume wiring + cleanup-step reset wiring + per-cycle pool parity regen.
- **Cycle 4** (Bench agent, ~1 cycle): Deserted Temple real-EoE probe (or sibling-swap per §10.3) + 4,286-deck decline-set parity check + Phase-1 SL entry closure.

**Impact estimate:** +2 cards / low decks(1g) realized leverage at Phase-1 closure (Swarmyard + Deserted Temple); +28 cards / 34,470 decks over the Carrier-AA campaign (Phase 1/2/3/N, ~12-18 total cycles per design doc §1.3 calibration). 0 strength cost today (no admit; the substrate sits inert behind the §2 admit teeth).

**Pinned by:** `tests/test_carrier_aa_phase_1_substrate_cycle_1.py` — 20 substrate + invariant pins (Python class SoT, Rust parse + to_pydict round-trip, bridge dict→Python arms, CardDef field shape, build_rust_state emit + mutual-exclusion guard, `_card_def_to_python_printing` reverse arm, substrate-only DECLINED invariant, `regeneration_shield` field smoke check).

## Carrier-AA substrate Phase 1 Cycle 3 LANDED — SBA-time `regeneration_shield` consume + cleanup-step reset on Rust + Swarmyard real-EoE per-card cross-engine byte-equality probe (Swarmyard `covered_by_construction` → PROBED)

**Where:**

- PROBE_MODULES registration — `scripts/measure_pool_parity.py::PROBE_MODULES` (Swarmyard's `covered_by_construction` → PROBED tier flip; PROBED 382 → 383, covered_by_construction 40 → 39).

**What the shortcut WAS — now CLOSED:** The Cycle-1 SL entry above documented three gaps:
1. **No production-deck admit** — CLOSED by Cycle 2 (`0cc08732`): Swarmyard ADMITTED at the bridge admit gate via `_printing_is_bridge_simple_carrier_aa_land` + the `_aa_is_phase1_sub_shape_a` STRICT bare-`{T}` gate.
2. **`Effect::RegenerateTargetCreature` resolve is set-only (no SBA consume)** — CLOSED by THIS CYCLE: the Rust SBA pass now reads `regeneration_shield` and replaces destroy with the CR 701.15 regenerate sequence byte-equal with Python's `turn.py:1265-1278` consume.
3. **No zone-change reset for `regeneration_shield`** — CLOSED by THIS CYCLE: the Rust cleanup step now drains every shielded battlefield permanent's flag back to `false`, mirroring Python's `turn.py:1052` blanket clear at the CR 514 cleanup pass.

**Remaining shortcut (carries forward from C2):** **Deserted Temple stays DECLINED on the STRICT bare-`{T}` gate.** Deserted Temple's live cost is `{1}, {T}` — Cycle 2's `_aa_is_phase1_sub_shape_a` predicate requires `cost.mana is None`, so the second pilot stays DECLINED honestly post-C3. The Cycle-4 follow-up (or Phase-1.5 cost-shape widen) is the next Carrier-AA cycle's pivot. The design doc §10.3 sibling-swap rationale (Terrain Generator / Thespian's Stage with their own Effect-class ports) remains an alternative path; per the C2 commit message Deserted Temple stays declined as the Phase 2 (`{T}, Sac:` cost-shape widen) lane's first pivot card.

**Why it's OK:**
- The SBA-consume's regen-eligibility gate honors CR 701.15's "replaces destruction from lethal damage or a destroy effect" — 704.5f (zero-toughness) and 704.5i (walker loyalty) are correctly NOT regen-eligible per the `regen_eligible == false` flag the C3-modified `collect_sba_victims` stamps. Pinned by `test_rust_sba_no_consume_on_zero_toughness_shielded` (the honest gate-on-not-zero-toughness pin).
- The cleanup-step drain has the same CoW-skip shape as the sibling damage / UEOT drains — zero-shield states pay no `Arc::make_mut` cost; the new dict key `regeneration_shields_cleared` is back-compat (callers with a default-fallback `.get("regeneration_shields_cleared", 0)` stay unbroken).
- The cross-engine probe drives scenarios (a) + (b) with full `compare_fields` byte-equality over the whole field view — damage / tapped / bf membership all in the per-zone 8-tuple; the shield bit itself elided from the view per the C1 SL entry's per-object fingerprint convention but asserted via direct `get_regeneration_shield` / Python attribute reads.

**Failure mode (post-C3 residual):**
- A future card with a multi-AA carrier whose first AA is a Phase-1-sub-shape regenerate AND second AA is a Phase-2+ shape would stay DECLINED at the admit gate (the predicate gates on `len(printing.activated_abilities) == 1`). Phase 2 multi-AA widen pivots this.
- A future card with the regen effect bound to a NON-tap-self cost (e.g. `{1}, Sac:` or `Pay 2 life:`) would stay DECLINED — Phase 2 / Phase N widen.
- A future replacement-effect-engine port could surface an interaction where the C3 SBA-consume path's "no combat-state propagation past attackers/blockers retain" diverges from Python's per-object `attacking=False` / `blocking=None` / `blocked_by=[]` writes; field-view doesn't catch this (combat-state is GameState-level on Rust), but downstream combat-resolution observers might. Phase-N replacement-effects port revisit.

**Fix scope:** CLOSED for the Phase-1 sub-shape A admit; Deserted Temple cost-shape widen is the next Carrier-AA cycle (Cycle 4 or Phase 1.5).

**Impact estimate:** Swarmyard `covered_by_construction` → PROBED (PROBED 382 → 383; covered_by_construction 40 → 39); ~1 17lands deck attributable to Swarmyard's single-card production-deck slot (low decks(1g) realized leverage per the design doc §0 calibration). 0 strength cost — the consume + cleanup-reset Rust slices mirror Python's behavior byte-equal; no new divergence introduced.

**Pinned by:** `tests/test_swarmyard_parity.py` — 10 pins: parser SoT (Swarmyard claimed + printed attrs match design doc §2.1), bridge round-trip (`_carrier_aa_land_card_def` → CardDef → Rust dict → Python printing byte-equal on `activated_abilities`), Rust parse smoke, 4 substrate unit pins (SBA-consume on shielded lethal damage, SBA NO-consume on zero-toughness shielded, cleanup drains unconsumed shield, cleanup zero-count), 2 GENUINE real-EoE cross-engine byte-equal probes (scenario (a) baseline cleanup drain + scenario (b) regenerate-the-attacker SBA-consume).

## Carrier-AA substrate Phase 2 LANDED (Phase 2a + Phase 2b, 2026-05-25) — two new Rust Effect variants (`ReturnTargetLandFromGraveyardToHand`, `PutBasicLandFromHandOntoBattlefieldTapped`) + cost-gate widen to admit `sacrifice_self=True` + per-card real-EoE probes; Petrified Field + Terrain Generator `covered_by_construction` → PROBED

**Location:** `rust/src/cards.rs` (Effect enum variants + parse / to_pydict arms) + `rust/src/state_ops_resolve.rs` (resolve arms) + `rust/src/state_ops_legal.rs:3556-3629` (graveyard-Land target fan-out for the Phase-2a arm — Phase-2b has no target so no fan-out arm) + `rust/src/state_ops_actions.rs:980-995` (apply-time validation arm for the Phase-2a graveyard-target) + `src/mtg_bot/parity/cross_engine.py` (bridge arms — forward `_python_aa_to_safe_dict` + reverse `_ta_dict_to_python_effect`) + `src/mtg_bot/parity/trajectory.py:8476-8550` (`_carrier_aa_phase_1_effect_classes` widen to 4 Effect classes + `_aa_is_phase1_sub_shape_a` cost-gate widen to admit `sacrifice_self=True`).

**Phase 2a SL entry — `ReturnTargetLandFromGraveyardToHand`.** Ports the Effect at the minimum graveyard→hand zone-move semantics; CR-608.2b resolution-time target-legality re-check is honored (the re-check fires if the bound target left the graveyard between activation and resolve, silent-fizzling); no replacement-effect interactions modeled (CR 614 — none of the EoE printings trigger replacement effects on graveyard→hand transitions). The cost-gate widens to admit `sacrifice_self=True` under the existing Phase-1.5a generic-mana cost shape; every other cost-bool gate stays bit-identical (`exile_self`, `tap_permanent_you_control`, `sacrifice_a_desert`, `sacrifice_another_*`, `pay_life`, `requires_*`, colored / hybrid / X-pip mana) — the widen is strictly additive on the `sacrifice_self` axis. Same shape as Phase 1's SL entry 2.

**Phase 2b SL entry — `PutBasicLandFromHandOntoBattlefieldTapped`.** Ports the Effect at the minimum first-basic-in-hand greedy semantics ("may always yes when a basic is in hand" — matches Python's behavior at `effects/generic/zone_moves.py:382`); the activator's hand-search is internal to the resolve (no target plumbed, no PendingDecision); ETB / landfall trigger dispatch via `Event::Enters` (queued in `pending_etb_dispatches` for the caller to drain post-resolve, mirroring Python's `fire_landfall_triggers(state, basic)` call at `zone_moves.py:394`). Both engines mirror the "may always yes" simplification; the no-may-yes scenario (player wants to decline a basic-in-hand activation despite having a target) is not yet plumbed — future cycles can plumb a `PendingDecision::MayPutLand` if any printing makes the no-may-yes scenario load-bearing.

**Why it's OK:**
- The `sacrifice_self` cost-pay path is the existing Lander `{N}, Sac:` token-AA precedent (`state_ops_actions.rs:1190-1224` Phase 5b commit) — ZERO new cost-shape machinery. The cost-gate widen is a pure Python admit-predicate change.
- Both new Effect variants are pure no-rider zone-moves with a clear CR-608.2b-style resolve-time legality re-check (Phase 2a) or first-legal greedy pick (Phase 2b); no replacement-effect / "may" choice surface to model.
- ETB / landfall dispatch on the basic-land hand→bf transition uses the same `pending_etb_dispatches` queue every other ETB-aware zone-move (Anticausal Vestige, Astelli Reclaimer, Famished Worldsire, SearchLibraryForBasicLandTapped) consumes; landfall fan-out is byte-equal cross-engine.
- `_carrier_aa_phase_1_effect_classes` now carries 4 Effect classes; the function name preserves the Phase-1 prefix for back-compat — it's the single source of truth for the Carrier-AA admit-effect set.

**Failure mode:**
- A future card whose `PutBasicLandFromHandOntoBattlefieldTapped` activation MUST decline despite a basic-in-hand (e.g. a narrow combo where putting a basic onto the battlefield triggers an unwanted opponent effect) would diverge from optimal play under the "may always yes" simplification. The current EoE pool (Terrain Generator only) doesn't surface this.
- A future replacement-effect engine port could surface graveyard→hand or hand→bf replacements that aren't yet modeled; today no EoE card triggers such a replacement on these transitions.
- Phase 3 / Phase N candidates (Thespian's Stage `BecomesCopyOfTargetLand` / Mystifying Maze `ExileTargetAttackingCreatureUntilEndStep` / Scavenger Grounds `ExileAllGraveyards` + `sacrifice_a_desert`) stay honestly DECLINED at the Phase-2b Effect-class admit set + cost-shape gates — pinned by `test_carrier_aa_30_no_silent_auto_grow_admit_set_swarmyard_plus_deserted_temple_plus_petrified_field_plus_terrain_generator`.

**Fix scope:** CLOSED for Petrified Field + Terrain Generator under the Phase-2 cost-gate + Effect-class admit set. Phase 3+ widens each remaining Carrier-AA Effect on its own per-Effect cycle.

**Impact estimate:** +2 cards (Petrified Field + Terrain Generator) PROBED tier; -2 from BLOCKED-SG Carrier-AA row (28 → 26 cards remaining at Carrier-AA Phase-2 close). Carrier-AA Phase-2 admit set: Swarmyard + Deserted Temple + Petrified Field + Terrain Generator (4 cards). 0 strength cost — the substrate is byte-equal cross-engine; no new divergence introduced (Phase 2a's graveyard-target fan-out + Phase 2b's hand-search both have load-bearing real-EoE probes covering baseline silent-fizzle + load-bearing zone-move lines).

**Pinned by:** `tests/test_carrier_aa_phase_2a_substrate_cycle_1.py` (Phase 2a Rust substrate pins — parse / resolve / fan-out / apply-time validation), `tests/test_carrier_aa_phase_2b_substrate.py` (Phase 2b Rust substrate + Python admit pins — parse / resolve / round-trip + inversion), `tests/test_petrified_field_parity.py` (Phase 2a per-card real-EoE probe), `tests/test_terrain_generator_parity.py` (Phase 2b per-card real-EoE probe).

## Carrier-AA substrate Phase 4C Cycle 2 — Ghost Vacuum AA[1] recall variant's `grant_flying_counter` + `grant_subtype_and_pt` riders are data-carrying only at Rust resolve (Phase-N continuous-effect substrate gap, 2026-05-26, `feature/carrier-aa-phase-4c-cycle-2-flip-p1`)

**Location:**
- `rust/src/state_ops_resolve.rs` (`Effect::PutEachCreatureCardExiledWithSourceOntoBattlefieldUnderYourControl` resolve arm — Phase 4C C1 substrate at commit `8004d970`).
- `rust/src/cards.rs:11091` (the new `ActivatedAbility::sorcery_speed: bool` slot — Phase 4C C2 — data-carrying only; the CR-605.3a activation-time legality gate is a sibling Phase-N gap, see below).
- `src/mtg_bot/parity/cross_engine.py` (`_python_aa_to_safe_dict` AA-rider gate widen at line 14798; forward emit arms for both `ExileTargetCardFromGraveyard` + `PutEachCreatureCardExiledWith...UnderYourControl` carry the rider payloads on the wire).
- `src/mtg_bot/effects/generic/exile.py:993` (Python's `PutEachCreatureCardExiledWithSourceOntoBattlefieldUnderYourControl.resolve` — the layered-grant-applying side; Rust's mirror DOES NOT apply the grants).

**Shortcut:** Phase 4C Cycle 2 was scoped to FLIP Ghost Vacuum DECLINED → ADMITTED at the Carrier-AA admit gate end-to-end. The Phase 4C C1 substrate (`8004d970`) landed both Rust Effect variants (`ExileTargetCardFromGraveyard` for AA[0] + `PutEachCreatureCardExiledWithSourceOntoBattlefieldUnderYourControl` for AA[1]) + per-player-graveyard fan-out + zero-target mass-effect resolve + cross-engine bridge arms. C2 widens the Python admit gate (Effect-class set 9 → 11 + `sorcery_speed` AA-rider gate lifted) and adds the Rust `ActivatedAbility::sorcery_speed: bool` slot + parse arm. **Two Rust-side gaps remain at Phase 4C C2 close:**

1. **AA[1] recall-variant rider divergence (load-bearing).** The recall Effect's `grant_flying_counter: bool` + `grant_subtype_and_pt: Option<(String, i32, i32)>` payload round-trips bit-equal on the wire (Python forward emit + Rust `parse_effect` extract + Rust `to_pydict` arm + Python reverse arm all handle the riders), but **Rust's `apply_effect` resolve arm DOES NOT apply the grants at recall time** — the recalled creatures land on the activator's bf without a flying counter, without a Spirit subtype overlay, and without a 1/1 base P/T continuous-effect layer. Python's resolve arm DOES apply the grants (`PutEachCreatureCardExiledWithSourceOntoBattlefieldUnderYourControl.resolve` at `exile.py:993` stamps flying counters and pushes a `StaticAbility` overlay for the subtype + base P/T). The cross-engine divergence is real but bounded to Ghost Vacuum's AA[1] resolve — a code path no other live EoE printing exercises.

2. **`sorcery_speed` activation-time legality gate (defense-in-depth).** Rust's `ActivatedAbility.sorcery_speed: bool` slot is data-carrying only at C2 — the activation-time legality check (CR 605.3a: a sorcery-timing AA can only be activated during the active player's main phase with an empty stack) is NOT enforced on the Rust side. Today Rust admits the activation regardless of timing; only Python enforces the gate (via the priority-pass machinery + `ActivatedAbility.sorcery_speed` check at activation time). The slot exists so the bridge round-trip stays bit-equal and a follow-up cycle can wire the gate without re-walking the registry.

**Why it's OK:**
- The bridge-floor + Rust struct + parse arms close the Phase 4C C2 substrate; Ghost Vacuum FLIPs DECLINED → ADMITTED end-to-end at the production-deck admit gate (the predicate + Artifact builder + loader-side admit-set all admit). The Phase 4C C3 PROBED-tier slot lands at `tests/test_ghost_vacuum_parity.py` via AA[0] exile-from-graveyard resolve byte-equality + bridge round-trip + Rust register acceptance.
- The AA[1] recall-rider divergence affects only Ghost Vacuum's recall activation outcome (the recalled creatures fly + carry Spirit-overlay on Python, plain creatures on Rust); the zone-move + linkage-clear axes (cards exit exile, land on activator's bf, `exiled_with_source` clears) ARE byte-equal cross-engine — those are the load-bearing C1 substrate observables and they ship at C1.
- The `sorcery_speed` legality-gate gap means Rust accepts a Ghost Vacuum recall activation outside a main-phase / empty-stack window where Python rejects it. In production self-play this surfaces only when the activator chooses a non-sorcery-timing activation window for AA[1]; the AlphaZero-style policy head typically activates at main-phase post-combat-step where the gate doesn't bite. **No production-deck game today exercises this path** because Ghost Vacuum hasn't been admitted to the cross-engine pool until Phase 4C C2 — the divergence is a forward-looking caveat, not a regression.
- Both gaps are bounded to ONE printing in the EoE pool (Ghost Vacuum's AA[1]) and both have a clean follow-up landing path (the continuous-effect substrate is shared with Phase 5+ layered-grant cards; the sorcery-timing gate is a sibling of the existing tier_threshold timing check in `state_ops_legal.rs`).

**Failure mode:**
- A Ghost Vacuum AA[1] recall activation under cross-engine self-play: Python's bf carries recalled creatures with `+flying_counter` + `subtype="Spirit"` + base P/T `1/1`; Rust's bf carries the same creatures without those grants. Combat damage, blocker eligibility (flying), and creature-type subtype-gated effects (e.g. Spirit anthem-style statics) will diverge. No live EoE card OTHER than Ghost Vacuum's AA[1] sets `grant_flying_counter` OR `grant_subtype_and_pt` on the recall Effect — the gap is bounded.
- A Ghost Vacuum AA[1] sorcery-speed activation under cross-engine self-play: Rust permits an activation that Python rejects; the AA fires on Rust but yields no Action on Python, surfacing as a divergence on the next priority round. Bounded to Ghost Vacuum's AA[1] (no other EoE Carrier-AA admit carries `sorcery_speed=True` today; Keys to the House at Phase 4D will be the second admit).
- A future card with the same `grant_flying_counter` / `grant_subtype_and_pt` Effect-rider shape (no live EoE today) would inherit the divergence until the layered-grant substrate ships.

**Fix scope:** Phase-N — Rust continuous-effect substrate for layered grants:
1. Add a `flying_counters: u8` slot on `GameObject` (sibling of the existing `loyalty_counters`); stamp it at recall time; consume it in combat-damage / blocker-legality dispatch.
2. Add a `granted_subtypes: Vec<Arc<str>>` + `base_pt_override: Option<(i16, i16)>` slot on `GameObject`; stamp them at recall time as continuous-effect overlay layers (CR 613 layer 4 + layer 7a); consume them in `effective_subtypes` / `effective_power_toughness` dispatch.
3. Lift the AA[1] resolve arm's TODO at `state_ops_resolve.rs` (the C1 commit log explicitly notes the "Phase-N gap — logs-and-continues without applying the grants").

Phase-N — Rust `sorcery_speed` activation-time legality gate:
1. In `legal_decisions` AA emission, gate the AA on `printing.activated_abilities[idx].sorcery_speed && !(state.active_player == activator && state.phase == MAIN && state.stack.is_empty())`.
2. In `apply_action`'s `ActivateAbility` arm, re-check the gate (defense-in-depth — mirrors the Python tier_threshold check).

Both fixes are small (<5 cycle each) and self-contained — no Python schema change, no new substrate. Defer until either (a) a second EoE carrier with the same rider shape ships, OR (b) a self-play probe surfaces a measurable trajectory-parity divergence from Ghost Vacuum's recall activations.

**Impact estimate:** +1 PROBED tier at Phase 4C C2 close (Ghost Vacuum — the AA[0] exile-from-graveyard resolve byte-equality is the load-bearing observable; AA[1] recall is Python-side resolve-only on this lane). -1 BLOCKED-SG Carrier-AA row. **Phase 4C CLOSED.** Phase-N follow-ups defer the AA[1] resolve-rider divergence + the sorcery-timing legality gate to a continuous-effect substrate cycle.

**Pinned by:**
- `tests/test_ghost_vacuum_parity.py` (Phase 4C C3 PROBED-tier flip — parser SoT + bridge round-trip on both AAs + loader-end-to-end admit + Rust register acceptance + AA[0] cross-engine byte-equal resolve probes + AA[1] Python-side resolve probe with the documented divergence trace + admit-FLIP regression).
- `tests/test_carrier_aa_phase_4c_substrate_cycle_2.py` (Phase 4C C2 substrate pins — Effect-class widen 9 → 11 + `sorcery_speed` AA-rider gate widen + Rust `parse_activated_ability` accept + default-false + type-check + reverse arm + AA0/AA1 round-trip + admit-predicate FLIP + builder-gate FLIP + INVERTED Phase-4A no-silent-auto-grow walk over Mirrorpool/Keys/All-Fates).
- `tests/test_carrier_aa_phase_4c_substrate_cycle_1.py` (updated invariants — Ghost Vacuum admit predicates INVERTED to admit post-C2; the C1 Rust substrate pins stay green).
- `tests/test_carrier_aa_phase_4a_substrate_cycle_1.py` (updated invariants — Ghost Vacuum drops out of `PHASE_4_DECLINED_CARRIERS`; loader-side Artifact admit set grows from 0 to 1 card `["Ghost Vacuum"]`).
- `tests/test_carrier_aa_phase_3c_close_decline_walk.py` (updated invariants — Ghost Vacuum FLIPs out of `_PHASE_4_DEFERRAL_CARRIERS` into `_PHASE_4C_C2_FULL_FLIP_CARRIERS`; predicate-level + loader-side admit sets both grow by 1).

- `src/mtg_bot/parity/trajectory.py` (`_carrier_aa_phase_1_effect_classes` admit set widened 13 → 15 — adds `CreateTokenCopyOfTargetCreatureYouControl` at C2 commit `58988ade` and `CopyTargetInstantOrSorceryYouControl` at C4 commit `b17b0c66`).
- `src/mtg_bot/effects/generic/stack_control.py::CopyTargetInstantOrSorceryYouControl.resolve` (Python AA[0] resolve — the SHORT-CIRCUIT shape that this SL entry documents).

**Phase 4B SL entry — Mirrorpool dual-AA copy substrate + Python AA[0] short-circuit SHAPE divergence.** Ports the CR-707.2 spell-copy + CR-707.5 token-creature-copy substrate end-to-end for Mirrorpool's dual-AA carrier. The Rust AA[0] resolve is **CR-707.2-faithful**: it pushes a new StackItem with `is_copy=true` carrying the same source_obj_id as the target spell; the copy resolves BEFORE the original per CR 608.2 / 707.10 (top-of-stack-first). The Rust AA[1] resolve mints a new token-copy of the target Creature on the activator's bf with `summoning_sick=true`. The Python AA[1] resolve mirrors Rust byte-equal at the observable level: a new Token-supertype-stamped permanent under p0's control with the target's printing identity. **The Python AA[0] resolve diverges in SHAPE — it short-circuits by re-running the target spell's `spell_effect.resolve` inline with freshly-chosen targets (no second StackItem push).** Functionally equivalent for any single-target single-effect spell whose `spell_effect` is deterministic on a freshly chosen target (e.g., `DrawCards`, `DealDamage`, `Counterspell`). The end-state observables (mana pool drain, sacrifice_self, hand size deltas from re-runs of the effect, library deltas, post-drain stack empty, target spell graveyard cleanup) are byte-equal across engines on the Phase 4B C5 probe fixture (`tests/test_mirrorpool_parity.py`).

**Why it's OK:**
- The byte-equal observable end-state across both engines covers the Phase 4B PROBED-tier evidence: Mirrorpool sacrificed off bf + cost paid + the copied spell's effect resolved TWICE (once per source — the copy + the original) + stack empty post-drain. The C5 probe fixture (a vanilla `draw 1` Instant) is the canonical PROBED-tier shape.
- The Python short-circuit is the SOLE Python-vs-Rust SHAPE divergence in the Mirrorpool substrate; AA[1]'s token-copy resolve is byte-equal at the observable level on both engines (Python mints a Token-supertype-stamped permanent; Rust mints a new GameObject with the target printing under p0's control).
- For the live EoE pool today (2026-05-26), the only carrier of `CopyTargetInstantOrSorceryYouControl` is Mirrorpool; the only spell-effects Mirrorpool can target are bridge-admitted EoE Instants/Sorceries whose `spell_effect` is deterministic on a freshly chosen target. No multi-resolve state machinery (modal spells with mid-resolve mode picks, X-cost spells with mid-resolve X picks, chained Counterspell targets) is exercised by the Mirrorpool printing — the substrate gap is real but unreached.

**Failure mode:**
- A future modal Instant/Sorcery whose `spell_effect.resolve` picks modes mid-resolution would diverge between Rust (the copy picks modes a SECOND time on the top-of-stack resolve) and Python (the short-circuit re-runs `spell_effect.resolve` with the SAME modes the original spell carried). The current EoE pool has no such Instant/Sorcery that Mirrorpool can also target (the modal Instants in the pool are Counterspells whose mode is fixed at cast).
- An X-cost spell copied by Mirrorpool's AA[0] would diverge in the same way (Rust's copy re-picks X via the new StackItem; Python's short-circuit re-runs with the same X). Again, the EoE pool has no live X-cost Instant/Sorcery Mirrorpool can target.
- A Counterspell-targeting variant where the copy's NEW target is a DIFFERENT stack item (e.g., the copy is Counterspell on the copy of itself per the printed "you may choose new targets") would diverge between Rust's faithful CR-707.2 walk + Python's short-circuit. The current EoE pool has no such interaction.

**Fix scope:** CLOSED for Mirrorpool under Phase 4B C1+C2+C3+C4+C5. Future cycles that wire modal-Instant or X-cost-Instant carriers Mirrorpool can target may need a Python AA[0] port to the stack-push shape (mirror Rust's `state_ops_resolve.rs` CR-707.2 resolve arm). Sketch: add a new `StackItem.is_copy: bool` field on the Python `StackItem` dataclass; mutate `CopyTargetInstantOrSorceryYouControl.resolve` to push a synthetic StackItem copy onto `state.stack` (sibling of the round-23 `_push_synthetic_spell_to_stack` helper) rather than re-running `spell_effect.resolve` inline; teach `resolve_top_of_stack` to honor the `is_copy=true` flag on cleanup (CR 707.10 — copies cease to exist and don't go to graveyard). Estimated 2-3 cycles when the live EoE pool exercises the surface.

**Impact estimate:** +1 card (Mirrorpool) PROBED tier; -1 from `covered_by_construction` row at Phase 4B close. Carrier-AA Phase 4B admit set: Mirrorpool (1 card — the SOLE Phase-4B carrier in the EoE pool). 0 strength cost on the live EoE pool (no Mirrorpool-copyable modal/X-cost spell exists today); a future strength cost would surface only if a new printed Instant/Sorcery requiring mid-resolve choices joins the bridge-admit pool. MIRRORPOOL CAMPAIGN FULL CLOSURE.

**Pinned by:** `tests/test_carrier_aa_phase_4b_substrate_cycle_1.py` (Phase 4B C1 Rust AA[1] substrate pins — target fan-out + validation + target-aware resolve + forward arm), `tests/test_carrier_aa_phase_4b_substrate_cycle_2.py` (Phase 4B C2 Python AA[1] admit widen — Option A partial widen + per-AA admit FLIP), `tests/test_carrier_aa_phase_4b_substrate_cycle_3.py` (Phase 4B C3 Rust AA[0] substrate pins — Effect variant + parse + to_pydict + stack-target fan-out + validation + push-on-resolve + StackItem.is_copy round-trip), `tests/test_carrier_aa_phase_4b_substrate_cycle_4.py` (Phase 4B C4 Python AA[0] admit widen + bridge arms + Mirrorpool FLIP DECLINED → ADMITTED + walk inversion + pool-parity invariant), `tests/test_mirrorpool_parity.py` (Phase 4B C5 per-card real-EoE byte-equal probe — 4 baseline pins + 2 load-bearing cross-engine scenarios: AA[0] spell-copy line + AA[1] token-copy line).

## Carrier-AA substrate Phase 4E Cycle 2 PARTIAL-FLIP — All-Fates Scroll declines at the cross-engine builder gate via the "any" coin Rust ManaPool substrate gap (HONEST-STOP, 2026-05-26, `feature/carrier-aa-phase-4e-cycle-2-flip-p1`)

**Location:**
- `src/mtg_bot/parity/cross_engine.py` (`_python_aa_to_safe_dict` `AddManaToPool` forward arm — explicit "any" color decline).
- `src/mtg_bot/parity/trajectory.py` (`_carrier_aa_phase_1_effect_classes` admit set 7 → 9; `_aa_is_phase1_sub_shape_a` `is_mana_ability=True` rider gate lifted).
- `rust/src/cards.rs:15888` (`validate_mana_symbol` — Rust closed-vocab gate the Python side defers to).
- `rust/src/state.rs:942` (`ManaPool::push_coins` — the underlying substrate gap; no "any" coin slot).

**Shortcut:** Phase 4E Cycle 2 was scoped to FLIP All-Fates Scroll DECLINED → ADMITTED at the Carrier-AA admit gate. Verify-first invalidated the design doc §4.4.1 claim that Rust's `Effect::AddManaToPool` admits `produces=(("any", 1),)` via an "any" color discriminator — Rust's `validate_mana_symbol` is a closed vocab over `{W,U,B,R,G,C}` and rejects "any" at `register_printing` time; the `ManaPool` substrate lacks an "any" coin slot in `push_coins` (the `_ => return` defensive no-op would silently drop "any" coins at resolve time). Neither Option A (validator-only widen — would silent-no-op resolve, BREAKING parity) nor Option B (`PendingDecision::ManaColorChoice` fan-out — fundamentally incompatible with `is_mana_ability=True`'s CR-605 bypass-stack property) was a minimal-scope fit for a "Python admit widen" cycle. C2 ships a **PARTIAL-FLIP**: the per-AA admit predicate lifts the `is_mana_ability` rider gate + widens the Effect-class set to include `AddManaToPool` + `DrawCardsByConditionMultiplier`, so All-Fates Scroll FLIPS at the **predicate level** (both per-AA + printing-level Artifact admit predicate now pass). The cross-engine builder gate at `_carrier_aa_artifact_card_def` still returns `None` because the bridge floor's new `AddManaToPool` forward arm honest-declines `produces` carrying the "any" color discriminator. **Net loader-side admit-set: UNCHANGED at C2** — the BLOCKED-SG Carrier-AA tier does not shrink at C2; the +1 admit lands at C2.5 (Rust ManaPool "any" coin substrate cycle).

**Why it's OK:**
- The honest-decline at the bridge floor is **strictly safer** than the Option A alternative (validator widen + silent-no-op resolve), which would have minted nothing in Rust vs an "any" coin in Python — a hard parity break on every live "any" mana-ability resolve. The C2 substrate keeps cross-engine byte-equality at the loader-side admit set.
- The C2 widens are **substrate prerequisites** for C2.5 — `_carrier_aa_phase_1_effect_classes` + `_aa_is_phase1_sub_shape_a` widens are reusable by C2.5 without modification (the only Phase 4E C2.5 work is the Rust ManaPool "any" coin substrate + lifting the bridge floor's "any" decline arm).
- All-Fates Scroll's BLOCKED-SG status persists ONE additional cycle (C2.5); the pool-parity row delta is +0 at C2 close. The 5 design-doc Phase 4E test pins (§6.5 #32-34, #38-39) ALL land at C2 with the partial-FLIP teeth-trace explicitly pinned.

**Failure mode:**
- A future Carrier-AA candidate whose live AA shape uses `produces=(("any", N),)` (the same shape — see Gemstone Caverns / Sunken Citadel in the live EoE pool — neither of which is currently a Carrier-AA admit target but BOTH match this teeth) stays DECLINED at the bridge floor until C2.5 ships the Rust ManaPool "any" coin substrate. Today this affects only All-Fates Scroll's FLIP timing (one additional cycle).
- A future card carrying both an "any"-coin mana-ability AND a non-"any" companion AA stays declined under the multi-AA all-or-nothing bridge-floor contract (mirrors All-Fates Scroll's shape — Eldrazi Temple-style 2-AA shapes with all-W/U/B/R/G/C colors round-trip clean; "any" tail kills the whole printing).
- The per-AA admit predicate diverges from the loader-side admit gate at the predicate level for any card that passes the per-AA gates but carries a bridge-floor-only teeth ("any" coin, multi-pair `AddManaToPool`, `spend_restriction`-tagged `AddManaToPool`, negative amount). The divergence is **bounded by the builder gate** — the cross-engine loader always consults the builder, never the predicate alone — so the loader-side admit set is honest.

**Fix scope:** Phase 4E C2.5 — a Rust ManaPool "any" coin substrate cycle. Required work:
1. Widen `validate_mana_symbol` (`cards.rs:15888`) to accept "any" (or a sentinel byte like `b'A'`).
2. Add an `any: u8` slot to `ManaPool` alongside `white/blue/black/red/green/colorless`.
3. Add a `b'A'` byte arm to `push_coins` (`state.rs:942`) and `drain_first_n_where`.
4. Update colored-payment drain semantics so an "any" coin satisfies any color request (the spend-flexibility property — mirrors Python's `ManaCoin(color="any")` semantics at `game.py:2453-2455`).
5. Add a `ManaCoin.color = b'A'` discriminator to `ManaCoin::from_color_str` so the round-trip across the JSON-serialized pool stays byte-equal.
6. Lift the "any" decline arm in `_python_aa_to_safe_dict`'s `AddManaToPool` forward arm.
7. Add the per-card real-EoE probe (`tests/test_all_fates_scroll_parity.py`) — the C2-partial probe is in `tests/test_carrier_aa_phase_4e_substrate_cycle_2.py` and uses a W-color synthetic variant as a "FLIP-ready" stand-in.

The Rust ManaPool widen is a self-contained ~1 cycle of Rust work (no Python schema change, no PendingDecision substrate); the "any" coin satisfies-any-color drain semantics fits in `drain_first_n_where`'s existing predicate-driven contract.

**Impact estimate:** +0 cards PROBED tier at Phase 4E C2 close (the partial-FLIP — predicate lifts but builder gate still declines on the "any" teeth); -0 from BLOCKED-SG Carrier-AA row. Phase 4E C2.5 ships +1 (All-Fates Scroll). The C2 substrate work is reusable by C2.5 without modification — Effect-class set + `is_mana_ability` rider gate + bridge floor's `AddManaToPool` forward arm + `is_mana_ability` emit-on-dict + 5 Python unit pins + per-card partial-flip probe all stay landed.

**Pinned by:** `tests/test_carrier_aa_phase_4e_substrate_cycle_2.py` (Phase 4E C2 partial-FLIP pins — Effect-class widen + AA-rider gate widen + bridge-floor `AddManaToPool` forward arm admit/decline gates + `is_mana_ability` round-trip + All-Fates Scroll partial-FLIP teeth-trace + per-card W-color synthetic probe + no-regression on Phase-1-3 admits + no-silent-auto-grow on Mirrorpool/Ghost Vacuum/Keys), `tests/test_carrier_aa_phase_4e_substrate_cycle_1.py` (updated invariants — admit-predicate inversion + builder-gate-stays-None partial-FLIP teeth), `tests/test_carrier_aa_phase_4a_substrate_cycle_1.py` (updated invariants — All-Fates Scroll splits out to `PHASE_4_BUILDER_GATE_DECLINED_CARRIERS` + loader-side admit set unchanged sweep).

## Phase 4E satisfies-any-color follow-on LANDED (2026-05-27, `feature/phase-4e-payment-time-any`) — Rust payment-time "any" coin satisfies any colored requirement (CR 106.5)

**Location:**
- `rust/src/state_ops_legal.rs::pool_can_cover` — widened to count `pool.any` toward each unmet colored requirement; leftover wildcards fold into the generic-payable total.
- `rust/src/state_ops_legal.rs::auto_tap_headroom_pool` — adds an `"any"` arm to the `mana_produced` symbol match so a battlefield permanent with `mana_produced=["any"]` credits the wildcard coin into headroom.
- `rust/src/state_ops_decisions.rs::can_pay_mana_cost_internal` / `pay_mana_cost_internal` — same widening as `pool_can_cover` for the decision-callback count-only pay primitive.
- `rust/src/state_ops_cast.rs::pay_mana_cost` (legacy count-only) — same-color FIFO first; wildcard `b'a'` covers any colored shortfall; generic drain order extended `C → W → U → B → R → G → a` (wildcard preferred LAST among generic-payable sources). `pool_total` widened to include `pool.any`.
- `rust/src/state_ops_cast.rs::auto_tap_pay_for_cost` — colored coin-plan walk accepts `b'a'` coins as matching any color, byte-mirroring Python's `actions._coin_matches_color` (`actions.py:203-207`) returning True for `coin.color == "any"`.
- `rust/src/state_ops_mana.rs::GameState::pay_mana_cost` (PyMethod) — same widening as the legacy `pay_mana_cost`; preserves the legacy C → W → U → B → R → G generic drain with `b'a'` appended at the tail.

**Closes:** Phase 4E C2.5 deferred follow-on (CR 106.5 — "If a player adds mana of any type that a permanent could produce, the player chooses which type the mana is."). Closes the Phase 4E C2 SL entry's "Fix scope" item 4 ("Update colored-payment drain semantics so an 'any' coin satisfies any color request"). After this slice, the Rust ManaPool wildcard coin behaves byte-equal to Python's `ManaCoin(color="any")` at the count-level affordability gate AND at the position-level FIFO drain.

**Why it's OK (parity-equivalence proof at count level):**
- `pool_can_cover` and the count-only `pay_mana_cost` paths use "same-color first, then any for shortfall, then any joins generic" — provably byte-equal to Python's `can_pay_cost` enumerate-walk for any final-empty-pool outcome. Worked examples in `tests/test_phase_4e_payment_time_any.py`: `[any: 1]` pays `{W}` (drains any); `[W: 1, any: 1]` pays `{W}` (drains W, retains any); `[W: 1, any: 1]` pays `{W}{W}` (drains both); `[any: 2]` pays `{2}` (both wildcards drain at the generic tail); `[C: 1, any: 1]` paying `{1}` drains C first (preserves wildcard).
- `auto_tap_pay_for_cost` byte-mirrors Python's `auto_tap_for_cost` (`actions.py:919-986`) — Python's `_coin_matches_color` returns True for `coin.color == "any"` AND `coin.color == color`. The Rust walk picks the FIRST matching coin in pool insertion order; an "any" coin earlier in the pool IS drained before a same-color coin appearing later (intentional FIFO parity, NOT a divergence).

**Failure mode:**
- The count-level "same-color first" preference is order-neutral for any pool where the final outcome is "pool is fully drained" (the common case after a single CastSpell). It DIVERGES from Python's enumerate-walk ONLY at the position-level INSIDE the same drain — and that surface is what `auto_tap_pay_for_cost` covers (which DOES walk positions). No live admitted card produces "any" coins today that would exercise the path; All-Fates Scroll's AA[0] is the first.
- Hybrid mana symbols (`{W/U}` etc.) are still treated as generic-1 per the engine-wide ManaCost.hybrid simplification — orthogonal to the "any" coin pathway.

**Fix scope:** CLOSED at this slice. The per-card real-EoE byte-equal probes for All-Fates Scroll (Phase 4E Cycle 3) and Gemstone Caverns (Phase 4E variant probe) are the natural follow-ons that compose against this substrate.

**Impact estimate:** Substrate-only at the engine surface; no new admit set growth (the C2.5 admit set delta — All-Fates Scroll, Gemstone Caverns — already landed at `a82cf1e8`). Enables the next-cycle PROBED flips for both cards. 0 strength cost — the widening is strictly additive (closed-vocab pools behave identically; existing tests unchanged).

**Pinned by:** `tests/test_phase_4e_payment_time_any.py` (16 pins — count-level satisfies-any-color via `pay_mana_cost` PyMethod across same-color preference, multi-colored requirement, partial-shortfall, leftover-pays-generic, insufficient-total, pure-generic, colorless-before-any priority, mixed-priority, snapshot-rollback-on-fail, cross-engine signature parity smoke). Existing Phase 4E C2.5 substrate pins at `tests/test_carrier_aa_phase_4e_substrate_cycle_2_5.py` continue to PASS — additive widen, not a replacement.

**Amendment (2026-05-27, `feature/auto-tap-any-arm-afs-probe`):** The Phase 4E follow-on's plan-phase widen at `state_ops_cast.rs:526` (FIFO-accept `b'a'` coins for any color requirement) shipped without a matching commit-phase mirror. The commit-phase per-color-cache decrement match at `state_ops_cast.rs:614-622` handled `b'W'/b'U'/b'B'/b'R'/b'G'/b'C'` and silently fell through on `b'a'`; result: `mp.coins.remove(i)` correctly dropped the wildcard coin from the insertion-ordered vec, but `mp.any` stayed at its pre-spend count whenever `auto_tap_pay_for_cost` consumed a wildcard. The drift was confined to that one payment surface (every other coin-removal call site already routes through helpers that carry the `b'a'` arm — `ManaPool::drain_first_n_where` at `state.rs:1077`, `ManaPool::push_coins` at `state.rs:1034`, `assert_count_sync` at `state.rs:1170`). Surfaced by parity-driven probe-writing: Worker C diagnosed the gap while attempting to write the All-Fates Scroll variant probe (whose PAY half exercises `cast_spell_noncreature` → `auto_tap_pay_for_cost` against a real-EoE wildcard mint, distinct from the Gemstone Caverns sibling probe which exercises `pay_mana_cost`). Closed by adding `b'a' => mp.any = mp.any.saturating_sub(1)` to the commit-phase match. Regression pin: 4 Rust pins at `tests_rust/test_cast.py::test_auto_tap_any_coin_*` exercising Worker C's exact repro + close-by scenarios (colored cost, pure-generic, mixed pool, partial-spend leftover). End-to-end byte-equal proof at the real-EoE level: `tests/test_all_fates_scroll_parity.py::test_cross_engine_real_eoe_all_fates_scroll_mint_then_pay_via_auto_tap_byte_equal` (which the original Phase 4E follow-on landing would not have passed pre-amendment).

## Carrier-AA substrate Phase 3C CLOSED (Phase 3C C1+C2+C3+C4+C5, 2026-05-26) — CR-613 layer-1 object-copy substrate (`GameObject.original_printing_id: Option<u32>` slot + per-zone-change reset hookup) + `Effect::BecomesCopyOfTargetLand` Rust variant + Python admit widen + per-card real-EoE probe; Thespian's Stage `covered_by_construction` → PROBED

**Location:** `rust/src/state.rs` (the new `GameObject.original_printing_id: Option<u32>` slot — Phase 3C C1 substrate at commit `f5a2a1ce`) + `rust/src/cards.rs` (Effect enum variant + parse / to_pydict arms — Phase 3C C2 at commit `6de50d8d`) + `rust/src/state_ops_resolve.rs` (resolve arm with re-copy snapshot logic) + `rust/src/state_ops_legal.rs::activate_ability_dict` (Land-target fan-out) + every Rust bf-leave call site (zone-change reset hookup clearing `original_printing_id = None` per CR 400.7) + `src/mtg_bot/parity/cross_engine.py` (forward `_python_aa_to_safe_dict` arm at line 14917 + reverse `_ta_dict_to_python_effect` arm at line 12975) + `src/mtg_bot/parity/trajectory.py` (`_carrier_aa_phase_1_effect_classes` widen to include `BecomesCopyOfTargetLand` — 7th Effect class — at commits `43ed68e6` + `cc47f026`).

**Phase 3C SL entry — `BecomesCopyOfTargetLand`.** Ports the CR-613 layer-1 object-copy substrate for `Effect::BecomesCopyOfTargetLand` (Thespian's Stage's pilot effect). The new `GameObject.original_printing_id: Option<u32>` slot mirrors Python's `GameObject.original_printing: CardPrinting | None` field (at `game.py:599`); the resolve arm pushes a fresh CardPrinting derivation onto the registry (target's printing + the Stage's pre-copy AAs) on first activation, then re-copies pivot the target printing while preserving the snapshot. Per-zone-change reset clears `original_printing_id = None` at every bf-leave site (CR 400.7 — Python mirror at `turn.py:314-315` routes through `revert_printing_if_no_layer1_copies` at `game.py:1666`, which restores the printing to the snapshot and clears the snapshot in lockstep). Re-copy retention via the snapshot slot — calling `BecomesCopyOfTargetLand` on an already-copied source does NOT mutate `original_printing_id` (or Python's `original_printing`); the new printing build re-derives from the ORIGINAL printing's AAs, not the post-first-copy accumulated AAs. NOT modeled in this slice: other copy-effect shapes (creature-copy, planeswalker-copy, spell-copy, token-creature-copy via `CreateTokenCopyOfTargetCreatureYouControl`). Mirrorpool's two copy AAs sit in DIFFERENT copy-machinery families (CR-707.2 spell-copy + CR-707.5 token-creature-copy) and are Phase 4B deferrals.

**Why it's OK:**
- The CR-613 layer-1 object-copy substrate is byte-equal cross-engine — the Rust `original_printing_id` snapshot slot + per-zone-change reset audit at every bf-leave site mirrors Python's `original_printing` field + `revert_printing_if_no_layer1_copies` tail call in `move_off_battlefield`. No replacement-effect interactions modeled (CR 614 — none of the EoE printings trigger replacement effects on the copy-resolve path itself).
- The `BecomesCopyOfTargetLand` resolve does NOT write a layer-1 `is_copy` registry entry — it mutates the printing slot directly (the Thespian's Stage idiom; distinct from Clone's layer-1 entry path). So `revert_printing_if_no_layer1_copies` always fires on Stage-leaves-bf, the snapshot always resets, and graveyard re-entries never expose the post-copy surface.
- `_carrier_aa_phase_1_effect_classes` now carries 7 Effect classes (Phase 1: `RegenerateTargetCreature` + Phase 1.5a: `UntapTargetLand` + Phase 2a: `ReturnTargetLandFromGraveyardToHand` + Phase 2b: `PutBasicLandFromHandOntoBattlefieldTapped` + Phase 3A: `ExileTargetAttackingCreatureUntilEndStep` + Phase 3B: `ExileAllGraveyards` + Phase 3C: `BecomesCopyOfTargetLand`) — the function name preserves the Phase-1 prefix for back-compat; it remains the single source of truth for the Carrier-AA admit-effect set.
- The full Phase-3 Carrier-AA admit set is EXACTLY 7 cards (Swarmyard + Deserted Temple + Petrified Field + Terrain Generator + Mystifying Maze + Scavenger Grounds + Thespian's Stage) — exhaustive over the live EoE pool per the Phase 2 §2.1 30-card residue walk; pinned by `test_carrier_aa_30_no_silent_auto_grow_admit_set_swarmyard_plus_deserted_temple_plus_petrified_field_plus_terrain_generator_plus_mystifying_maze_plus_scavenger_grounds_plus_thespians_stage` at `test_carrier_aa_phase_1_substrate_cycle_2.py:501`.

**Failure mode:**
- A future copy-effect shape that DOES write a layer-1 `is_copy` registry entry (e.g., Mirage Mirror's continuous "becomes a copy" UEOT) would NOT zone-revert via `revert_printing_if_no_layer1_copies` — the `has_layer1` check at `game.py:1690-1696` would honor the lingering entry. Today Thespian's Stage is the only EoE Carrier-AA pilot of this Effect class.
- A future card whose `BecomesCopyOfTargetLand` activation must decline despite a legal Land target (e.g., a narrow combo where copying a specific Land would lose the game) would diverge from optimal play under the auto-choose path — but the Effect itself supports per-target choice via `legal_targets`, so this is a search-side concern, not an engine divergence.
- Phase 4+ multi-AA Carrier-AA candidates (Mirrorpool / Ghost Vacuum / Keys to the House / All-Fates Scroll / Haunted Screen / The Eternity Elevator) stay honestly DECLINED at the multi-AA per-AA Effect-class + AA-rider teeth — pinned by the `test_carrier_aa_30_no_silent_auto_grow_admit_set_...` walk above + the Phase-4A C1 substrate's per-AA decline-axis walk at `test_carrier_aa_phase_4a_substrate_cycle_1.py` (commit `a6fe7c9c`).

**Fix scope:** CLOSED for Thespian's Stage under the Phase-3C C1+C2+C3+C4+C5 substrate + admit + probe. ## Meteor Crater Phase 4 Cycle 1 LANDED — Rust substrate (`Effect::AddOneManaOfChosenPermanentColor` unit variant + cross-engine bridge arms); deterministic WUBRG-canonical-first color choice on Rust diverges from Python's `sorted(options)[0]` lexicographic-first pick under the no-agent fallback (admit gate STAYS DECLINED post-C1 — Cycle 2 ships the FLIP)

**Location:** `rust/src/cards.rs` (new `Effect::AddOneManaOfChosenPermanentColor` unit variant alongside `AddChargeCounterManaOfChosenColor` + `parse_effect` arm for the `add_one_mana_of_chosen_permanent_color` 1-key dict + `to_pydict` arm — Phase 4 C1 substrate at branch `feature/meteor-crater-cycle-1-substrate-p1`) + `rust/src/state_ops_resolve.rs::apply_effect` (resolve arm walking the source-controller's battlefield, unioning colored pips from each permanent's `mana_cost`, picking the canonical-first WUBRG-ordered color, minting one coin via `push_coins`; empty-union defensive fallback mints `b'C'`) + `src/mtg_bot/parity/cross_engine.py` (reverse arm in `_ta_dict_to_python_effect` + forward arm in `_python_aa_to_safe_dict` — both gated on the SPECIFIC class per the Phase-3A/3B/3C/4B/4C/4D/4E specificity contract).

**Phase 4 C1 SL entry — `AddOneManaOfChosenPermanentColor`.** Ports the unit Effect class for Meteor Crater's single `{T}: Choose a color of a permanent you control. Add one mana of that color.` AA. The new Rust variant walks `state.players[controller_idx].battlefield` at resolve time, accumulating `(white|blue|black|red|green) > 0` pip presence across each permanent's `mana_cost` to build the color union, mirroring Python's `set(o.printing.mana_cost.colors)` walk at `effects/generic/mana.py:251-254`. On empty union both engines mint a colorless `{C}` coin (matches Python's `if not options: color = "C"` at `mana.py:255-256`); on non-empty union Rust picks the **canonical-first WUBRG-ordered** color while Python picks **`sorted(options)[0]`** — `sorted({"W","U","B","R","G"})` is alphabetic = `["B","G","R","U","W"]`, so Python's lexicographic-first under the no-agent fallback is `B` whereas Rust's canonical-first is `W`. **This is a deliberate divergence under the no-agent fallback** — the user spec at the Worker-H dispatch explicitly required matching the Phase-4E `any` code-path's canonical-first choice precedent (`daecd399`, `state_ops_mana.rs` generic-drain order `C → W → U → B → R → G → a`), which is WUBRG-canonical.

**Substrate-only at Cycle 1.** Meteor Crater STAYS DECLINED at the Python admit gate post-C1 — the Effect-class admit set `_carrier_aa_phase_1_effect_classes` does NOT yet include `AddOneManaOfChosenPermanentColor`, so the per-AA admit gate `_aa_is_phase1_sub_shape_a` declines AA[0] on the Effect-class teeth, which cascades to the printing-level admit through the Phase-4A multi-AA all-or-nothing per-AA walk. The Cycle 2 widen (16 → 17 in `_carrier_aa_phase_1_effect_classes`) + admit-set pin bump + per-card real-EoE byte-equal probe all ship together as the FLIP — substrate-only invariant pin `test_meteor_crater_stays_declined_at_admit_gate_post_cycle_1` is the load-bearing closure marker. Pool-parity side-effect at C1 (Effect-coverage instrument): covered_by_construction 34 → 35 (+1, Meteor Crater's single AA now has a live Rust Effect mirror); BLOCKED-SG row 33 → 32 (the row was the Effect-uncovered axis on the Carrier-AA decline); PROBED tier unchanged — the covered_by_construction → PROBED move waits for Cycle 2's per-card probe.

**Why it's OK:**
- The C1 substrate-only invariant means the no-agent fallback is NEVER exercised in cross-engine probes this cycle — Meteor Crater stays in the covered_by_construction tier, not PROBED. The WUBRG-vs-sorted divergence is harmless until Cycle 2's per-card real-EoE probe seats an agent (the probe convention is `_PickFirstLegalTargetAgent`-style — agents seated explicitly bind the color choice cross-engine).
- The sibling Phase-4E payment-time `any` substrate (`daecd399`) already established the WUBRG-canonical-first precedent for Rust no-agent fallbacks in mana-side resolves; this slice continues that precedent rather than introducing a fresh divergence axis.
- The `{W, U, B, R, G}` color set is bounded — no `any` wildcard creeps into the Effect's resolve surface. The defensive `{C}` empty-union fallback mirrors Python verbatim.
- Source-controller scoping is byte-equal — Rust's 5-zone walk + stack scan mirrors Python's `state.player_by_id(controller_id)` lookup at `mana.py:249`; the color union iterates `controller.battlefield` only (`if o.controller_id != controller_id: continue` mirror at `mana.py:251-253`).

**Failure mode:**
- Cycle 2's per-card real-EoE probe surfaces the WUBRG-vs-sorted divergence on a multi-color real-game scenario (Python's `Agent.choose_mana_color` would pick something other than Rust's W if the agent harness's deterministic choice doesn't align with WUBRG-canonical). Likely needs the decision-callback plumbing OR a probe-side agent seating that converges both engines on the same color BEFORE the PROBED bump can land. Round-28 deterministic-mana-color precedent applies — see SL entry for `AddNManaOfChosenColor`.
- A future printing carrying `AddOneManaOfChosenPermanentColor` with an additional rider (e.g. a `tier_threshold>0` gate or a different cost shape) would NOT auto-admit at C1 because the printing's AA-rider gates would still fire independently — defense-in-depth on the per-AA admit predicate.

**Fix scope:** C1 Rust substrate (this slice) + C2 Python admit widen + admit-set pin bump + per-card real-EoE probe (Cycle 2 single combined landing or pair of landings) → Meteor Crater FLIPS DECLINED → ADMITTED → PROBED, closing the closure in ~2 cycles per the BLOCKED-tail scout's recommendation. **Reflecting Pool sibling** (~1.5 cycles after Meteor Crater C1) — the `AddOneManaFromControlledLandsProductions` Effect class has the same color-union-fan-out substrate shape, differing only in the predicate (controller's lands' `produces` instead of permanents' `mana_cost.colors`). The agent-callback color-choice plumbing is an INDEPENDENT cross-cutting slice (round-28 precedent applies); if the C2 probe surfaces a byte-equality gap, ship that slice in lockstep with the PROBED bump.

**Impact estimate:** Meteor Crater STAYS DECLINED at C1 (this slice, covered_by_construction +1 / BLOCKED-SG -1); the admit FLIP + PROBED tier bump wait for Cycle 2. 0 strength cost at this slice — the substrate is byte-equal cross-engine on the bridge round-trip; the no-agent fallback divergence is gated by the substrate-only invariant.

**Pinned by:** `tests/test_meteor_crater_substrate_cycle_1.py` (14 unit pins from C1 — parser SoT verify-first + Python class shape pin + live Meteor Crater AA-shape pin + cross-engine forward/reverse/round-trip + Rust register + Rust to_pydict + Rust resolve canonical-W pick + Rust resolve canonical-WUBRG-first multi-color union + Rust resolve colorless fallback on empty union + Rust resolve source-controller fan-out + Rust resolve color-union-scoping invariant + substrate-only invariant pin `test_meteor_crater_stays_declined_at_admit_gate_post_cycle_1` LOAD-BEARING + count sentinel for the 16-entry Effect-class admit set). **Phase 4 C1 SL entry — `DealDamageToControllerAndAddMana`.** Ports the fields Effect class for Ancient Tomb's single `{T}: Add {C}{C}. This land deals 2 damage to you.` AA — today's only EoE printing emitting it is Ancient Tomb itself (`damage=2`, `produces=(("C", 2),)`); the parser's `_PAIN_TWO_MANA_LINE_RE` regex at `cards/parser/land_builder.py:1366` captures `damage` + colorless `produces` count so a future printing with `Add {C}{C}{C}. This land deals 3 damage to you.` would claim by table extension. **Resolve order: damage BEFORE mana.** The Rust arm applies the life decrement first (`player.life -= damage as i32`) then mints the produces tuple — STEP-FOR-STEP mirror of Python's `effects/generic/damage.py:179-193` where `p.life -= self.damage` executes before the `for color, count in self.produces: for _ in range(count): p.mana_pool.append(ManaCoin(color=color))` loop. Order matters when the controller's life is exactly equal to the damage amount: under damage-first, the controller's life is at 0 (or negative) AFTER the life decrement and BEFORE the mana is minted, which is the state SBAs observe at the next check (CR 704.5a: "a player with 0 or less life loses"). The mana minted after lethal damage stays in the (now-losing) controller's pool until SBAs clear it; this is byte-equal with Python (the `.resolve()` body unconditionally appends ManaCoins after the life decrement).

**Damage applied as raw life-loss, NOT through `dispatch_event`.** Rust mirrors Python's `p.life -= self.damage` write-direct-to-life pattern at `damage.py:186` — Python's resolve does NOT fire a `DEALT_DAMAGE` dispatch and the Rust port does NOT call into the damage pipeline either. Sibling-shape of `PainForAllDamageEchoEffect` (`state_ops_resolve.rs:17571`) + `LifeLossForAttacking` (`state_ops_resolve.rs:17515`). The implication: if a future printing fires a triggered ability OFF this damage (e.g. a hypothetical "whenever you take damage from a Land" shape), it would NOT trigger — but the live tree has no such trigger interaction for the Ancient-Tomb shape, and Python takes the same shortcut, so cross-engine byte-equality holds.

## Grove of the Burnwillows LANDED — Sequence-IN-AA admit (Carrier-AA Phase-1 leaf-only → recursive Sequence) + NEW Rust `Effect::GrantLifeToEachOpponent` (life-GAIN sister of `each_opponent_loses_life`); Grove BLOCKED-SG → PROBED (the FLIP, single-slice closure)

**Location:** `rust/src/cards.rs` (new `Effect::GrantLifeToEachOpponent { amount: i32 }` fields variant + `parse_effect` arm `grant_life_to_each_opponent` + `to_pydict` arm + effect-vocab string entry) + `rust/src/state_ops_resolve.rs` (resolve arm: 5-zone + stack walk for source-controller resolution, then `players[opponent_idx].life = .saturating_add(amount)` + `life_gained_this_turn += amount` for `amount > 0`) + `src/mtg_bot/parity/cross_engine.py` (reverse arm `grant_life_to_each_opponent` in `_ta_dict_to_python_effect`; forward arms `_carrier_aa_add_n_mana_chosen_color_to_dict` + `_carrier_aa_grant_life_to_each_opponent_to_dict` + the Sequence-IN-AA emit + the recursive leaf-emit helper `_carrier_aa_seq_leaf_to_dict` in `_python_aa_to_safe_dict`) + `src/mtg_bot/parity/trajectory.py` (`_carrier_aa_phase_1_effect_classes` admit-set widen 19 → 21 adding `AddNManaOfChosenColor` + `GrantLifeToEachOpponent`; `_aa_is_phase1_sub_shape_a` Effect-class gate factored into `_carrier_aa_effect_class_admitted` with the recursive Sequence arm — the LOAD-BEARING substrate).

**The Sequence-IN-AA admit (the novel substrate).** Grove's AA[1] body is `Sequence(AddNManaOfChosenColor(1, ('R','G')), GrantLifeToEachOpponent(1))` — a combinator, not a bare leaf. The Carrier-AA Phase-1 admit was LEAF-only (`type(aa.effect) in _carrier_aa_phase_1_effect_classes()`). The new `_carrier_aa_effect_class_admitted` helper admits a `Sequence` iff EVERY leaf is itself recursively admitted (an exact-class match on the leaf classes preserves the Phase-1 specificity contract — a subclass of an admitted leaf does NOT auto-admit). The bridge floor `_python_aa_to_safe_dict` provides the byte-equality teeth in lockstep: its Sequence arm recurses each child through `_carrier_aa_seq_leaf_to_dict` all-or-nothing — a child with no forward arm declines the whole Sequence, so an admit-set/bridge-floor drift fails honestly rather than silently dropping a child. This substrate amortizes to any future Carrier-AA card with a multi-step Sequence resolve body whose leaves all admit.

**`GrantLifeToEachOpponent` resolve as direct life-gain via `gain_life` semantics (NOT through a triggered LIFE_GAINED dispatch).** The Rust arm mirrors Python's `GrantLifeToEachOpponent.resolve` (`effects/generic/life.py:603`) which routes each opponent through `game.gain_life` (`game.py:1358`): adds `amount` to the opponent's life AND increments `life_gained_this_turn` (used by `ConditionalIfYouGainedLifeAtLeast` / Ragost). Neither engine fires a "life gained" triggered-ability dispatch off the gain — Python's `gain_life` is a direct field write with a tracker bump, and the Rust port matches it (same shortcut both engines, sibling of the `GainLife` arm at `state_ops_resolve.rs:2435`). The implication: a future printing firing a triggered ability OFF an opponent's life gain from this effect would NOT trigger — but the live tree has no such interaction for Grove, and both engines take the same shortcut, so cross-engine byte-equality holds.

**No no-agent-fallback color-picker divergence to gate around (unlike Meteor Crater C2 / Reflecting Pool C2).** Grove's `AddNManaOfChosenColor(1, ('R','G'))` carries a FIXED 2-tuple options list from the parser — NOT a board-walk union. Both engines pick `options[0]='R'` under the no-agent fallback (Python `effects/generic/mana.py:115` `opts[0]`; Rust `state_ops_resolve.rs:14055+` first-option fallback), so both deterministic-mint `R` byte-equal with no seating constraint. The MC/RP WUBRG-canonical-vs-sorted-alphabetic divergence (gated to multi-color unions) is structurally absent here. The agent-callback color-choice plumbing through `choose_mana_color` is exercised by neither engine in the probe (no agent seated); if a future probe scenario seats an agent that returns a non-`options[0]` color, both engines must agree on the chosen color — they read the same agent callback, so the contract holds, but the no-agent path is the one pinned today.

**Why it's OK:**
- Both AAs are byte-equal cross-engine under the live fixture: AA[0] mints 1 `C` coin (no life change); AA[1] mints 1 `R` coin + the one opponent gains 1 life (20 → 21), both lives + both pools byte-equal on both engines (pinned by `test_grove_of_the_burnwillows_parity.py` Scenarios MINT-C + MINT-R+LIFE).
- `GrantLifeToEachOpponent` fields exactly mirror Python's dataclass (`amount: int = 1`); the wire dict always emits `amount` explicitly. Source-controller scoping is byte-equal (the 5-zone walk + stack scan is verbatim the round-26 `EachOpponentLosesLife` template; only the apply step flips sub→add).
- The `life_gained_this_turn` tracker increment is symmetric Python parity (not a Rust-only behavior); a future `ConditionalIfYouGainedLifeAtLeast` consumer reading the opponent's tracker sees the same value on both engines.
- The Sequence-IN-AA recursion preserves the Phase-1 specificity contract (exact-class leaf match) and the all-or-nothing bridge-floor recursion guarantees no silently-dropped child.

**Failure mode:**
- A silently-added Effect class to `_carrier_aa_phase_1_effect_classes` that admits an unexpected card surfaces at the count sentinel `test_grove_carrier_aa_effect_classes_count` (pins the 21-entry size).
- A future Sequence-carrying Carrier-AA whose leaf class is in the admit set but whose forward arm is missing declines at the bridge-floor recursion (`_carrier_aa_seq_leaf_to_dict` returns None) — defense-in-depth, pinned by `test_grove_sequence_in_aa_admit_invariant` (a Sequence with a `DrawCards` leaf declines).
- A future engine-side refactor that wires a LIFE_GAINED triggered dispatch into one engine's life-gain path but not the other surfaces as a cross-engine divergence; both engines need the change in lockstep.

**Fix scope:** Single-slice closure (this slice) — new Rust `Effect::GrantLifeToEachOpponent` end-to-end + the two leaf-class admit widens + the Sequence-IN-AA admit + the per-card real-EoE probe. `AddNManaOfChosenColor` was already live on the Rust side (round-21 / Phase-4E mana bridge slice) — this slice only added its cross-engine forward arm + admit-set entry. Grove FLIPS DECLINED → ADMITTED → PROBED in one slice (the scout's §#3 ~2-3 cycle estimate; the Sequence factor-out turned out to be one clean recursive helper).

**Impact estimate:** Grove FLIPS BLOCKED-SG → PROBED (covered_by_construction → PROBED via the probe). PROBED 434 → 435; BLOCKED-SG 30 → 29; Carrier-AA BLOCKED bucket 15 → 14; Effect-uncovered 22 → 21. Rust Effect coverage 190 → 191 Python classes (224 → 225 Rust variants). 0 strength cost — the substrate is byte-equal cross-engine on both AAs' real-EoE drive.

**Pinned by:** `tests/test_grove_of_the_burnwillows_parity.py` (9 pins — parser SoT verify-first + Python dual-AA shape pin + bridge round-trip canonical Rust dict + reverse-arm rehydration of both AAs + Rust register acceptance + loader end-to-end admit + cross-engine real-EoE Scenario MINT-C (AA[0] 1-C mint) + cross-engine real-EoE Scenario MINT-R+LIFE (AA[1] Sequence: 1-R chosen-color mint + each-opponent +1 life, LOAD-BEARING) + Sequence-IN-AA admit invariant (admits valid Sequence, declines Sequence-with-non-admitted-leaf, declines bare non-admitted leaf, admits nested Sequence) + 21-entry count sentinel). **Status (feature/fumarole-ptswitch, 2026-06-01): the layer-7e swap is
REAL.** The prior substrate-only no-op is replaced. What remained
