## Rust `Effect::SacrificeNLandsYouControl` — deterministic no-agent land pick + Lotus Field composite-admit honest-stop (2026-05-31)

**Where:** `rust/src/cards.rs` (`Effect::SacrificeNLandsYouControl { count }` decl + `parse_effect` + `effect_to_pydict`), `rust/src/state_ops_resolve.rs` (resolve arm — the `while remaining > 0` rescan-pick-first-eligible-land-excluding-source loop), `src/mtg_bot/parity/cross_engine.py` (`_ta_dict_to_python_effect` reverse arm).

**What the shortcut is:**
- The Rust resolve arm mirrors Python's `SacrificeNLandsYouControl.resolve` (`effects/generic/zone_moves.py:236`) deterministic NO-AGENT path: each loop iteration rescans the source-controller's battlefield for the smallest-index LAND whose id != source (the entering Lotus Field is excluded), picks it (Python's `options[0]`), and sacrifices it. Real MTG (CR 701.16) lets the controller choose WHICH lands to sacrifice; both engines instead pick the canonical-first land under the no-agent harness. This is the SAME no-agent-first-legal convention already documented for `choose_sacrifice` in §5 and the round-31 `SacrificeFirstPermanentYouControl` bridge target.
- **Lotus Field STAYS BLOCKED at the loader admit gate this slice (substrate-only landing).** The scout (`docs/BLOCKED_TAIL_TRACTABILITY_SCOUT_2026-05-27.md` §Lotus Field) estimated the only uncovered piece was the `SacrificeNLandsYouControl` ETB Effect, with enters-tapped + hexproof "already covered". That under-counted the loader admit surface: Lotus Field is a COMPOSITE carrier (chosen-color mana AA + `enters_tapped=True` + `keywords={hexproof}` + an ETB `triggered_abilities`). NO existing bridge admit predicate accepts that combination — `_printing_is_bridge_simple_carrier_aa_land` hard-declines any printing with `keywords` (`trajectory.py:9847`) AND any with `triggered_abilities` (`trajectory.py:9849`); the tapped-mana-land predicates decline any printing with activated/triggered abilities. Admitting Lotus Field needs a brand-new composite-admit path (mana AA + enters_tapped + hexproof + ETB trigger co-gated on one printing) — left as characterized follow-up work.

**Why this is OK:**
- The deterministic land pick is byte-equal cross-engine (both engines pick `options[0]` / smallest-index eligible land per rescan), so the resulting battlefield/graveyard split agrees bit-for-bit on the controlled probe. Under the bench play strategy (no agent installed), this is the only path taken.
- The substrate is genuinely uncovered (no prior Rust `SacrificeNLandsYouControl` variant) and amortizes to any future card with that ETB effect. Landing it cleared the Effect-uncovered axis for Lotus Field (BLOCKED → covered-by-construction) without a fragile composite-admit flip — a characterized honest-stop per the campaign policy.
- The ETB-effect resolve dispatch is the same `apply_effect` path whether the effect rode a trigger or an AA, so the Rust unit pins (driving it as a mana-ability AA for harness convenience) exercise the real resolve semantics.

**Failure mode:**
- A real game where the optimal play is to sacrifice a DIFFERENT land (e.g. keeping a dual, sac'ing basics) is not modeled — both engines sac the canonical-first lands. Same class as the existing `choose_sacrifice → first legal` default.
- A future composite-admit widen that flips Lotus Field to loader-admitted will trip the LOAD-BEARING `test_lotus_field_stays_declined_at_loader_admit_gate` pin — the author must then update it to the PROBED-tier expectation deliberately rather than silently auto-admitting the unmodeled rider cluster.

**Fix scope:** Substrate-only this slice — new Rust `Effect::SacrificeNLandsYouControl` end-to-end (decl + parse + to_pydict + resolve) + cross-engine bridge reverse arm + the per-card real-EoE probe (SAC-TWO / SAC-UNDER / MINT-3 byte-equal). The composite-admit path (chosen-color-mana-land + enters_tapped + hexproof + ETB trigger co-gated) is a future cycle.

**Impact estimate:** Lotus Field moves BLOCKED (Effect-uncovered) → covered-by-construction. PROBED 446 (unchanged — Lotus Field is NOT loader-admitted, so it cannot be PROBED this slice); covered_by_construction 0 → 1; BLOCKED-SG 29 → 28. 0 strength cost — the substrate is byte-equal cross-engine on the real-EoE drive of both the ETB sac path and the {T}:add-3-chosen-color mana path.

## Lotus Field composite loader-admit — `enters_tapped` symmetric drop + narrow composite carrier path (2026-05-31)

**Where:** `src/mtg_bot/parity/trajectory.py` (`_printing_is_bridge_carrier_aa_land_with_etb_sac_and_keyword` composite-admit predicate + `_carrier_aa_land_with_etb_sac_and_keyword_card_def` builder + the `_printing_to_card_def` dispatch arm + the `_filter_deck_to_bridge_supported` OR-disjunct). PYTHON-ONLY — no `rust/` change (the `Effect::SacrificeNLandsYouControl` Rust variant + reverse bridge arm landed at merge `5dbb9c37`; the keyword + mana-AA pieces round-trip through the pre-existing `keywords` Vec + `_python_aa_to_safe_dict` floor with Phase-4E's mana-AA lift).

**What the shortcut is:**
- **Composite carrier admit (the closure).** A brand-new NARROW admit predicate co-gates all four Lotus Field riders on one printing: a single chosen-color mana AA (`AddNManaOfChosenColor(3, WUBRG)`) + `enters_tapped=True` + `keywords ⊆ {hexproof}` + EXACTLY one ETB `IsSelf` triggered ability whose effect is the bridge-admitted `SacrificeNLandsYouControl`. It admits ONLY the exact Lotus Field shape (Phase-1 specificity contract — NOT a widen of the Carrier-AA Land predicate, which still hard-declines on `keywords` + `triggered_abilities`). The builder emits all four pieces all-or-nothing (the mana AA via the safe-dict round-trip floor, the keyword via the CardDef `keywords` field, the ETB trigger emitted directly as a `{"event": "enters", "predicate": {"kind": "source_is_self"}, "effect": {"kind": "sacrifice_n_lands_you_control", "count": N}}` round-trip dict — NOT via the generic `_python_ta_to_safe_dict` gate, keeping that gate un-widened).
- **`enters_tapped` symmetric drop (the deliberate simplification).** The CardDef bridge carries no plain `enters_tapped` field, and Rust's `register_printing` has no land-tapped-entry path. The predicate POSITIVELY requires `enters_tapped=True` (to identify Lotus Field's shape), but the builder DROPS it symmetrically — both engines materialize Lotus Field as an UNTAPPED land. This is the round-85 Planet land / Cathedral of War symmetric-drop precedent extended to the composite shape.
- **`hexproof` admitted as a static Land keyword.** `hexproof` is NOT in `_SAFE_KEYWORDS` (that set is the combat-relevant creature-keyword whitelist; hexproof's targeting-protection lifecycle is fragile in the trajectory CREATURE context). On a LAND it round-trips as a pure stored `keywords` data field (Python frozenset ↔ Rust Vec), gated by a dedicated single-member `_LOTUS_FIELD_COMPOSITE_SAFE_KEYWORDS = {hexproof}` set so the Phase-1 specificity contract holds (a future keyword on this shape fails loudly at the subset gate rather than riding through).

**Why this is OK:**
- The `enters_tapped` drop is byte-equal cross-engine — both engines build the land untapped from the CardDef default; neither honors a tapped-entry it never received. Under the bench play strategy (no agent) the tapped-vs-untapped delta only affects whether the land could tap for mana the turn it entered; the symmetric drop means both engines agree bit-for-bit at every observable.
- The `hexproof` drop-into-data is byte-equal — neither engine's bench moves target a land, so the land's hexproof is never exercised; it round-trips as identical stored data on both sides.
- The ETB sac + the chosen-color mana mint both resolve byte-equal cross-engine on the loader-built printing (the SAC-TWO / SAC-UNDER / MINT-3 probes drive the ACTUAL `_printing_to_card_def(Lotus Field)` → Rust registry dict end-to-end, not a hand-wired synthetic). The composite admit therefore proves the full real-EoE Lotus Field shape, not just its primitives.

**Failure mode:**
- A real game where Lotus Field's tapped-entry matters (e.g. a turn-timing line that depends on it not being available for mana the turn it's played) is not modeled — both engines treat it as untapped. CR-incomplete; same class as the round-85 Planet land / Cathedral of War tapped-entry drops.
- A regression that drops the composite admit (or silently auto-admits Lotus Field via the broad Carrier-AA path) trips the `test_lotus_field_admitted_at_loader_admit_gate` ADMIT pin.

**Fix scope:** A full-fidelity tapped-entry would need a plain `enters_tapped` bool on CardDef + a matching Rust land-tapped-entry play path (distinct from the existing conditional-painland `enters_tapped_unless_any_player_life_at_most` threshold). Deferred — the symmetric drop is byte-equal under the bench, and the tapped-entry fidelity gap is shared with every other admitted tapped land.

**Impact estimate:** Lotus Field moves covered-by-construction → PROBED. PROBED 448 → 449; covered_by_construction 1 → 0; BLOCKED-SG 26 unchanged. 0 strength cost — byte-equal cross-engine on the real-EoE loader-built drive of the ETB sac path AND the {T}:add-3-chosen-color mana path; the two drops (tapped-entry, land-hexproof) are symmetric and bench-unobservable.

**Pinned by:** `tests/test_lotus_field_parity.py` (11 pins — the original 8 [parser SoT verify-first, the now-flipped LOADER-ADMIT pin, bridge reverse-arm round-trip, Rust register acceptance, synthetic-driven SAC-TWO / SAC-UNDER / MINT-3] + 3 NEW composite-loader-admit real-EoE probes driving the ACTUAL `_printing_to_card_def` → Rust registry dict end-to-end [loader-admit SAC-TWO / SAC-UNDER / MINT-3]). Probe module registered in `scripts/measure_pool_parity.py` PROBE_MODULES; PROBED attribution via the existing `test_cross_engine_real_eoe_lotus_field_*_parity` functions' `_PRINTINGS["Lotus Field"]` references.

## Rust `Effect::MovePlusOneCounterBetweenPermanentsYouControl` — Nesting Grounds dual-target-AA FLIP + bare-`+1` increment (doubling / observer-trigger surface not mirrored) (2026-05-31)

**Location:** `rust/src/cards.rs` (`Effect::MovePlusOneCounterBetweenPermanentsYouControl` unit variant decl + parse_effect arm + to_pydict arm), `rust/src/state_ops_resolve.rs` (`apply_effect` dual-target resolve arm reading `current_resolve_payload_target_id` / `_2`; + the trigger resolve entry points' `current_resolve_payload_target_id_2 = payload.target_id_2` swap), `rust/src/actions.rs` + `rust/src/state_ops_actions.rs` (`Action::ActivateAbility.target_creature_id_2` field + dual-target validation + `new_trigger_with_two_targets` push), `rust/src/state.rs` (`TriggerPayload.target_id_2` + `StackItem::new_trigger_with_two_targets`), `src/mtg_bot/parity/cross_engine.py` (`_python_aa_to_safe_dict` forward arm + `_ta_dict_to_python_effect` reverse arm).

**FLIP context.** The substrate landing (`c995ac04`) shipped the Rust Effect end-to-end (decl + parse + to_pydict + dual-target resolve via the 2-slot `current_resolve_payload_target_id` / `_2` plumbing + cross-engine bridge arms) but left Nesting Grounds DECLINED because the Rust Carrier-AA *activation* path bound only ONE target (`new_trigger_with_target` → slot 0). THIS slice closed that gap: a SECOND `Action::ActivateAbility.target_creature_id_2` field threads the recipient onto the StackItem's `trigger_payload.target_id_2` (new `StackItem::new_trigger_with_two_targets` constructor), and the trigger resolve entry points swap it into `current_resolve_payload_target_id_2` (mirroring the spell-cast path's `target_obj_id_2` swap). With the gap closed, the Effect class joined `_carrier_aa_phase_1_effect_classes` (admit set 21 → 22) and Nesting Grounds FLIPPED covered_by_construction → PROBED. **The cost/rider/Land-carrier surface was always accepted** (`_aa_is_phase1_sub_shape_a` admits the `{1}{T}` generic-only cost + `sorcery_speed=True` rider; `_printing_is_bridge_simple_carrier_aa_land` admits the printing) — the only walls were the Effect-class omission + the now-closed AA 2nd-target slot.

**What the remaining shortcut is:**

**Bare-`+1` increment — Loading-Zone doubling + Terrasymbiosis observer triggers NOT mirrored.** Python's recipient-side counter add routes through `game.add_plus_one_counters` (`game.py:2023`), which (a) multiplies the count by `_counter_doubling_factor` (Loading-Zone-style doublers controlled by the recipient's controller) and (b) fires `fire_counters_added_to_your_creature_triggers` (Terrasymbiosis-style observer triggers) when the recipient is a creature. The Rust resolve arm increments `obj.counters` by a flat `+1` ONLY — neither the doubling factor nor the observer triggers are replicated.

**Why it's OK:** the per-card real-EoE byte-equal probe (including the load-bearing AA-activation scenario) + the tests_rust pins all seat NO doublers (factor 1) and use a recipient where the observer-trigger surface is dormant, so both engines move exactly one counter byte-equal. The PROBED-tier evidence is honest: it asserts byte-equality on a controlled state where the doubler/observer surface is provably absent, NOT a claim that every Nesting-Grounds board plays byte-equal. A real game where the recipient's controller has a Loading-Zone-style doubler or a Terrasymbiosis observer would diverge — that surface is the documented remaining gap below.

**Failure mode:** a board with a recipient-controlled Loading Zone (or a Terrasymbiosis-style observer) diverges: Python moves 2 counters / fires the observer; Rust moves 1 / fires nothing. EoE itself has no `+1/+1`-counter doubler or `counters-added` observer permanent in the pool, so this surface is unreachable from the EoE pool today (it would only bite under a cross-set board state). The probe's narrow seating keeps the byte-equal teeth honest by construction.

**Fix scope:** port `_counter_doubling_factor` (Loading-Zone replacement) + the `fire_counters_added_to_your_creature_triggers` observer to the Rust counter-add path. Out of scope for the EoE pool (no doubler/observer card in EoE); a follow-up if a cross-set board makes it reachable.

**Impact estimate:** Nesting Grounds FLIPS covered_by_construction → PROBED. PROBED 449 → 450; covered_by_construction 1 → 0; BLOCKED-SG 25 unchanged. The Effect-class admit set grows 21 → 22 (Nesting Grounds is the SOLE EoE carrier of the new class — verified no-auto-grow via the full-pool admit invariant in `test_carrier_aa_phase_4b_substrate_cycle_4.py::test_full_pool_admit_set_grows_by_exactly_one_post_c4`). 0 strength cost — the AA-activation path now drives the real dual-target counter move byte-equal cross-engine.

**Pinned by:** `tests/test_nesting_grounds_parity.py` (12 pins — parser SoT verify-first + printed-attrs incl. the dual-target teeth + the LOAD-BEARING loader-ADMIT FLIP pin (`test_nesting_grounds_now_admits_at_loader_admit_gate`) + the cost/rider-admit characterization + bridge forward/reverse/effect-level round-trip + Rust register acceptance + cross-engine real-EoE MOVE / FIZZLE / MULTI via the spell-resolve path + **the FLIP probe `test_cross_engine_real_eoe_nesting_grounds_aa_activation_move_parity` driving the ACTUAL parsed AA via `apply_action` with both targets seated**, byte-equal on the (donor, recipient, tapped) triple) + `tests_rust/test_move_plus_one_counter_between_permanents_you_control.py` (12 Rust-engine pins — the 8 spell-path resolve pins + 4 NEW AA-activation pins: dual-target-moves-one / missing-2nd-target-fizzles / recipient-not-on-bf-raises / multi-counter-donor). ## Rust `Effect::ChangeControllerToCombatDamageSource` — Contested War Zone FLIP (covered_by_construction → PROBED); the two engine-deep walls (multi-subject predicate dispatch + deferred StackItem source-controller mirror) are CLOSED (2026-05-31)

**STATUS: RESOLVED — the live DEALS_COMBAT_DAMAGE trigger now drives byte-equal on both engines.** This entry documents the closure of the substrate-only landing's two deferred walls. The card is now PROBED (a per-card real-EoE live-trigger byte-equal probe registered in `PROBE_MODULES`).

**Where (the closure):** `rust/src/cards.rs` (`Predicate::ControlledByYou { slot }` matches arm — now slot-aware: `slot == "target"` reads `state.resolving_combat_damage_target_player_id` and compares to the source's controller), `rust/src/state.rs` (`TriggerPayload.combat_damage_source_controller_id: Option<u8>` + `combat_damage_amount: Option<i32>` fields + the three `new_trigger*` constructors default them `None`), `rust/src/state_ops_resolve.rs` (`push_triggered_ability` seats the two payload fields from the live `resolving_combat_damage_*` slots when the source-controller slot is live; BOTH trigger resolve entry points re-mirror them into the transient state slots, save→set→restore-bracketed exactly like the payload-target slots). The substrate (the `Effect::ChangeControllerToCombatDamageSource` variant + parse/to_pydict/valid-kinds arms + the `resolving_combat_damage_source_controller_id` state slot + the `dispatch_combat_damage_to_player` slot-seat + the `cross_engine.py` / `trajectory.py` bridge arms) landed in the prior substrate slice and is unchanged.

**What the two walls were, and how they closed:**

1. **Multi-subject predicate dispatch.** Contested War Zone's trigger predicate is `And(Subject(slot='source', IsCreature()), Controlled(by=YOU, subject='target'))` — "a creature deals combat damage to the Land's controller (you)". The `target` half references the DEFENDING PLAYER. Rust's `dispatch_event` carries a single `subject_id` (the damaging creature). **Closure:** the `ControlledByYou { slot }` matches arm is now slot-aware — when `slot == Some("target")` it reads the defending-player id off `state.resolving_combat_damage_target_player_id` (seated by `dispatch_combat_damage_to_player` for the duration of the observer walk, which is precisely when `matches` runs) and compares it to the source's controller. This is the byte-equal mirror of Python's `Controlled(by=YOU, subject="target")` evaluating `defending_player.id == source.controller_id`. NON-BREAKING: every existing `ControlledByYou` consumer passes `slot` `None` or `Some("controller")` and is byte-identical (the slot-blind game-object / `PLAYER_SUBJECT_OFFSET` paths are unchanged); only the `Some("target")` branch is new, and the only producer of that slot is the DEALS_COMBAT_DAMAGE bridge.

2. **Deferred StackItem source-controller mirror.** A combat-damage-triggered ability resolves LATER from the stack; the transient `resolving_combat_damage_source_controller_id` slot is restored to its `u8::MAX` sentinel after the synchronous observer walk in `dispatch_combat_damage_to_player`, so by trigger-resolve time the resolve arm would read the sentinel. **Closure:** `TriggerPayload` now carries `combat_damage_source_controller_id: Option<u8>` (+ the `combat_damage_amount: Option<i32>` sibling). `push_triggered_ability` snapshots the live state slots onto the just-pushed trigger's payload — guarded on the source-controller slot being live (`!= u8::MAX`), so every non-combat-damage trigger leaves the payload fields `None` (byte-identical to the pre-flip path). Both trigger resolve entry points (`resolve_top_of_stack` + `resolve_top_of_stack_pause`) re-mirror the payload's `Some(_)` values back into the transient state slots for the duration of the trigger's `apply_effect`, save→set→restore-bracketed exactly like the payload-target / mode-index siblings. This is the byte-equal mirror of Python's `StackItem.combat_damage_source_controller_id` / `combat_damage_amount` re-mirror at `actions.py:2680-2686`.

**Bonus — deferred `resolving_combat_damage_amount` production write unblocked.** The `combat_damage_amount` sibling on the payload re-mirrors the amount at resolve time too, so the production deferral the `resolving_combat_damage_amount` slot carried (an amount-reading effect that resolves later — Starwinder's `DrawCardsEqualToResolvingCombatDamage` — would have seen the reset `0` slot) is now closed alongside. The amount production write in `apply_damage_pass` / `dispatch_combat_damage_to_player` was already live; this slice closes the deferred-carry gap.

**Why this is OK / byte-equal:** verified across all three firing configurations cross-engine: (A) attacker(p1) deals combat damage to the Land's controller(p0) → both engines flip the Land's `controller` to p1 (permanent direct write; `controller_override` stays `None`); (B) attacker(p1) hits a non-Land-controller(p1) → predicate declines on both engines, no fire; (C) attacker(p0) == the Land's controller hits p0 → predicate matches but same-controller short-circuit no-op on both engines. The control change is a PERMANENT direct `controller` write (no `continuous_effects` layer-2 UEOT entry), byte-equal via the snapshot's `controller_id` key.

**Residual honest shortcut (loader-admit, deliberately NOT taken):** Contested War Zone is PROBED via the per-card real-EoE probe, NOT via the production-deck loader admit gate. The card's `{1},{T}` `PumpCreaturesYouControlUntilEOT` AA + the compound multi-subject DEALS_COMBAT_DAMAGE trigger keep it out of `_is_safe_trigger_dict` / the bench loader's simple admit gates; widening `_is_safe_trigger_dict` to recognize the compound `And(SubjectIsCreature, ControlledByYou{slot:"target"})` predicate shape was NOT done (it would be speculative — the AA blocks bench-admit regardless, and the PROBED metric is purely probe-based, not loader-admit-based). The card is therefore byte-equal-pinned at the live-trigger level but does not flow through the full-game bench corpus today. This is the only residual shortcut.

**Impact:** Contested War Zone covered_by_construction → PROBED. PROBED 454 → 455; covered_by_construction 1 → 0; BLOCKED-SG 20 unchanged. Pool byte-equal (Effect+bridge level) 455 (unchanged — the card was already counted byte-equal at the substrate level; the flip moves it to the stronger PROBED tier). 0 strength cost.

**Pinned by:** `tests/test_contested_war_zone_parity.py` (10 pins — parser SoT verify-first + reverse-serializer round-trip + covered-class pin + all-effects-covered flip pin + 4 Rust resolve-arm unit pins + the substrate-level real-EoE cross-engine probe + **the new `test_cross_engine_real_eoe_contested_war_zone_parity` live-trigger byte-equal flip probe**) + `tests_rust/test_change_controller_to_combat_damage_source.py` (6 Rust-engine pins). Registered in `scripts/measure_pool_parity.py` `PROBE_MODULES`. Scout doc at `docs/BLOCKED_TAIL_TRACTABILITY_SCOUT_2026-05-27.md` §Group-1 Contested War Zone.

## Carrier-AA substrate — Sliver Overlord FLIP: the FIRST Creature carrier + the first no-tap-mana cost shape; Sliver-target validation uses PRINTED (not layered/effective) subtypes (2026-05-31, `feature/sliver-overlord`)

**Location:**
- `rust/src/cards.rs` (new `Effect::GainControlOfTargetSliverPermanently` unit variant + `parse_effect` arm + `to_pydict` arm + valid-kinds list).
- `rust/src/state_ops_resolve.rs` (resolve arm — direct permanent `obj.controller = activator` write, reusing the Contested War Zone direct-controller-write mechanic; reads `current_resolve_payload_target_id` + `current_resolve_source_controller`).
- `rust/src/state_ops_legal.rs` (Sliver-creature target fan-out arm — BOTH bfs, ANY controller, printed-Creature + printed-`"Sliver"`-subtype).
- `rust/src/state_ops_actions.rs` (apply-time target validation arm — re-checks bf-presence on either player + printed-Creature + printed-`"Sliver"`-subtype).
- `src/mtg_bot/parity/cross_engine.py` (forward `_python_aa_to_safe_dict` arm + reverse `_ta_dict_to_python_effect` arm).
- `src/mtg_bot/parity/trajectory.py` (`_carrier_aa_phase_1_effect_classes` widen +1; `_aa_is_phase1_sub_shape_a` no-tap-mana cost-gate widen; new `_printing_is_bridge_simple_carrier_aa_creature` admit predicate + `_carrier_aa_creature_card_def` builder + `_any` dispatcher + OR-chain wiring; reverse-serializer leaf in `_python_spell_effect_to_dict`).

**Shortcut 1 (PRINTED vs effective/layered subtypes for the Sliver filter).** The Rust legal-fan-out, the apply-time validator, AND the resolve arm test the target's `"Sliver"` membership against the target's PRINTED subtypes (`registry.printings[..].subtypes`), NOT a layered/effective-subtypes view (CR 613 layer 4 type-changing effects). Python's `GainControlOfTargetSliverPermanently.legal_targets` / `.resolve` use `effective_subtypes(state, obj)` (the layered view). This mirrors the SAME printed-subtype basis the already-shipped `SearchLibraryForCard` `"sliver"` filter uses on both engines (`state_ops_resolve.rs:15231` checks `printing.subtypes`), so the two Sliver-Overlord AAs are consistent.

**Shortcut 2 (no-tap mana cost-gate widen — Python admit-predicate only).** `_aa_is_phase1_sub_shape_a` was widened to admit a pure generic-mana cost with `tap_self=False` (Sliver Overlord's two `{3}` AAs — the first non-tap Carrier-AA cost shape). This is a PURE Python admit-predicate change: the Rust legal-emit gate already conditions its tap-gate on `ability.cost.tap_self` (`state_ops_legal.rs:3467`), and the AA cost serializer omits the `tap_self` key when False — ZERO new Rust cost-shape machinery. The widen REQUIRES a non-empty generic-mana cost (a degenerate free/zero-cost no-tap AA declines), and the all-or-nothing per-AA + Effect-class teeth keep every OTHER no-tap-mana-only carrier in the pool (Equipment-equip / pump / draw AAs whose Effect classes are NOT in the admit set) DECLINED — only Sliver Overlord, whose BOTH AAs carry admitted Effect classes, clears the combined gate (verified by a full-pool admit-set walk: `_printing_is_bridge_simple_carrier_aa_any` admits exactly 21 cards, Sliver Overlord the sole Creature).

**Why it's OK:**
- **Printed-subtype basis is byte-equal in the live EoE pool.** No EoE card grants or removes the `Sliver` subtype via a layer-4 type-changing continuous effect (the only Sliver-subtype-touching cards are Sliver Overlord's own two AAs, which CONSUME the subtype, not grant it). So `effective_subtypes(state, obj) ∩ {Sliver}` == `printed_subtypes(obj) ∩ {Sliver}` for every battlefield permanent today — the two bases agree, and the cross-engine probe (p1's printed Sliver → p0 gains control) is byte-equal.
- **The control change is a PERMANENT direct `controller` write** (the printed AA "lasts indefinitely"), reusing the EXACT direct-write substrate Contested War Zone's `ChangeControllerToCombatDamageSource` proved byte-equal (no `continuous_effects` layer-2 UEOT entry, `controller_override` stays `None` on both engines). The only new dimension vs that effect is the TARGET (a Sliver on either bf) vs source-self — covered by the new fan-out + validator + the target-reading resolve arm.
- **The no-tap cost widen is admit-set-surgical.** Confirmed by a verify-first full-pool scan: the widen pulls in ZERO spurious cards under the all-or-nothing Effect-class contract.

**Failure mode:**
- A future card (no live EoE today) that grants the `Sliver` subtype to a non-Sliver creature via a layer-4 continuous effect, then is targeted by Sliver Overlord's AA[1]: Python's `effective_subtypes`-based `legal_targets`/resolve would admit it (the grant makes it a Sliver); Rust's printed-subtype basis would REJECT it (the printing is not printed-Sliver). Divergence bounded to that hypothetical layered-grant interaction — the same bounded gap the shipped `SearchLibraryForCard` `"sliver"` filter already carries.
- A future no-tap-mana Carrier-AA carrier whose BOTH (all) AAs carry admitted Effect classes would now auto-admit under the widen — intended (the widen is the general no-tap cost lane), but any such future carrier must land its own per-card real-EoE probe to claim PROBED.

**Fix scope:** Layer-4 effective-subtypes parity for the Sliver filter is Phase-N — it requires the Rust continuous-effect/layered-subtypes substrate (the same `effective_subtypes` dispatch the Ghost Vacuum recall-rider entry above also needs). Shared with any future subtype-target effect. ~1 substrate cycle once the layered-subtypes overlay lands; until then the printed-subtype basis is byte-equal in the live pool.

**Impact estimate:** +1 card (Sliver Overlord) PROBED tier (PROBED 455 → 456); BLOCKED-SG 20 → 19 (Carrier-activated-abilities subsystem row 5 → 4). First Carrier-AA Creature carrier admit + first no-tap-mana cost lane (both amortize to future cards). The direct-controller-write substrate amortizes to any future "gain control of target permanent" (permanent, no-UEOT) card. 0 strength cost — the substrate is byte-equal cross-engine in the live pool; the one bounded printed-vs-layered-subtype divergence has no live EoE consumer.

## Haunted Screen — HONEST-STOP (stays BLOCKED): three independent substrate walls, two un-byte-equal-able (2026-05-31)

**Location:** `src/mtg_bot/parity/trajectory.py` `_aa_is_phase1_sub_shape_a` (`pay_life` decline arm ~`:10120`; `activate_only_once` decline arm ~`:10194`; Effect-class gate `_carrier_aa_effect_class_admitted` ~`:10224`) + `rust/src/cards.rs` (`ActivationCost` struct `:11437` has no `pay_life`; `ActivatedAbility` defers `activate_only_once` `:11431`/`:11871`; no `Effect::BecomeType` variant — parser rejects the `"become_type"` kind) + `rust/src/state_ops_combat.rs:319` (`is_creature_now` reads only the printing's `card_types`) + `rust/src/state_ops_snapshot.rs` (`object_to_pydict` does NOT surface `subtypes`/`card_types`/`is_creature`).

**What the shortcut is:** Haunted Screen (`{3}` Artifact, DSK) carries THREE AAs and is held in the BLOCKED — subsystem-gated / Effect-uncovered tier. A flip is gated by the Carrier-AA multi-AA all-or-nothing admit contract (every AA must pass `_aa_is_phase1_sub_shape_a`). Verify-first dump of the real parsed printing found:
- **AA[0]** `{T}: Add {W} or {B}.` (`AddNManaOfChosenColor`, `is_mana_ability=True`) — **ALREADY ADMITS**.
- **AA[1]** `{T}, Pay 1 life: Add {G}, {U}, or {R}.` — **WALL #1: `pay_life` AA-cost.** Declined by the per-AA cost gate (`if cost.pay_life: return False`). Rust `ActivationCost` has NO `pay_life` field, `parse_activation_cost` accepts only `mana`/`tap_self`/`sacrifice_self`/`sacrifice_a_desert`, and the Rust AA legal-emit + cost-pay carry no life-payment leg (`pay_life_cost` exists at `state_ops_life.rs:108` but is unwired to AA activation).
- **AA[2]** `{7}: Put seven +1/+1 counters on this artifact. It becomes a 0/0 Spirit creature in addition to its other types. Activate only once.` = `Sequence(PutPlusOneCounterOnSelf(7), BecomeType(creature, Spirit, base_pt=(0,0)))`, `activate_only_once=True` — **WALL #2: permanent `BecomeType` type-layer** (the genuinely-uncovered Effect) AND **WALL #3: `activate_only_once` rider**.

This slice does NOT flip the card, does NOT widen any shared admit predicate, and ships ZERO Rust changes — an honest-stop with a precise remaining-work characterization (per the campaign honest-stop policy).

**Why it's OK / why no widen:**
- **WALL #2 is the policy's named "sprawling type-layer machinery that can't byte-equal."** Rust has NO permanent per-object type-change substrate. `is_creature_now` reads only the printing's `card_types`; there is no added-types/added-subtypes/base-PT override registry. The one "becomes a creature" path (`Effect::BecomeLandCreatureUEOT` → `UeotModifier::BecomesLandCreature`) is UEOT-only (auto-expires at cleanup). Haunted Screen's `BecomeType` is **permanent** (`expires_at=None`, persists until the artifact leaves play) — no Rust analogue. AND `battlefield_snapshot` does not surface `subtypes`/`card_types`/`is_creature`, so the "became a Spirit creature" change is not even byte-equal-observable on the current snapshot surface.
- **The one tractable amortizing piece can't land in isolation.** Adding `PutPlusOneCounterOnSelf` to the Effect-class admit set (its `Effect::PutPlusOneCounterOnSelf` variant + parse + to_pydict + resolve + reverse bridge arm ALL already live on main; observable byte-equal via the `counters` snapshot field) cannot flip Haunted Screen alone (AA[1]'s `pay_life` + AA[2]'s `BecomeType`/`activate_only_once` still bite). AND it would silently change the loader-admit *path* of an already-PROBED card: **Intrepid Tenderfoot** (single-type Creature, fixed 2/2, single `{3}` no-tap `PutPlusOneCounterOnSelf` AA, no other riders) would newly pass `_printing_is_bridge_simple_carrier_aa_creature`. (Rust Harvester stays declined — its Sequence's second leaf `DealDamageEqualToSourcePowerAnyTarget` is not admitted.) Perturbing a covered card's admit path without a probe verifying the new path is byte-equal is the silent auto-grow the discipline forbids, so the widen is deferred to a slice that flips Intrepid Tenderfoot in lockstep with its own probe.

**Failure mode:** None new — the card stays honestly BLOCKED; no shared predicate loosened, no spurious admit, no Rust change. The diagnosis is regression-pinned, so a future accidental widen that admits Haunted Screen (or that flips Intrepid Tenderfoot's path) without closing the three walls + adding probes would fail the pins.

**Fix scope estimate:** Full flip = 3 substrate cycles. (1) **`pay_life` AA cost** (~1 Rust cycle): new `ActivationCost.pay_life: i32` + parse + legal-emit life-availability gate + cost-pay life-deduction + cross-engine AA-cost serializer/deserializer. (2) **permanent `BecomeType` type-layer** (~1 large Rust cycle, the gating one): new permanent per-object `added_types`/`added_subtypes`/`base_pt_override` fields + every `is_creature_now`/subtype-reader/effective-P/T reader consulting them + leave-play reset + new snapshot surface for byte-equal observability + new `Effect::BecomeType` variant (parse/to_pydict/resolve/bridge arms). (3) **`activate_only_once`** (~0.5 Rust cycle): new `ActivatedAbility.activate_only_once: bool` + per-object once-only latch + legal-emit gate + bridge round-trip. Plus the `PutPlusOneCounterOnSelf` admit widen (Python-only, but must flip Intrepid Tenderfoot + ship its probe in lockstep).

**Impact estimate:** 0 cards flipped (PROBED 456, BLOCKED-SG 19 — unchanged). The substrate that WOULD amortize: `BecomeType` (permanent type-change) → any future "this permanent becomes a creature/changes type permanently" card once the Rust type-layer overlay lands; `pay_life` AA cost → any future mana-ability / AA paying life; `activate_only_once` → any future once-only AA. 0 strength cost (no behavior change this slice).

**Pinned by:** `tests/test_haunted_screen_blocked.py` (8 pins — parser SoT verify-first of all 3 AA shapes + AA[0] admits + AA[1] declines-purely-on-`pay_life` (isolated-variable) + AA[2] declines on Effect-class + `activate_only_once` + `BecomeType` not-in-admit-set + the loader-stays-BLOCKED invariant + the Rust-rejects-`become_type` substrate-gap pin). Deliberately NOT a `*_parity.py` credit-eligible probe and NOT registered in `scripts/measure_pool_parity.py` `PROBE_MODULES` (mirrors the `atomic_microsizer` honest-stop attribution-pin precedent) — ZERO free PROBED flips.

- **Counter-doubling (Loading Zone, NEW 2026-06-01):** `counter_placement_count_multiplier` + `doubled_plus_one_counter_delta` helpers (~`:398`) consulted at EVERY +1/+1-counter-placement arm (`Effect::AddCounters`, `PutPlusOneCounterOnSelf`, `PutPlusOneCounterOnCreatureYouControl`, `PutPlusOneCounterOnTargetCreature`, `PutPlusOneCounterOnOpponentsCreature`, `PutPlusOneCounterOnEachCreatureYouControl`, `...EqualToSourcePower`, `PutPlusOneCounterOnEachOfUpToNTargetCreatures`, `PutPlusOneCountersOnSelfPerOtherCreatureOrArtifact`, `MoveSelfCountersToTargetCreatureYouControl`, `PutChargeCountersOnSelf`, `BiosynthicBurstEffect`, the `ReturnUpToNSmallCreaturesFromGraveyardWithCounters` reanimation-with-counter rider, and `PutPlusOneCountersAndGrantKeywordsUEOTOnTargetCreatureYouControl` — every `obj.counters.saturating_add(positive_delta)` site). Negative deltas (-1/-1, Python's `add_minus_one_counters` which does NOT double) and out-of-scope recipients (non-creature/non-Spacecraft) pass through unchanged.
- **Extra-trigger (Starfield Vocalist, NEW 2026-06-01):** `entered_trigger_instance_multiplier` (~`:430`) folded into the `dispatch_event` push loop — for `Event::Enters` firings ONLY, each per-source firing is pushed N times (base 1 + sum of `add_instances` deltas keyed on the firing's controller).

**What the substrate is:** The Phase-5 ReplacementEffect-static substrate (Rust `StaticReplacement` struct + `static_replacements` field + parse + closed-vocab whitelist; bridge `CardDef.static_replacements` field + forward emit + reverse arm) ships in full and round-trips byte-equal for ALL THREE event shapes — AND all three now have live Rust resolve consumers.

**Why the two new arms are byte-equal:**
- **Loading Zone — recipient-controller keyed + creature-or-Spacecraft scope.** `counter_placement_count_multiplier` mirrors Python's `_counter_doubling_factor` (`game.py:1992`) EXACTLY: short-circuits to 1 for non-creature/non-Spacecraft recipients, keys the doubler on the RECIPIENT's controller (NOT the caster — so `PutPlusOneCounterOnOpponentsCreature` doubles iff the OPPONENT has a Loading Zone, matching counters.py:815), folds matching factors multiplicatively (two Loading Zones → ×4). Probe: place-1 → BOTH engines land 2; neg-control / p1-owned-LZ-on-p0-creature → BOTH land 1.
- **Starfield Vocalist — ENTERS-only mirror of `etb_trigger_multiplier`.** Python applies the instance multiplier ONLY for `Event.ENTERS` firings (`actions.py:3475`: `etb_trigger_multiplier(...) if event is Event.ENTERS else 1`) even though the printed text covers all triggered abilities; the Rust arm is gated identically (the `Event::Enters` arm in `dispatch_event` is the only caller). Both engines share the same deliberate non-ENTERS-trigger gap, so the firing set is byte-equal. Probe: an ENTERS-trigger creature with Starfield Vocalist → BOTH engines push 2 instances; two Vocalists → 3; neg-control / p1-owned-Vocalist → 1.
- **Reanimation-with-counter ordering.** The `ReturnUpToNSmallCreaturesFromGraveyardWithCounters` arm moves the counter application to AFTER the object lands on the battlefield (mirroring Python's `put_into_battlefield(...)` THEN `add_plus_one_counters(...)` order at `graveyard.py:279-283`) so the doubler sees the now-on-bf recipient.

**Failure mode (residual):** The warp+static bench-loader admit widen is still honest-stopped, so no bench trajectory drives these cards through a full game — but the per-card resolve arms are now byte-equal, so a future admit widen would NOT surface a counter/trigger-count divergence. The only remaining non-ENTERS-trigger gap (Starfield Vocalist's text vs the `etb_trigger_multiplier` ENTERS-only model) is SHARED by both engines (no cross-engine divergence).

**Fix scope estimate (residual only):**
- **Warp+static bench-loader admit widen (all three):** ~1 cycle. A `_printing_is_bridge_replacement_static_*` admit predicate folded into `_filter_deck_to_bridge_supported` (the per-card `_*_card_def` builders exist but aren't wired into the general admit gate). Each card's warp-cast path verified byte-equal in lockstep.
- **Non-ENTERS Starfield Vocalist triggers (shared gap, NOT a divergence):** the printed text covers ALL triggered abilities; both engines model only ENTERS (the `etb_trigger_multiplier` shape). Closing it means a per-controller instance multiplier at every `dispatch_event` event family on both sides — a coordinated cross-engine widen, deferred because it's a SHARED simplification, not a parity gap.

**Impact estimate:** Same +3 cards PROBED; this slice HARDENS the Rust-side byte-equality (token-doubling-only → all-three-wired), it does not change the tier (all three were already PROBED via the Python-resolve idiom). The substrate amortizes: the battlefield-walk-and-fold helper pattern + the additive `dispatch_event` instance-multiplier are reusable for any future ReplacementEffect-static card (Anointed-Procession token-multiply, Doubling-Season counter-doubling, Strionic-Resonator extra-trigger). 0 strength cost.

## Nexus of Fate — FLIPPED BLOCKED → PROBED: the extra-turn-clause Effect substrate LANDED (extra turns are QUEUED byte-equal but NOT taken in search — accepted parity-vs-search divergence) — 2026-05-31, `feature/nexus-of-fate`

**The card.** Nexus of Fate `{5}{U}{U}` Instant (Special Guests reprint in the EoE pool): "Take an extra turn after this one. If Nexus of Fate would be put into a graveyard from anywhere, instead shuffle it into its owner's library."

**Both gates closed.** Nexus had TWO independent gates and both are now closed:

* **Clause 2 — the shuffle-self `would_go_to_graveyard → library` redirect static.** Already CLOSED by the Green Sun's Zenith flip (the entry directly above, `feature/gsz-flip`): the Rust `move_source_post_resolve` hook reroutes a resolving spell whose printing carries that `StaticReplacement` to its owner's library + shuffles, mirroring Python's `_send_to_graveyard_or_library`. Nexus carries the IDENTICAL static (verified — `_printing_has_unbridgeable_replacement_static(Nexus) is False`), so no further redirect work was needed in this lane. (The GSZ-vs-Nexus shuffle-vs-position concern is a non-issue: GSZ's "fetch a creature" is a SEPARATE library search; the SPELL-SELF redirect on resolve — the only static both cards share — is the same shuffle-this-card-into-the-owner's-library reroute for both, with no position semantics.)

* **Clause 1 — the `TakeExtraTurnAfterThisOne` spell_effect.** This lane lands the genuinely-missing piece. The Python effect `effects/generic/stack_control.py:231` `TakeExtraTurnAfterThisOne` (field-free frozen dataclass: `state.extra_turn_queue.append(controller_id)`) had NO Rust mirror. This lane adds the Rust `Effect::TakeExtraTurnAfterThisOne` unit variant (parse arm `take_extra_turn_after_this_one` + `to_pydict` arm + resolve arm) + a NEW `GameState.extra_turn_queue: Vec<u8>` field (mirrors Python's `list[int]` of controller ids; default-empty at every construction site; cloned forward; surfaced via the `extra_turn_queue()` getter as `bytes`/`list[int]`) + the `take_extra_turn_after_this_one` dict→Python bridge arm (`cross_engine.py`) + the reverse-serializer leaf (`trajectory._python_spell_effect_to_dict`). The class is now covered+bridged (`covered_python_class_set()` 1:1 identity), so Nexus ADMITS at the spell-card-bridge gate and flips to PROBED.

**THE DELIBERATE SHORTCUT (parity-not-search).** Extra turns were historically "declined" because they explode the AI SEARCH tree. That is SEPARATE from cross-engine PARITY. The substrate landed here is **minimal byte-equal extra-turn-QUEUE modeling only**: resolving Nexus appends exactly one controller id to `state.extra_turn_queue` on BOTH engines, byte-equal. **The Rust turn-advance does NOT pop this queue — the AI search does not actually take the queued extra turn.** Python's `simulate._advance_to_next_active_player` DOES consume the queue (the Python sim loop takes extra turns), but the Rust engine's turn advancement deliberately ignores it.

* **Location.** Rust: `state_ops_resolve.rs` `Effect::TakeExtraTurnAfterThisOne` arm (appends to the queue, no pop); `state.rs` `extra_turn_queue` field + `extra_turn_queue()` getter (no consumer). Python: `effects/generic/stack_control.py:243` (append) + `simulate.py:411-418` (consume — Python-only).
* **What the shortcut is.** The queue is QUEUED identically on both engines but only CONSUMED on the Python sim side; the Rust engine never grants the extra turn during its own turn rotation.
* **Why it's OK (and when not).** The cross-engine PARITY metric only requires the post-resolve QUEUE STATE to be byte-equal, which it is (the probe asserts `py.extra_turn_queue == list(rs.extra_turn_queue()) == [0]`). It is NOT OK if a future lane wires the Rust engine to actually take queued extra turns in self-play search — that would re-introduce the search-tree explosion the project deliberately avoids, AND the two engines' turn-rotation would then need to be re-verified byte-equal through the extra turn (currently un-exercised). The Python sim consumes the queue today, but production self-play caps `max_turns`, so an extra turn merely shifts which player acts next within the cap.
* **Failure mode.** A full game that actually reaches the extra-turn consumption on Python but not on Rust would diverge on `active_player` / turn rotation. The probe does NOT advance the turn, so this path is un-exercised by the parity probe (byte-equal queue STATE only). No production self-play parity check drives Nexus through a turn boundary today.
* **Fix scope (deferred — NOT taken here per the honest-stop policy).** Wiring the Rust turn-advance to pop the queue + byte-equal extra-turn rotation is a broad turn-pipeline change with AI-search-explosion implications; explicitly out of scope. The substrate is built so a future lane CAN light it up if the search-side decision changes.
* **Impact estimate.** Zero strength cost today (extra turns are not taken in search on either the Rust engine or production self-play within the turn cap). Parity-probe-positive: Nexus flips BLOCKED → PROBED.

**Field-view / fingerprint exclusion.** `extra_turn_queue` is NOT in `parity_smoke.FIELD_DIFF_FIELDS` and NOT in the fingerprint (transient turn-scoped scheduling state — same exclusion as `spell_warped_this_turn` / `created_tokens_this_turn`). The probe reads it via the dedicated `extra_turn_queue()` getter (Rust) / `state.extra_turn_queue` (Python), alongside the FULL `compare_fields == []` field-view byte-equality for the clause-2 library-redirect observable (which IS in the field view via the library/graveyard zones).

**Pinned by:** `tests/test_nexus_of_fate_parity.py` — `test_real_nexus_spell_effect_and_redirect_static` (parser SoT verify-first), `test_take_extra_turn_effect_class_covered` (covered-set), `test_take_extra_turn_serializer_round_trip` (field-free unit-variant bridge round-trip), `test_nexus_admits_at_bridge_gate_after_extra_turn_substrate` (the FLIP pin), `test_rust_nexus_queues_extra_turn_for_controller` + `test_rust_nexus_shuffles_self_into_library` + `test_rust_instant_without_extra_turn_effect_does_not_queue` (Rust resolve-arm pins + control), and **`test_cross_engine_real_eoe_nexus_of_fate_extra_turn_and_shuffle_parity`** (the GENUINE real-printing whole-field-view byte-equal probe + extra-turn-queue byte-equality — the PROBED-tier credit). REGISTERED in `PROBE_MODULES`.

## Robe of Stars phasing substrate (CR 702.26 partially modeled) — 2026-05-31, `feature/robe-of-stars`

**Status: PROBED flip landed.** Robe of Stars (`{1}{W}` Artifact —
Equipment, "Astral Projection — `{1}{W}`: Equipped creature phases
out") was `blocked_subsystem_gated` on exactly one uncovered Effect
class, `PhaseOutEquippedCreature` (the `EquipToTargetCreatureYouControl`
equip ability was already covered). This lane landed the genuinely-new
Rust Effect + a minimal phasing-status substrate and flipped the card
to PROBED.

**Where.**
- Rust `GameObject.phased_out: bool` field (`rust/src/state.rs`;
  mirrors Python `game.py:613`) — defaulted `false` at all 15
  construction sites; SURFACED in the snapshot dict
  (`rust/src/state_ops_snapshot.rs::object_to_pydict`, additive key —
  unlike the snapshot-elided `regeneration_shield`) so the phase-OUT
  state change is byte-equal-observable.
- Rust `Effect::PhaseOutEquippedCreature` unit variant — enum decl +
  parse arm + to_pydict arm + valid-kinds string (`rust/src/cards.rs`);
  resolve arm (`rust/src/state_ops_resolve.rs::apply_effect`, beside
  `RegenerateTargetCreature`) reading the resolving Equipment source's
  `attached_to`, stamping `phased_out = true` on the host, and clearing
  the host from `state.attackers` / `state.blockers`.
- Cross-engine reverse bridge arm `phase_out_equipped_creature`
  (`src/mtg_bot/parity/cross_engine.py::_ta_dict_to_python_effect`).
- Probe `tests/test_robe_of_stars_parity.py` (registered in
  `scripts/measure_pool_parity.py` PROBE_MODULES); Rust unit pins
  `tests_rust/test_phase_out_equipped_creature.py`; snapshot key pin
  `tests_rust/test_snapshot.py::EXPECTED_KEYS`.

**What the probe asserts (the byte-equal-observable surface).** The
phase-OUT state change ONLY: the equipped host's `phased_out` flips
`true` byte-equal on both engines, the Robe itself + unrelated
creatures stay `phased_out=false` byte-equal, and an unequipped Robe's
AA is a byte-equal silent no-op. The Rust side drives the FULL real
`{1}{W}` AA-activation (`apply_action` activate_ability → mana pay →
stack push → resolve); the Python side drives the real-parsed Effect's
`.resolve(state, controller_id, ())` with `resolving_source` set (the
established Ancient-Tomb-substrate cross-engine drive idiom — Python's
auto-tap cost machinery holds coin objects, not symbols, so driving it
would exercise the cost path, not the phasing effect; the resolve
boundary is where byte-equality is asserted).

**The deliberate shortcut (CR 702.26 NOT fully modeled — same
simplification both engines).**
- **Phase-IN (CR 702.26e — phased-out permanents phase in during their
  controller's untap step).** Python clears `phased_out` at untap
  (`turn.py:64-65`). The Rust untap-step clear is NOT wired (no probe
  drives a full turn rollover). The per-card probe exercises only the
  phase-OUT half.
- **Treat-as-nonexistent (CR 702.26c — a phased-out permanent is
  treated as though it does not exist for every game action).** NEITHER
  engine fully models this. Python applies the bit ONLY to combat-damage
  resolution (`combat.py:382`) + the combat-state clear at phase-out;
  triggers, anthems, SBA, and targeting still see phased objects. Rust
  surfaces the bit + clears the host's combat participation but no game
  action consumes `phased_out` beyond that.

**Why it's OK (for the PROBE).** The PROBED tier is a controlled-state
byte-equality probe, not a full-game-trajectory guarantee. The probe's
observable (host `phased_out` flips, snapshot byte-equal) is exactly
modeled byte-equal on both engines. The unmodeled phasing semantics are
NOT exercised by the probe and are simplified IDENTICALLY on both
engines, so they cannot introduce a cross-engine divergence on the
phase-OUT surface.

**Failure mode.** A full-game trajectory that (a) phases a creature out
and then runs the phased creature's controller's untap step (Rust would
NOT phase it back in — `phased_out` stays stuck `true`), or (b) relies
on treat-as-nonexistent for triggers/SBA/targeting/anthems while the
creature is phased. These are out of the probe's scope; the bench
trajectory tier does not admit Robe (Equipment-AA carrier not in the
loader-admit set), so no full-game path exercises the unmodeled half
today.

**Fix scope (remaining phasing-mechanic work, if a future card needs
it).** Full CR 702.26: (1) Rust untap-step phase-IN clear (~0.5 cycle —
mirror Python's `turn.py:64-65` in the Rust untap step + a turn-rollover
probe); (2) treat-as-nonexistent across the action / SBA / combat /
targeting / static-ability pipeline (multi-cycle, broad blast radius —
every legal-action enumeration, SBA pass, trigger dispatch, and
continuous-effect application would need a `phased_out` exclusion
filter on BOTH engines, plus Python's own model widened past the
combat-damage-only filter). The phase-OUT substrate landed here is the
reusable foundation; phase-IN is a cheap follow-on, treat-as-nonexistent
is the genuine mechanic build.

**Impact estimate.** PROBED 461 → 462 (97.3%); BLOCKED-SG 14 → 13;
covered_by_construction unchanged (0). One new Rust Effect + one new
GameObject bool field (snapshot-surfaced). 0 strength cost on the
closed surface — the new field defaults `false` everywhere (all
pre-substrate snapshot / hash baselines byte-identical) and no game
action consumes it beyond the combat-state clear at phase-out.

**Other BLOCKED/future cards needing phasing.** NONE in the current EoE
pool — Robe of Stars is the sole phasing card. A future "phases out" or
"phase out target permanent" card would reuse this `phased_out` field +
snapshot surface but would need the treat-as-nonexistent build if its
probe observes any action-exclusion semantics.

**Pinned by:** `tests/test_robe_of_stars_parity.py`
(`test_cross_engine_real_eoe_robe_of_stars_parity` — the GENUINE
real-printing byte-equal PROBED credit, plus parser-SoT / coverage /
bridge-round-trip / Rust-register / snapshot-default pins) +
`tests_rust/test_phase_out_equipped_creature.py` (Rust parse / snapshot
/ resolve unit pins). The existing `tests/test_robe_of_stars.py`
(Python-side unit tests) is unchanged.

## Pinnacle Starcage — token mint by registry-id (not name) + AA delivered via ETB-trigger in the probe (2026-05-31)

**Location.** `rust/src/cards.rs` (the new `Effect::ExileAllMatching
UntilSourceLeaves` / `MoveEachExiledWithSourceToOwnersGraveyard` /
`CreateNTokensFromLastExileRecall { token_printing_id }` /
`SacrificeSelf` variants), `rust/src/state_ops_resolve.rs` (their
resolve arms), `rust/src/state.rs` (the transient
`last_exile_recall_count` field), `src/mtg_bot/parity/cross_engine.py`
(the four reverse bridge arms), `tests/test_pinnacle_starcage_parity.py`
(the probe).

**What the shortcut is — TWO documented divergences.**

1. **Token mint by `token_printing_id` (Rust) vs `token_name` (Python).**
   Python's `CreateNTokensFromLastExileRecall(token_name="Robot")`
   mints via the static `TOKEN_PRINTINGS["Robot"]` table; the Rust
   `Effect::CreateNTokensFromLastExileRecall { token_printing_id }`
   carries a registry pid instead (the project-wide Rust token-minting
   convention — every Rust token variant carries a pid, not a name).
   The bridge resolves the name → a registered token printing id via
   the existing `register_token_printing` / `_seat_token_printings`
   path. This is NOT a behavioral divergence (both engines mint the
   same 2/2 Robot under the same controller) — it's a wire-shape
   asymmetry the bridge reconciles, identical to the precedent set by
   `create_token` / `create_token_and_attach_self`.

2. **The AA Sequence is delivered via an ETB-trigger vehicle in the
   cross-engine probe, NOT the full `{6}{W}{W}` activation cost path.**
   The probe (`test_cross_engine_real_eoe_pinnacle_starcage_aa_recall_
   tokens_sac_parity`) stages the genuine parsed AA Sequence onto the
   stack with the source set (Python: `push_triggered_ability`; Rust: a
   synthetic carrier whose ETB carries the Sequence dict), rather than
   paying `{6}{W}{W}` and tapping. The byte-equality claim is over the
   THREE Effect RESOLVES (recall-to-graveyard + token-mint + sac), not
   over the cost machinery. `resolving_source` is set by the stack
   resolver on both engines, so `exiled_with_source` stamping +
   `SacrificeSelf` source-lookup behave identically to a real
   activation. The production-deck loader path (which would pay the
   real cost) is NOT exercised by this probe — Pinnacle Starcage stays
   DECLINED at the bridge admit gate (the AA cost-gate +
   ETB-trigger-admit widens are a separate, broader surface not needed
   for the PROBED credit).

**Why it's OK.** (1) The token-id-vs-name asymmetry is purely a wire
encoding the bridge round-trips losslessly (round-trip pin
`test_pinnacle_starcage_bridge_reverse_arms_rehydrate`). (2) The
ETB-vehicle delivery exercises the exact same resolve arms a real
activation would; the cost path is orthogonal to the 3-effect
byte-equality being proven (same precedent as the Seam Rip / Grove
until-leaves probes, which also bypass cast/activation cost via
inject-and-fire). The exile-with-source state machinery (the
`exiled_with_source` field + `return_paired_exiles_for` recall hook)
was REUSED unchanged — no new linked-exile state machine was needed.

**Failure mode.** If a future card mints a DIFFERENT token from a
last-exile-recall whose pid the bridge doesn't seat, the reverse arm
falls back to the canonical `"Robot"` name (the only EoE consumer
today). A non-Robot consumer would need the bridge's
`_seat_token_printings` pass extended (cheap). The ETB-vehicle probe
does NOT pin the `{6}{W}{W}` activation legality / cost-payment — a
real-game divergence in Pinnacle Starcage's activation (mana payment,
sorcery-speed timing, tap) would not be caught by this probe.

**Fix scope estimate.** Closing the production-loader admit (so a real
`{6}{W}{W}` activation drives the AA) is the AA cost-gate widen
(`_aa_is_phase1_sub_shape_a` admitting a generic+colored mana cost) +
the ETB-trigger admit path + token-printing seating — a moderate
multi-arm surface, NOT needed for the byte-equal-Effect PROBED credit.

**Impact estimate.** PROBED 462 → 463 (97.5%); BLOCKED-SG 13 → 12.
Three new Rust Effect variants + one effect-body leaf + one transient
`i32` GameState scratch field (NOT in the fingerprint — transient like
`current_resolve_source_controller` / `next_etb_timestamp`). 0 strength
cost on the closed surface; the scratch field defaults 0 everywhere
(all pre-substrate snapshot / hash baselines byte-identical) and is
read only within a single Sequence resolve.

**Pinned by:** `tests/test_pinnacle_starcage_parity.py` (parser-SoT /
bridge-reverse-arm / Rust-register / two GENUINE real-printing
byte-equal probes — ETB mass-exile + AA recall/token/sac) +
`tests_rust/test_resolve.py` (the `test_pinnacle_*` Rust resolve-arm
unit pins).

## Secluded Starforge — FLIPPED BLOCKED-SG → PROBED + Rust tap-X cost WIRED: AA2 tap-X-artifacts → +X/+0 X-channel substrate LANDED on both engines + parser claim-ordering fix (2026-05-31, `feature/secluded-starforge-flip`); Rust cost-payment wired (2026-06-01, `feature/secluded-tapx-rust` — see Scope-simplification-CLOSED below)

**STATUS: FLIPPED to PROBED.** The variable-tap-cost X-channel substrate
the map below described has LANDED on both engines, and the parser now
emits the full faithful 3-AA printing. Secluded Starforge is PROBED
(POOL_PARITY 466→467, BLOCKED-SG 9→8). The body below is preserved as
the design record; the **FLIP-LANDED** note at the end records what
actually shipped and the one scope simplification taken.

**Where (the fix)**: parser claim path
`src/mtg_bot/cards/parser/land_builder.py:_try_build_colorless_utility_land`
now routes ALL lines of a multi-line tap-for-{C} land through
`_parse_activated_ability_line` (NO trailing-AA drop); the single-line
case keeps the historical `make_colorless_land`. Static mirror
`src/mtg_bot/cards/lands.py` carries the full 3-AA `make_utility_land`
(byte-identical to the parser).

**Raw oracle (real EoE printing — `data/edge_of_eternities.json`)**,
`type_line = "Land"`, `mana_cost = ""`:

  1. `{T}: Add {C}.`
  2. `{2}, {T}, Tap X untapped artifacts you control: Target creature
     gets +X/+0 until end of turn. Activate only as a sorcery.`
  3. `{5}, {T}: Create a 2/2 colorless Robot artifact creature token.`

**VERIFY-FIRST finding (the load-bearing correction to the prior
"the parser drops its activated abilities — parsed printing comes out
EMPTY" framing).** The parser does NOT lack recognizers for AAs 1 and
3 — both ALREADY parse cleanly through the existing grammar:

  * `_parse_activated_ability_line("{T}: Add {C}.")` →
    `ActivatedAbility(AddManaToPool(produces=(("C",1),)),
    is_mana_ability=True)` (and the colorless `{T}: Add {C}` mana line
    is also directly buildable, as Plaza of Heroes does).
  * `_parse_activated_ability_line("{5}, {T}: Create a 2/2 colorless
    Robot artifact creature token.")` → `ActivatedAbility(cost={5}+tap,
    CreateToken(token_printing=Robot, count=1))` — the `{5}, {T}` cost
    classifies (mana + tap atoms) and the Robot-token effect body is
    already recognized by `_parse_effect` (effects.py Robot-token arm).

The reason the live printing is empty is purely the *whole-card*
recognizer ordering: `_try_build_colorless_utility_land` claims any
plain `Land` whose first line is `{T}: Add {C}.` and emits a bare
`make_colorless_land` — it does NOT route the remaining lines through
the AA grammar. AAs 1+3 are tractable today; **AA2 is the sole real
blocker.** Both Rust effect kinds needed for 1+3 are in the valid-kinds
set (`add_mana_to_pool`, `create_token`).

**What AA2 genuinely needs (the new substrate — multi-file, BOTH
engines).** AA2's `+X/+0` where X = the number of untapped artifacts
the controller *chooses to tap as part of the cost* is a variable
cost-payment-determined X. The existing X-channel
(`state.resolving_x_value`, consumed by `PumpSelfXPowerUEOT`
pump.py:912 and `PutChargeCountersOnSelf(amount_from_x=True)`
counters.py:572) is set ONLY from `{X}` **mana** `x_pips`
(`actions.py:1957-1970` `_choose_and_apply_x`). AA2's X comes from a
non-mana cost atom, which has no machinery. Concretely the closure
needs:

  1. **New cost atom / `ActivationCost` field** — e.g.
     `tap_x_untapped_artifacts_you_control: bool` (Python
     `effects/base.py:329` `ActivationCost`; Rust mirror in
     `rust/src/cards.rs` `ActivationCost`). Parser recognizer in
     `activated.py` (`_classify_cost_piece` / `_build_cost_from_pieces`)
     for the literal `Tap X untapped artifacts you control`.
  2. **Legal-actions enumeration of the chosen X** — a NEW
     cost-payment decision shape: at activation, enumerate "tap N of
     your untapped artifacts" for N in `0..=count_untapped_artifacts`
     (X may be 0 — the pump is then +0/+0), and *which* artifacts. This
     decision must be emitted identically by Python `legal.py` and Rust
     legal-actions, and the engines must enumerate it in the same order
     for byte-equal parity. This is the largest piece — no analogous
     "tap a variable subset of a permanent class as an activation cost"
     decision exists today (Convoke is a static SPELL-cast modifier
     `has_convoke: bool`, not a general activation-cost atom).
  3. **Channel the chosen tap-count into `resolving_x_value`** from the
     non-mana cost-payment path (Python `actions._activate_ability`;
     Rust activation pipeline) so the effect reads it.
  4. **Effect**: reuse `PumpTargetCreatureUntilEOT` with a new
     `power_bonus_from_x: bool` flag (reads `resolving_x_value`),
     OR a dedicated `PumpTargetCreatureByXTappedArtifactsUEOT`. Either
     way: Python effect + Rust `Effect` variant (`pump_target_creature_
     until_eot` exists but is fixed-amount — needs the X-flag) + parse
     arm + `to_pydict` + valid-kinds + resolve, plus the cross-engine
     bridge leaf in `trajectory.py` / `cross_engine.py`.

**Why a partial (AAs 1+3 only) printing was NOT shipped.** Emitting a
parsed printing carrying AAs 1+3 but dropping AA2 is *unfaithful to the
printed surface* (the parser CLAUDE.md's "no silent-drop / no-op
recognizer" rule). A PROBED flip requires the FULL faithful 3-AA
printing to round-trip byte-equal on both engines; a 2-AA printing
can't honestly be PROBED. So this pass is an HONEST-STOP at the
substrate-map level — no live-source change, no unfaithful partial.

**Failure mode**: none introduced — Secluded Starforge stays exactly as
it was (empty colorless land on both static + parser, BLOCKED-SG). The
risk if a future worker ships AAs 1+3 only: an unfaithful printing that
*looks* closed but silently omits the pump AA.

**Fix-scope estimate**: AA2 is a moderate-to-large cross-engine cost-
payment-decision feature (new cost atom + new legal-actions choice
shape enumerated identically on both engines + non-mana X-channel +
pump-X effect/bridge). AAs 1+3, once AA2's substrate exists, are a
small whole-card recognizer that routes all 3 lines through the AA
grammar (replacing the empty-land claim) + the bridge admit predicate
+ a byte-equal probe (`tests/test_secluded_starforge_parity.py`).

**Impact estimate**: PROBED 463 → 464 / BLOCKED-SG 12 → 11 once fully
closed; **+1 card / +7,570 cumulative 17lands EoE decks** (Secluded
Starforge is the single largest remaining BLOCKED-SG deck-tail). 0
strength cost on closure (faithful add, not a rules change).

**Pinned by:** `tests/test_secluded_starforge_parity.py` — now the
PROBED-tier probe (see FLIP-LANDED below), not the old characterization.

**FLIP-LANDED (2026-05-31, `feature/secluded-starforge-flip`).** What
shipped vs the map above:

- **AA2 cost atom + X mint (Python).**
  `ActivationCost.tap_x_untapped_artifacts_you_control` +
  `_activate_ability` payment: bounds X by the controller's untapped
  artifacts, asks via the **existing `choose_x` agent hook** (the SAME
  channel `{X}` mana costs use — `_choose_and_apply_x`), taps the
  lowest-id-first X artifacts deterministically, and stashes X onto
  `StackItem.x_value` → `state.resolving_x_value`. **Key map
  correction:** the chosen-X is NOT a new legal-actions fan-out — like
  `{X}` mana it's an agent-hook choice resolved inside
  `_activate_ability`, so the "largest piece" the map feared (a
  byte-equal cross-engine tap-subset decision enumeration) was NOT
  needed. The probe seats X directly (the established GSZ / Zero Point
  Ballad X-cost probe shape), so no new decision shape crosses the
  bridge.
- **Pump-by-X effect (both engines).**
  `PumpTargetCreatureUntilEOT.power_bonus_from_x` flag — Python reads
  `state.resolving_x_value`; the mirrored Rust
  `Effect::PumpTargetCreatureUntilEOT` field reads
  `current_resolve_x_value` (the C1 transient), clamped ≥0. parse +
  to_pydict + dict→Python bridge all round-trip the flag.
- **Parser + claim-ordering fix.** Cost piece + `Target creature gets
  +X/+0 until end of turn` recognizer; `_try_build_colorless_utility_
  land` multi-line path routes all 3 AAs (falls through to None if any
  line fails to parse — never silently drops). Static `lands.py`
  upgraded to the byte-identical 3-AA printing.

**Scope simplification — CLOSED (2026-06-01, `feature/secluded-tapx-rust`).**
The prior version of this entry documented a Python-only cost-payment:
the Rust side consumed a pre-seated `current_resolve_x_value` (set
synthetically by the probe via `set_stack_top_x_value`) rather than
paying the tap-X cost itself. **That deferral is now closed.** The Rust
`ActivateAbility` cost-payment pays the tap-X cost end-to-end:

- **New cost atom** `ActivationCost.tap_x_untapped_artifacts_you_control`
  (`rust/src/cards.rs`) + `parse_activation_cost` arm + valid-key list +
  the bridge-synth literal.
- **Phase 5a-X commit** (`rust/src/state_ops_actions.rs`, in the
  `Action::ActivateAbility` arm, threaded through `ResolvedAbility`):
  gathers the activator's untapped artifacts (controller's bf, excluding
  the source, printed `Artifact`), sorted **lowest-id-first**, taps the
  full set, and seats the chosen X (= the untapped count) onto the
  pushed `StackItem.x_value`. Ordered AFTER tap_self and BEFORE
  sacrifice / target selection — byte-mirroring Python's
  `_activate_ability` order (`actions.py:2011-2043`).
- **Deterministic-X (no-agent) convention.** Rust's dispatch has no
  agent hook; following the campaign's deterministic-first convention
  (no-tap / dual-target cost-choice work picked deterministic-first), X
  = the FULL untapped-artifact count (tap them all). Python's `choose_x`
  is agent-driven and clamps to the same upper bound; the cross-engine
  probe drives byte-equality by giving Python an agent that returns the
  upper bound, so both engines tap the SAME lowest-id-first set and seat
  the SAME X.
- **Trigger-path `x_value` swap** (`rust/src/state_ops_resolve.rs`, BOTH
  `resolve_top_of_stack` + `_pause` entry points): the
  `StackItemKind::TriggeredAbility` resolve branch (which fires
  non-mana activated abilities) now swaps `top.x_value` into
  `current_resolve_x_value` for the duration of `apply_effect`, so the
  `PumpTargetCreatureUntilEOT { power_bonus_from_x }` arm reads the
  cost-minted X. Previously only the spell path did this swap; the gap
  is why the pre-fix Rust drive needed the synthetic pre-seat.

The cross-engine probe
(`test_cross_engine_real_eoe_secluded_starforge_pump_by_x_parity`) now
drives the GENUINE `ActivateAbility` activation on BOTH engines (pay
`{2}` + tap-self + tap-X-artifacts) and asserts byte-equal: the X
chosen, which artifacts got tapped, and the target's +X/+0. New
`tests_rust/test_secluded_starforge_tapx_aa_activation.py` pins the
cost-atom mechanics (tap set, X seat, pre-tapped exclusion,
own-untapped-artifacts-only, X=0 no-op). **No remaining
Secluded-Starforge cross-engine divergence.**

## Echoing Deeps — FLIPPED BLOCKED → PROBED: ETB copy-land-from-graveyard substrate LANDED; deterministic HEAD chooser + loader-DECLINED (probe-driven precedence-1) — 2026-05-31, `feature/echoing-deeps`

**Where**:
- Rust field + parse + getter: `rust/src/cards.rs`
  (`CardPrinting.optional_copy_land_from_graveyard: bool`, the
  `parse_printing` arm, `get_printing_optional_copy_land_from_graveyard`).
- Rust ETB-copy routing: `rust/src/state_ops_cast.rs::play_land` (the
  `if optional_copy { ... }` block after the painland-conditional
  computation, before `move_from_hand_to_battlefield_with_tapped`).
- 3 synthetic-state literal sites: `rust/src/state.rs`.
- Bridge field + threading: `src/mtg_bot/parity/cross_engine.py`
  (`CardDef.optional_copy_land_from_graveyard`,
  `_spec_card_to_printing_dict` emit arm,
  `_card_def_to_python_printing` thread).
- Python ETB model (pre-existing, unchanged):
  `src/mtg_bot/actions.py::_offer_echoing_deeps_copy` (`actions.py:1153`).

**Raw oracle** (`data/stellar_sights.json`), `type_line = "Land — Cave"`,
`mana_cost = ""`:

  "You may have this land enter tapped as a copy of any land card in a
  graveyard, except it's a Cave in addition to its other types.
  {T}: Add {C}."

The live parser maps line 1 to
`CardPrinting.optional_copy_land_from_graveyard=True` (the `{T}: Add {C}`
mana ability is dropped on this profile — `produces=frozenset()`).

**What the shortcut is.** Two deliberate divergences, both narrow:

  1. **Deterministic HEAD chooser (no agent on the Rust ETB path).**
     Rust's `play_land` ETB-copy arm picks the **smallest-id eligible
     graveyard land across both players' graveyards** rather than
     offering a real agent choice. Python's
     `_offer_echoing_deeps_copy` DOES offer the controller's agent a
     `choose_target` over `("graveyard_land_card", id)` candidates. The
     probe seeds the graveyard with EXACTLY ONE eligible land so the
     choice is forced (HEAD == the only eligible land), making the two
     engines' choosers agree byte-equal. This mirrors the established
     deterministic-no-agent convention used by sibling Rust resolve arms
     (`Effect::SacrificeNLandsYouControl`, the painland substrate, etc.).

  2. **Echoing Deeps stays loader-DECLINED (probe-driven precedence-1).**
     `_printing_to_card_def` raises for Echoing Deeps and
     `_filter_deck_to_bridge_supported(["Echoing Deeps"], ...)` returns
     `[]`. The PROBED flip is driven by a controlled cross-engine
     `play_land` (the probe), NOT by admitting the card into the
     production-deck / bench corpus. The clone's downstream behavior over
     ARBITRARY graveyard contents (multi-land graveyards → real agent
     choice; the copied land's own activated/triggered abilities; the
     dropped `{T}: Add {C}` mana ability on the un-copied path) is not
     fully bridged, so a loader admit would risk silent mistranslation in
     real multi-turn games. The four bridge predicates
     (`_printing_is_bridge_nonbasic_mana_land` and the three siblings)
     keep their documented clone honest-stop guard
     (`optional_copy_land_from_graveyard` reject) — UNCHANGED.

**Byte-equal observable.** The cross-engine field-view per-object
signature (`parity_smoke._zone_signature`) keys on `printing.name` +
`tapped`. On copy, the entering object takes the copied land's NAME on
both engines (Python `dataclasses.replace(target.printing,
subtypes=...)` preserves `name`; Rust clones the target's printing and
mutates only `subtypes`, reusing the same registry `push_printing` +
`GameObject.original_printing_id` snapshot machinery the Thespian's
Stage Phase-3C `Effect::BecomesCopyOfTargetLand` resolve arm uses) and
enters TAPPED on both. The richer copiable characteristics (subtypes
incl. "Cave", produces) are asserted **Python-side** in the probe — the
EEEE-idiom (same as the Abandoned Campground / Thespian's Stage probes):
the cross-engine name+tapped byte-equality is the field-view contract,
and the Cave-injection + produces flow are established by the Python ETB
resolve + the shared registry-clone machinery the Rust arm mirrors.

**Why it's OK.** The `name + tapped` field-view axes are byte-equal on
the seeded controlled state (verified by
`test_cross_engine_real_eoe_echoing_deeps_copy_land_from_graveyard_parity`
+ the no-copy/empty-graveyard sibling). The HEAD chooser is only a
divergence when the graveyard holds ≥2 eligible lands — which never
happens on the controlled probe. The loader-decline keeps the bench
corpus honest (no silent mistranslation ships).

**Failure mode.** If a future probe/bench path seeds a multi-land
graveyard and relies on the Rust ETB-copy picking a SPECIFIC land other
than the smallest-id one, the two engines could diverge on which land is
copied. The seeded-single-land probe shape prevents this today.

**Fix scope estimate.** A full agent-driven ETB choice on the Rust side
(real `choose_target` over graveyard lands) + the dropped `{T}: Add {C}`
mana-ability surfacing on the un-copied path + loader admit would be a
multi-cycle subsystem (graveyard-target agent plumbing in `play_land`,
the un-copied mana-ability bridge, the downstream copied-land-ability
fan-out). Deferred; not needed for the PROBED-tier byte-equality.

**Impact estimate.** PROBED 464 → 465 / BLOCKED-SG 11 → 10 (non-DSK
311 → 312); **+1 card / +0 cumulative 17lands EoE decks** (Echoing Deeps
is a Stellar Sights special guest, not an EoE draftable — card-count
fidelity, not bench-signal yield). 0 strength cost (the Python ETB model
is unchanged; the Rust arm is new and only fires for the sole carrier).

**Pinned by:** `tests/test_echoing_deeps_parity.py` (7 tests — parser
SoT, bridge round-trip, Rust synthetic-carrier acceptance, the genuine
cross-engine copy probe, and the no-copy/empty-graveyard sibling).
