## Rust port — Consult the Star Charts: kicker mana-payment cast pipeline NOW WIRED; probe drives a REAL Rust kicked cast (2026-06-01)

**Status.** The kicker mana-payment cast pipeline (shortcuts 1 & 2
below) is **CLOSED** as of the `feature/consult-kicker-payment` slice
(2026-06-01). `cast_spell_noncreature` now pays base+kicker and mints
`StackItem.was_kicked` from the real payment; the cross-engine probe
drives both engines through their genuine cast pipelines. Shortcut 3
(no `reset_public_knowledge` mirror) remains an accepted divergence —
it is byte-neutral on the fingerprint surface. The original deferral
text is preserved below with the closure annotated inline.

**Where (current).** `rust/src/cards.rs` (`Effect::ConsultTheStarCharts`
variant + `CardPrinting.kicker_cost: Option<ManaCost>` field +
parse arm); `rust/src/state_ops_cast.rs`
(`cast_spell_noncreature`'s `kicked` param — kicker-cost fold +
`was_kicked` mint); `rust/src/state_ops_actions.rs` (the
`Action::CastSpell{kicked}` dispatch thread-through);
`rust/src/state_ops_resolve.rs` (the resolve arm + the two
spell-resolve `current_resolve_was_kicked` swaps); `rust/src/state.rs`
(`StackItem.was_kicked` + `current_resolve_was_kicked`);
`rust/src/state_ops_stack.rs` (`stack_top_was_kicked` /
`set_stack_top_was_kicked` — the synthetic getter/setter substrate
stays for low-level pins but is NO LONGER the cross-engine kicked
driver); `src/mtg_bot/parity/cross_engine.py` (the
`consult_the_star_charts_effect` bridge arm);
`tests/test_consult_the_star_charts_parity.py` (the probes — now real
casts); `tests_rust/test_cast.py` (the kicker-payment pins).

**What the shortcuts WERE (now closed except #3).**

1. ~~**Kicker mana-payment cast pipeline is NOT ported to Rust.**~~
   **CLOSED (2026-06-01).** Consult the Star Charts carries the Kicker
   additional-cost mechanic (`kicker_cost = {1}{U}`). Python models
   kicker end-to-end (the `CastSpell.kicked` flag, `legal.py`'s
   kicked/unkicked dual emission, the base+kicker mana payment at
   `actions.py:1588-1601`, the `StackItem.kicked` field, the
   `state.resolving_kicked` swap). Rust now mirrors the cast side:
   `CardPrinting.kicker_cost: Option<ManaCost>` carries the kicker;
   `cast_spell_noncreature(obj_id, player_id, kicked=false)` (pyo3
   optional arg — every pre-slice 2-arg caller stays byte-identical)
   folds the kicker onto the base cost (CR 601.2f total cost — generic +
   each colored pip summed, `x_pips` preserved) BEFORE X resolution,
   pays the combined cost via the SAME `auto_tap_pay_for_cost`, and
   mints `StackItem.was_kicked = true`. The `Action::CastSpell{kicked}`
   dispatch threads the flag through. A kicked cast with only base-mana
   available now correctly FAILS to pay (the kicker is genuinely
   charged, not a synthetic flag). Kicker on the CREATURE cast path
   (`cast_creature`) is still deferred (no kicker-carrying creature in
   the live EoE pool); warp/impending/free-cast cast-payment stay
   deferred under their own contracts (see the alt-cost map below).

2. ~~**The probe drives the kicked branch via a synthetic StackItem
   setter, not a real kicked cast.**~~ **CLOSED (2026-06-01).** The
   cross-engine probe now drives a REAL kicked cast on both engines:
   Python's genuine `_cast_spell(..., kicked=True)` (folds kicker_cost,
   auto-taps blue Islands, sets `StackItem.kicked`) and Rust's real
   `cast_spell_noncreature(spell_id, 0, kicked=True)` (folds kicker_cost,
   pays base+kicker, mints `was_kicked`). The lands now produce blue
   mana (Island subtype + `mana_produced=["U"]`) so the {1}{U}{1}{U}
   combined cost is auto-tap-payable; X (= land count) tracks the funding
   land count, and the library staging is sized so the kept/bottomed
   sets match across both engines byte-equal. The `set_stack_top_was_
   kicked` synthetic setter is retained as a low-level substrate (pinned
   by `test_rust_was_kicked_stack_flag_round_trips`) but is no longer the
   parity-load-bearing driver. The legal-action kicked/unkicked dual
   emission on the Rust legal-cast path was NOT needed for byte-equal
   parity here (the probe calls the cast primitive directly, mirroring
   every other cross-engine cast probe); Python's `legal.py` dual
   emission is the SoT and unchanged.

3. **No `reset_public_knowledge` mirror in Rust** (STILL an accepted
   divergence). Python clears per-card
   public-knowledge reveal bits on the kept + bottomed cards
   (`effects/bespoke.py:1193/1201`). Rust has no public-knowledge surface
   in the cross-engine fingerprint (zone membership + per-object
   signature only), so the observable post-resolve state is byte-equal
   without it.

**Why it's OK.** PROBED is precedence-1 (probe-driven; no loader admit).
The probe asserts byte-equality on the post-resolve hand + library zones
across BOTH cast modes (unkicked keep-1; kicked keep-2; + a shared-
`random.Random` random-bottom). As of 2026-06-01 both engines drive
their GENUINE cast pipeline (cast-time kicker payment + `was_kicked`
mint), so the byte-equal claim now covers the cast side end-to-end, not
just the resolve rider. The `was_kicked` flag is additive + NOT
fingerprinted (mirrors `is_copy`), so every non-kicked push is `false`
and parity-NEUTRAL; the new `kicker_cost` printing field is `None` for
every non-kicker printing (back-compat parse default), so non-kicker
casts are byte-identical.

**Failure mode (post-closure).** None for the kicker cast path — a Rust
kicked cast now pays `{1}{U}{1}{U}` and resolves `was_kicked=true`
(keep 2), byte-equal to Python. The residual deferral is the CREATURE
kicker cast path (`cast_creature` ignores `kicked`): no kicker-carrying
creature is in the live EoE pool, so this is unreachable until such a
card is admitted. Consult is still not loader-admitted (PROBED), so the
only cross-engine driver remains the probe — which now exercises the
real cast.

**Remaining alt-cost cast-payment map (for a future cross-cutting
slice).** The kicker slice is **kicker-isolated** — it did NOT touch the
shared warp/impending/free-cast payment. Those stay deferred under their
own contracts:
  * **warp** — already LIVE on `cast_creature_warp` (pays `warp_cost`);
    the noncreature warp cast path is not yet exercised.
  * **impending** — `use_impending` flag still passes through silently
    (needs `impending_cost` payment + time-counter ETB init).
  * **free-cast** (`cast_for_free`) — flag still passes through silently
    (needs the mana-cost bypass in the pay phase).
  The kicker fold (`cast_spell_noncreature`'s `kicked` arm) is a clean
  template the impending/free-cast arms could reuse (read the printing's
  alt-cost, substitute/fold onto the base, pay via the SAME
  `auto_tap_pay_for_cost`, mint the matching StackItem flag) — but each
  is its own bounded slice; no general alt-cost refactor was attempted
  (honest-stop policy: kicker-only, no risky broad rework).

**Impact estimate.** No tier change (Consult was already PROBED). This
slice hardens the Rust CAST side to byte-equality (the resolve side was
already byte-equal). 0 strength cost (the Python model is unchanged; the
Rust kicker fold is additive and only fires for a kicker-carrying
printing cast with `kicked=true`, which is not loader-admitted).

**Pinned by:** `tests/test_consult_the_star_charts_parity.py` (10 tests —
parser SoT incl. the kicker-only / not-warp verify-first check, the
bridge round-trip, Rust synthetic-carrier acceptance, the `was_kicked`
flag round-trip, and the three genuine cross-engine byte-equal probes
now driving REAL casts: unkicked keep-1, kicked keep-2, and the kicked
random-bottom over a shared `random.Random`) + `tests_rust/test_cast.py`
(4 kicker-payment pins: `kicker_cost` parse round-trip, kicked cast pays
base+kicker & mints `was_kicked`, unkicked cast pays base-only, kicked
cast FAILS when only base is payable — the "kicker genuinely charged"
guard).

## Rust port — Tezzeret, Cruel Captain: loyalty-ACTIVATION subsystem + 0/−3/−7 abilities SHIPPED byte-equal; ONLY the −7 emblem's becomes-0/0-Robot animate honest-stopped (2026-06-01)

**UPDATE (2026-06-01, feature/tezzeret-loyalty).** The loyalty-ACTIVATION
subsystem and the 0 / −3 abilities are now SHIPPED byte-equal on both
engines (the prior deferral in the historical entry below is CLOSED
except for the −7 emblem):

- **Loyalty-activation subsystem (Python side, mirroring Rust's existing
  substrate).** Added `ActivationCost.loyalty: int = 0` (signed cost,
  same sign convention as Rust: a printed `+N` ability stamps
  `loyalty=-N` ADD, a `−N` ability stamps `loyalty=+N` PAY, `0:` stamps
  `loyalty=0`) at `effects/base.py`; the emission gate +
  once-per-turn-per-walker ledger (`state.loyalty_activated_this_turn`,
  cloned in `GameState.clone` + cleared in `turn.run_cleanup_step`) at
  `legal.py` / `game.py` / `turn.py`; the apply commit
  (`obj.loyalty_counters -= cost.loyalty` + ledger insert) at
  `actions._activate_ability`; the bridge `loyalty` cost key at
  `parity/cross_engine.py` `_aa_dict_to_python_activation_cost`. The
  parser (`cards/parser/planeswalker_builder.py`) now recognizes
  loyalty-activation lines (no longer strips them) and emits
  `ActivatedAbility(cost=ActivationCost(loyalty=N), sorcery_speed=True,
  effect=...)`. Rust's half (`ActivationCost.loyalty` + emission gate +
  `loyalty_activated_this_turn` ledger + loyalty-at-0 SBA) already
  existed and is unchanged — the Python side now mirrors it byte-equal.
- **0 ability** — "Untap target artifact or creature. If it's an
  artifact creature, put a +1/+1 counter on it." New
  `UntapTargetArtifactOrCreatureConditionalCounter` effect on BOTH
  engines (Python `effects/generic/tap.py`; Rust
  `Effect::UntapTargetArtifactOrCreatureConditionalCounter` — enum
  variant + `parse_effect` arm + `to_dict` arm + resolve arm with a
  deterministic first-match source-controller-side target pick).
  Byte-equal observable: untap + conditional +1/+1 on an artifact
  creature.
- **−3 ability** — "Search your library for an artifact card with mana
  value 1 or less, ..." Reuses the `SearchLibraryForCard` family with a
  new `artifact_small` filter (artifact card type + `mana_value <=
  max_mv`, with `max_mv=1`) on BOTH engines
  (`effects/generic/search.py` `_matches`; Rust
  `state_ops_resolve.rs` filter dispatch). Byte-equal deterministic
  first-match tutor (library → hand, loyalty 4 → 1).
- **Pinned by** `tests/test_tezzeret_cruel_captain_parity.py` (the
  loyalty-activation-cost + once-per-turn cross-engine probe; the 0
  untap+counter cross-engine probe; the −3 search cross-engine probe;
  the loyalty-cost bridge round-trip; the parser shape SoT) +
  `tests_rust/test_resolve.py` (5 new pins: untap-conditional-counter

  fetch-MV1 / skip-MV2) + the pre-existing `tests_rust/test_activated.py`

**UPDATE (2026-06-01, feature/tezzeret-emblem): the −7 EMBLEM
substrate LANDED byte-equal; ONLY the becomes-0/0-Robot animate
honest-stopped.** The emblem-object substrate (which did not exist on
EITHER engine) is now built and the −7 is modeled. Tezzeret's −7
grants an emblem with "At the beginning of combat on your turn, put
three +1/+1 counters on target artifact you control. If it's not a
creature, it becomes a 0/0 Robot artifact creature."

What LANDED (byte-equal cross-engine):

1. **Emblem object + command zone (CR 114).** `GameState.emblems:
   list[GameObject]` (Python, `game.py`) / `GameState.emblems:
   Vec<GameObject>` (Rust, `state.rs`). Each emblem is a synthetic
   `GameObject` (`Zone.COMMAND` / `ZONE_COMMAND=6`) whose `printing` is
   a synthetic `CardPrinting` (`make_emblem` Python / a source-printing
   clone stripped to CR-114.3 bare-abilities shape Rust) carrying ONLY
   the emblem's begin-combat trigger. Cloned in both `clone()`s;
   surfaced via Rust `emblems_snapshot`; fingerprinted via an emblems
   slot appended ONLY when non-empty (Python `parity_smoke.hash_state`
   + Rust `fingerprint()`), so every pre-emblem baseline stays
   byte-identical. Empty by default — no zone-transition plumbing
   (emblems never move, CR 114.5).
2. **`CreateEmblem` effect.** "You get an emblem with '...'." New
   effect on both engines (`effects/generic/emblem.py` Python;
   `Effect::CreateEmblem { emblem_kind }` Rust — parse + reverse
   `effect_to_pydict` + resolve via the `BecomesCopyOfTargetLand`
   per-resolve-printing `Arc::make_mut().push_printing` pattern). The
   parser (`planeswalker_builder.py`) now un-strips the −7 line and
   emits `CreateEmblem`. Bridge: `create_emblem` arm
   (`parity/cross_engine.py`) with a string `emblem_kind` discriminant.
3. **Emblem-sourced begin-combat trigger.** Both engines' trigger
   dispatchers (`dispatch_event` Python `actions.py` / Rust
   `state_ops_resolve.rs`) extended to scan `state.emblems` as an
   additional trigger SOURCE (Rust also extends `find_object_controller`
   so `ControlledByYou` resolves the emblem's controller). The emblem's
   "At the beginning of combat on your turn, …" ability fires from the
   command zone onto the stack.
4. **The 3-counter body.** `TezzeretEmblemBeginCombat` (Python) /
   `Effect::TezzeretEmblemBeginCombat { amount=3 }` (Rust): picks the
   first artifact the controller controls (deterministic, mirroring the
   sibling 0-ability target convention) and adds three +1/+1 counters
   (counter-doubling replacement honored; CountersAdded observer
   dispatched). Byte-equal: artifact net counters 0 → 3.

**HONEST-STOP (the becomes-0/0-Robot animate ONLY).** "If it's not a
creature, it becomes a 0/0 Robot artifact creature" is NOT applied —
the counters land, the type/P/T change does not. This is a PERMANENT
(not UEOT) layer-4 type-adding set (the artifact GAINS the Creature
card type + the Robot creature subtype) PLUS a layer-7b base-P/T set
(0/0). Why deferred:

- **No permanent type+P/T-set animate substrate exists on either
  engine.** The closest precedents are all UEOT and shaped for OTHER
  permanent types: `BecomeLandCreatureUEOT` (manland animation — a
  LAND, UEOT, with a fixed granted P/T) and the Spacecraft "becomes a
  creature" UEOT arm. There is NO arm that (a) targets an ARTIFACT, (b)
  ADDS the creature type while keeping the artifact type, (c) sets base
  P/T to 0/0, and (d) does so PERMANENTLY (lives forever, not cleared
  at cleanup). Building it touches the layer-4 type-layer reader and
  the layer-7b base-P/T reader on BOTH engines plus a new permanent
  (non-UEOT) continuous-effect lifetime, and must keep the 0/0 + any
  +1/+1 counters interacting correctly through the SBA (a 0/0 with 3
  +1/+1 counters is a 3/3 that survives; a 0/0 with 0 counters dies to
  CR 704.5f) — a multi-file layer-system slice.
- **Fix scope.** Both engines: a new `becomes_permanent_type_and_pt`
  continuous-effect kind (layer-4 add-type + layer-7b set-base-PT,
  PERMANENT lifetime) + the layer readers consulting it for artifacts +
  the SBA interplay with the simultaneously-added +1/+1 counters.
  Estimate ~3-5 cycles. NOT taken here per the campaign honest-stop
  policy — the 3-counter half is the bounded, byte-equal win, and NO
  risky broad layer-system refactor was attempted.
- **Failure mode.** In a real game, after the emblem's begin-combat
  trigger resolves on a NON-creature artifact, both engines agree it
  has 3 +1/+1 counters but DISAGREE-with-the-rules on its type: it
  stays a non-creature artifact (so it can't attack / block and the
  3 counters are inert on a non-creature). Both engines agree WITH EACH
  OTHER (byte-equal) — the divergence is from CR, not cross-engine. On
  an artifact that is ALREADY a creature, the emblem is fully correct
  (the "if it's not a creature" clause doesn't fire). Impact: 0
  cross-engine strength cost; a fidelity gap only on the
  not-yet-a-creature target case.

**Pinned by:** `tests/test_tezzeret_cruel_captain_parity.py` (+2 —
the emblem-effect bridge round-trip and the full cross-engine
byte-equal −7 emblem flow asserting the becomes-Robot animate is NOT
applied on both engines; the parser-SoT test now expects 3 modeled
abilities) + `tests_rust/test_tezzeret_emblem.py` (8 Rust pins:
parse/reverse round-trip, unknown-kind + negative-amount rejection,
CreateEmblem resolve → command zone, begin-combat 3-counter body,
no-artifact fizzle, fingerprint emblems slot, clone independence).

(`_LOYALTY_ACTIVATION_PREFIX` strips the printed loyalty-activation
lines).

**What this slice ships (byte-equal on both engines).** Tezzeret, Cruel
Captain (the LAST non-Duskmourn BLOCKED card) flips
blocked_subsystem_gated → PROBED on the planeswalker loyalty-GAIN
substrate: the `is_planeswalker`/`loyalty=4` printing surface, the
ENTERS → `PutLoyaltyCounterOnSelf(amount=1)` loyalty-gain trigger
("Whenever an artifact you control enters, put a loyalty counter on
Tezzeret"), the `loyalty_counters` GameObject slot (snapshot-surfaced
on both engines), and the walker-at-0 SBA. The cross-engine probe
drives the loyalty-gain effect through BOTH engines' resolve paths and
asserts byte-equal loyalty 4 → 5.

**What is DELIBERATELY DEFERRED (the shortcut).** The three printed
loyalty-ACTIVATED abilities and the emblem are NOT modeled on the
Python side and so are NOT probed:

- `0: Untap target artifact or creature. If it's an artifact creature,
  put a +1/+1 counter on it.`
- `−3: Search your library for an artifact card with mana value 1 or
  less, ...`
- `−7: You get an emblem with '...'.`

**Why it's OK / what makes it not-OK.** The PYTHON parser intentionally
strips loyalty-activation lines — Python has NO loyalty-ability
activation substrate (no pay/add-loyalty `ActivationCost` atom, no
sorcery-speed once-per-turn-per-walker activation gate, no emblem
object). RUST, by contrast, ALREADY carries the full loyalty-COST
activation substrate (`ActivationCost.loyalty` signed cost + emission
gate at `state_ops_legal.rs` + `loyalty_activated_this_turn`
once-per-turn-per-walker ledger per CR 606.3 + the loyalty SBA). The
asymmetry means a byte-equal cross-engine activation probe is not
buildable on the Python side today: you would have to build the entire
Python loyalty-ability-activation subsystem first. The −7 emblem has no
emblem-object substrate on EITHER engine. Not-OK if/when a strategy
actually activates Tezzeret's abilities in a real game — the loyalty
abilities (and the immediate board-affecting untap/search/+1+1 they
provide) are then invisible to both the engine and the search.

**Failure mode.** In a real game, Tezzeret sits on the battlefield,
grows loyalty off artifact ETBs (modeled), and can be attacked / dies
at 0 loyalty (modeled), but never activates an ability — the 0/−3/−7
lines are no-ops. No crash, no divergence (both engines agree: zero
loyalty abilities offered, because the printing carries none). The
loss is strength fidelity for this single planeswalker, not a parity
break.

**Fix scope estimate.** Large — the full Python planeswalker
loyalty-ability-activation subsystem: a signed loyalty `ActivationCost`
atom + `_activate_ability` loyalty pay/add + the sorcery-speed
once-per-turn-per-walker activation gate (CR 606.3) + parser
recognition of the `[+−-]?\d+:` activation lines (currently stripped)
+ the three abilities' effects (untap-target+conditional-+1/+1 reusing
existing untap+put-counter; search-artifact-MV≤1 reusing the
SearchLibraryForCard family with an artifact+MV≤1 filter; the −7
emblem needs a NEW emblem-object substrate on both engines). Rust's
half of the activation machinery already exists; the work is almost
entirely Python-side. Estimate ~4-6 cycles, emblem its own multi-cycle
slice.

**Impact estimate.** PROBED 467 → 468 / BLOCKED-SG 8 → 7 (non-DSK
314/315 → **315/315 = 100%** of the non-DSK pool — the campaign
milestone). The 7 remaining BLOCKED cards are all Duskmourn off-set
special-guest cards. +1 card; 0 strength cost on the modeled slice
(loyalty-gain + SBA are byte-equal); the deferred loyalty-activation /
emblem strength cost is the fidelity gap above.

**Pinned by:** `tests/test_tezzeret_cruel_captain_parity.py` (6 tests —
parser SoT incl. the activated-abilities-stripped verify-first check,
the bridge round-trip byte-equality vs the real parsed printing, Rust
synthetic-carrier acceptance, and the genuine cross-engine byte-equal
loyalty-gain probe driving BOTH engines' resolve to loyalty 5) +
`tests_rust/test_resolve.py` (4 `put_loyalty_counter_on_self` resolve
pins: increment / amount-two / amount-zero-no-op / off-battlefield
fizzle, mirroring the sibling `PutPlusOneCounterOnSelf` pins).

## DealDamageEqualToSourcePowerAnyTarget — DIES-trigger LKI + counter read (CLOSED, hub todo ddc12150)

**Location**: `rust/src/state_ops_resolve.rs` — the
`Effect::DealDamageEqualToSourcePowerAnyTarget` resolve arm + the new
`read_source_power_lki` helper (sibling of `read_famished_source_power`).

**What the shortcut WAS (now FIXED)**: the resolve arm read the
source's power by searching ONLY `player.battlefield` for the source
object and computing `base + ueot_power_bonus` (counters OMITTED). Two
divergences from Python's `DealDamageEqualToSourcePowerAnyTarget.resolve`
(`effects/generic/damage.py`), which reads
`effective_power(state, state.resolving_source)`:

1. **DIES-trigger last-known-information (CR 603.10).** Fired from a
   DIES / leaves-battlefield trigger, the source is in the graveyard at
   resolve time. The battlefield-only scan found nothing → `amount = 0`
   → silent no-op. Python's `state.resolving_source` is the
   `StackItem.source` GameObject reference captured at push time (the
   dying creature that survived the zone move), so Python deals the
   creature's last-known power. *Live divergence:* real-EoE Infernal
   Phantom DIES trigger — Python p1 −2/−3, Rust unchanged.

2. **Counter omission (CR 613 layer 7d).** The old read dropped
   `obj.counters`. The on-battlefield consumer Rust Harvester
   (`Sequence(PutPlusOneCounterOnSelf,
   DealDamageEqualToSourcePowerAnyTarget)`) adds a +1/+1 counter to
   itself THEN deals damage equal to its power — a 1/1 must deal 2.
   Pre-fix Rust read printed power 1 and dealt 1; Python read 2.

**The fix**: `read_source_power_lki(state, source_obj_id)` searches the
battlefield FIRST then falls back to every other zone (graveyard /
exile / hand / library / stack store), computing
`base_override.or(printed) + ueot_power_bonus + counters` — mirroring
`read_famished_source_power` + Python's `effective_power` for the
no-anthem/no-switch case. On-battlefield sources with no counters stay
byte-identical (battlefield searched first, same composition; `.max(0)`
floor preserved per CR 119.5). This works because BOTH engines' death-
move keep the dying object's `counters` + `ueot_modifiers` on the
graveyard copy (Rust `state_ops_sba.rs:982-986` clears
damage/tapped/attached but keeps counters; Python `move_off_battlefield`
likewise), so the all-zones search reproduces Python's
`resolving_source` reference read without threading a new payload field
through the trigger-push pipeline.

**Why no payload field was needed**: unlike the combat-damage
transients (which are reset after the synchronous observer walk and so
need a `TriggerPayload` snapshot), the dying GameObject itself persists
in the graveyard with its power-relevant fields intact until end-of-
turn cleanup. An id-keyed all-zones search is the lower-blast-radius
mirror of Python's by-reference read.

**Documented residual (shared with `read_famished_source_power`)**:
layer-7c static anthems and layer-7e P/T switches are NOT folded here
(same established combat-side asymmetry). No real-EoE source-power
consumer (Infernal Phantom DIES, Rust Harvester AA, Ouroboroid
beginning-of-combat trigger) stages an anthem/switch rider on the
source, so this is observationally byte-equal on the genuine pool.

**Sibling-pattern audit**: the two non-DSK source-power consumers are
**Rust Harvester** (`DealDamageEqualToSourcePowerAnyTarget`, on-bf
activated — had the latent counter bug, now byte-equal) and
**Ouroboroid** (`PutPlusOneCountersOnEachCreatureYouControlEqualToSource
Power`, on-bf beginning-of-combat trigger — uses
`read_famished_source_power`, already counter-correct and not DIES-
reachable, so unaffected). No other `*EqualToSourcePower*` Rust resolve
arm has the battlefield-only-search shape that is DIES-reachable.

**Status**: CLOSED. **Failure mode**: none remaining (divergence pin
flipped to a cross-engine byte-equal parity probe). **Impact**:
correctness gain; zero strength/perf cost (on-bf no-counter path
byte-identical).

**Pinned by**:
`tests/test_divergence_pins_dd.py::test_cross_engine_real_eoe_infernal_phantom_dies_damage_source_power_lki_parity`
(flipped from the divergence pin — both engines now deal 3 to p1) +
`tests/test_rust_harvester_parity.py::test_cross_engine_real_eoe_source_power_lki_with_counter_dies_damage_parity`
(counter-inclusive LKI cross-engine probe — 2/1 + counter deals 3) +
the existing `test_rust_harvester_parity.py` Python-side AA resolve
probe + `tests/test_deal_damage_equal_to_power_resolve.py` (Python
resolve pins).

## Structured-NN action history — inference now sees the SAME history as training (CLOSED); the Rust provider still tokenizes with an EMPTY history (open, bounded) — 2026-09-22, `feature/lf-history`

**Where:** `src/mtg_bot/search/action_history.py` (new: `ActionEvent`, `DEFAULT_ACTION_HISTORY_N`, the §3 relevance filter, `record_action_event`); `src/mtg_bot/search/engine_adapter.py` (`MtgGameStateAdapter.apply` records into `recent_actions`; `clone()` shares the tuple); `src/mtg_bot/search/nn_evaluator.py::_structured_forward` and `src/mtg_bot/search/shm_nn_eval_server.py::_tokenize_state` (read `getattr(state, "recent_actions", ())`); `src/mtg_bot/training/data_gen.py::_play_one_game_recording` (tokenizes from `adapter.recent_actions`; the hand-kept `action_history` list is gone); `src/mtg_bot/search/rust_engine_adapter.py::recent_actions` (always `()`); `src/mtg_bot/search/rust_shadow.py::recent_actions` (delegates to the Python checker).

**What was wrong (CLOSED).** The structured input carries up to 32 action-history tokens (roadmap §3). Training rows were built with the real per-game history, but every inference site passed `()` — the trunk was trained on a signal it never received while searching. The adapter now records each strategically-relevant decision (pre-apply engine clone + turn / step / actor) into an immutable tuple bounded to the last 32 relevant events; clones (MCTS children, PIMC / ISMCTS determinized worlds) inherit it by reference; data_gen and both inference sites tokenize from that one attribute. Pinned by `tests/search/test_engine_adapter_history.py` (byte-equal tokens vs the legacy data_gen construction at every sample point, both viewers) plus the NNEvaluator / SHM pass-through tests.

**The remaining deliberate shortcut.** `RustGameStateAdapter.recent_actions` is always empty. The tokenizer resolves each event's card printings against a Python `GameState` snapshot; the Rust provider has no Python engine state to clone, so a Rust-sourced structured search still evaluates leaves with zero action tokens.

**Why it's OK (today).** Production self-play / eval construct the Python adapter (`make_game_state_adapter` raises for `decision_source="rust"` at the Python-engine sites — B3-S5 is not flipped), so no live NN search runs through the Rust provider. `rust_shadow` (the bake-in) delegates to its Python checker, which applies every decision in lockstep, so it carries the real history.

**Failure mode.** If B3-S5 flips a structured-NN search onto the bare Rust provider, that search regresses to the pre-fix train/inference mismatch (history tokens present in training, absent at search) — a silent strength loss, not a crash. `NNEvaluator` does not warn; the property is simply `()`.

**Fix scope estimate.** ~1 cycle: either (a) have the Rust adapter build `ActionEvent`s whose snapshot is a `RustZoneView`-style read-only view exposing `battlefield` / `stack` / `players[].hand|graveyard|library` with `(id, printing)` pairs captured at apply time (the tokenizer only reads those), or (b) teach the tokenizer a resolve-at-capture path (store the resolved source / target printings on the event; no snapshot at all) and use it on both providers. (b) is also the cheaper memory shape for the Python adapter.

**Impact estimate.** Python path: 0 strength cost (parity by construction); per-apply cost +~33us on the ~10% of applies that survive the §3 filter (one `GameState.clone()`), +0 on PassPriority / mana abilities, adapter `clone()` unchanged (~23us) — see the feature commit message for the dated numbers. Rust path: unchanged from before (still empty history); bounded to a flip that has not happened.

**Pinned by:** `tests/test_rust_codec_slot_source.py::test_rust_provider_recent_actions_is_empty_and_shadow_delegates_to_python`.


## Per-game timeout — abandoned games now stop cooperatively; a thread wedged inside one non-cooperative call is still left running (bounded) — 2026-09-23, `feature/game-timeout-cooperative-stop`

**Where:** `src/mtg_bot/cancellation.py` (new: `CancelToken`, `GameCancelled`, `bind_token` / `unbind_token`, `raise_if_cancelled`); `src/mtg_bot/training/_timeout.py::run_with_timeout` + `_stop_and_wait` (binds the token, cancels + joins on timeout, `DEFAULT_STOP_GRACE_SEC = 30.0`); check sites at `src/mtg_bot/search/mcts.py::_search_serial` / `::_search_batched`, `src/mtg_bot/search/ismcts.py` (both iteration loops), `src/mtg_bot/search/pimc.py` (all three per-determinization sample loops), `src/mtg_bot/training/self_play.py::_play_capped_game`, `src/mtg_bot/training/data_gen.py::_play_one_game_recording`.

**What was wrong (CLOSED).** `run_with_timeout` ran each game in a `ThreadPoolExecutor` thread and, on timeout, called `executor.shutdown(wait=False)` and raised. CPython cannot kill a thread, so the abandoned game kept running inside the multiprocessing worker while the pool handed that worker the next game — two full games executing concurrently in one process, sharing the interpreter, the numpy/torch runtimes, `state_tokenizer._PRINTING_TO_ID_CACHE` and `search.eval_counters`. Observed in production on 2026-09-23: `ladder_runs/prod_2026-09-23/run.log` carries two `Fatal Python error: _PyEval_EvalFrameDefault: Executing a cache.` faulthandler dumps whose thread lists show TWO live `self_play._play_capped_game` frames in one worker, and the same pool then raised `ValueError: could not broadcast input array from shape (59,7) into shape (58,7)` out of `nn_evaluator._collate_structured_token_dicts` — a torn tokenizer dict (`tokenize_state` appends `token_type` / `token_emb_ids` / `token_scalars` in lockstep at 12 call sites each, so unequal lengths are interpreter-level corruption, not a logic bug). A zombie thread also permanently burned a core, shrinking the pool and making the next timeout more likely.

**The remaining deliberate shortcut.** The stop is *cooperative*. A thread that is wedged inside a single long non-cooperative call — a genuine engine hang in `effects/combinators.resolve`, or a single enormous torch op — never reaches a `raise_if_cancelled()` and is not stopped. After `stop_grace_sec` (default 30 s) `run_with_timeout` gives up waiting, prints a loud stderr warning, and raises `TimeoutError` with `"did NOT stop"` in the message; the thread keeps running exactly as it did before this feature.

**Why it's OK.** The check sites cover every loop that a game spends time in: one check per MCTS/ISMCTS iteration (~150 us – 2 ms of work each), one per PIMC determinization, one per game decision. Every timeout observed in the 2026-09-23 logs was a *slow* game (abandoned at 190–1070 decisions, i.e. steadily progressing), not a wedge, so the cooperative path covers the entire observed population. `mp.Pool.__exit__` calls `terminate()`, which kills the worker process and any surviving thread, so even an uncooperative thread is bounded by the run.

**Failure mode.** A genuine engine wedge degrades to the pre-fix behavior: one extra CPU-burning thread per wedged game plus the shared-state race with the next game in that worker. It is now *loud* (stderr warning + the TimeoutError message) rather than silent, which is the difference that matters for diagnosis.

**Fix scope estimate.** ~1–2 cycles for the fully-correct version: run each game in its own subprocess (`concurrent.futures.ProcessPoolExecutor` per game, or a `maxtasksperchild=1` inner pool) so the timeout can `terminate()` it. Rejected for now — Windows `spawn` start-up plus the per-process `NNEvaluator` / torch-model load is ~0.3–1 s, which on a ~200 s mean game is tolerable but on the cheap random-vs-heuristic pairs (~8 s/game) is a 5–10 % throughput tax paid on 100 % of games to fix a <2 % case.

**Impact estimate.** Cost: one `threading.local` attribute read (~100 ns) per MCTS iteration / PIMC sample / game decision — under 0.1 % of a ~150 us–2 ms iteration. Benefit: removes the two-games-in-one-process corruption class entirely for the observed (slow-game) timeout population, and returns the zombie's core to the pool, which breaks the timeout → fewer effective cores → more timeouts feedback loop.

**Pinned by:** `tests/test_cancellation.py` (12 cases), `tests/training/test_timeout.py` (the cooperative-stop / token-lifecycle / uncooperative-warning cases), `tests/training/test_timeout_stops_real_game.py` (a real MTG game through `self_play._play_capped_game` — the exact frame from the production dumps — asserted to unwind and leak no thread).


## Heuristic self-play carries `root_dirichlet_alpha` but the noise is INERT under UCB1 — 2026-09-24, `feature/heuristic-warm-start`

**Where:** `src/mtg_bot/training/config.py::PimcConfig` (new `root_dirichlet_alpha` / `root_dirichlet_eps` fields, forwarded to the inner `MCTS`); `src/mtg_bot/training/self_play_evaluator.py::build_heuristic_pimc_config`; the consumer gate is `src/mtg_bot/search/mcts.py::_select_and_expand` (`node is root and self.puct and self.root_dirichlet_alpha is not None`).

**What the shortcut is.** `mtg_bot iterate --self-play-evaluator heuristic` accepts the same `--root-dirichlet-alpha` / `--root-dirichlet-eps` knobs as the NN path, and the values are genuinely plumbed onto the stage spec, onto the worker's claim, and onto the constructed `MCTS`. They then do nothing. `_apply_root_dirichlet_noise` mixes noise into the root children's `prior` values, and `prior` is only ever read by PUCT selection; PUCT requires a policy-head evaluator, and `MtgHeuristicEvaluator` has none, so a heuristic sub-search runs UCB1 and never consults a prior.

**Why it's OK.** Under `FullEnumeration` (the production expansion policy) UCB1 expands and evaluates *every* root child at least once before any selection happens, so the "search never even looks at move X" failure mode that root noise exists to prevent cannot occur at a heuristic root. The self-play diversity knob that does apply is `--move-temperature` / `--temperature-cutoff`, which lives in `data_gen._play_one_game_recording` and is entirely strategy-agnostic (it samples the PLAYED move from whatever visit counts came back). Measured on the 20-game local verification shard: 49.8 % of multi-choice policy targets are near-uniform and mean normalised entropy is 0.876, i.e. the heuristic root distribution is already wide.

**Why it isn't silent.** Per `feedback_silent_noop_pipelines`, `build_heuristic_pimc_config` emits a one-time `logging.warning` naming the flag, the reason (UCB1 has no priors), and the knob that does work. `mtg_bot iterate --self-play-evaluator heuristic` prints it at stage start.

**Failure mode.** An operator tunes `--root-dirichlet-alpha` on a heuristic corpus run and measures no change, concluding the knob is useless in general. The warning is the mitigation.

**Fix scope estimate.** ~1 cycle, and only if wanted: give the heuristic path a prior source (e.g. `search/mtg_priors.py` as a hand-written policy prior) and run those sub-searches under PUCT, at which point the noise becomes live. That is a strength-affecting search change with its own evaluation burden, deliberately out of scope for corpus generation.

**Impact estimate.** Zero perf cost (two extra floats on a frozen dataclass). Zero strength cost today — the knob is a no-op in this configuration rather than a wrong behaviour.

**Pinned by:** `tests/training/test_self_play_evaluator.py::test_build_heuristic_pimc_config_carries_dirichlet_knobs` (asserts the values reach `MCTS` AND that `puct is False`), `::test_build_heuristic_pimc_config_warns_once_about_inert_noise`.


## Value-head calibration is a post-hoc scalar, and `trunk_no_printing` deliberately blinds the value head to card identity — 2026-09-25, `feature/value-calibration-identity-blind`

**Where:** `src/mtg_bot/training/value_calibration.py` (the fit); `src/mtg_bot/training/structured_model.py::StructuredModel.forward` (where the temperature and the identity-blind second trunk pass are applied); `StructuredModelConfig.value_temperature` / `.value_bias` / `.value_head_input`; `src/mtg_bot/search/nn_evaluator.py::NNEvaluator.from_metadata` + `_build_structured_model` (the loader that threads both off `metadata.json`); `src/mtg_bot/training/value_gate.py` (the gate now judges the calibrated number).

**What the shortcuts are.** Two, both opt-in-shaped.

1. **Post-hoc value calibration.** The trained value head's output is rescaled at inference by a single scalar temperature fit AFTER training on the held-out split: `value = tanh(logit / T)`. It is not learned jointly with the network and it is not re-fit as the self-play distribution drifts under a version — the temperature that ships with `vN` was fit against the data `vN` was trained on. `T` lives in `metadata.value_calibration`, not in `weights.pt`.

2. **`--value-head-input trunk_no_printing`.** The value head reads a SECOND pass of the same trunk weights over token embeddings with the per-printing (`EMB_FIELD_PRINTING` / `EMB_FIELD_TARGET_PRINTING`) lookups dropped. The value head then cannot see WHICH cards are on the battlefield / in hand / in the graveyard — only their count, zone, controller, and the schema-v2 numeric scalars (tapped, P/T, damage, counters, combat flags, life, poison, zone sizes, land counts, turn, stack size, priority). The policy head keeps the full-information pass. Default is `trunk`; nothing changes unless a run opts in.

**Why they're OK.** (1) A temperature is a strictly monotone transform, so it cannot change the value head's ORDERING of positions — only how loudly it asserts them. One free parameter against 10^5–10^6 held-out rows is not a capacity that can memorise; measured on the 1,000-shard fit the calibrated MSE landed on the theoretical `1 - r**2` to within 0.001, i.e. the fit is doing the one thing it is supposed to do and nothing else. (2) The identity-blind value head is an information restriction, and the thing being restricted is exactly what the s2 lineage memorised (`docs/SCALING_DIAGNOSTICS.md` D4/D5). The policy head — which is fine, and which needs card identity to pick a move — is untouched.

**Which scenarios make them not-OK.**

- A temperature fit on heuristic-guided self-play may be wrong for NN-guided self-play, which visits a different state distribution. The direction of the error is "the head stays over-confident for longer than it should", which is the pathology the calibration exists to remove. Re-fit with `mtg_bot calibrate-value --version vN --data-dir <newer pool>` after a distribution shift.
- `trunk_no_printing` throws away real evaluation signal. Two boards that are numerically identical but hold a bomb rare vs a vanilla 2/2 are indistinguishable to that value head. It is the right trade only while the value head's marginal use of card identity is negative -- and as of 2026-09-25 it is NOT: at the 9-epoch budget the production runs use, the shared trunk beats the identity-blind head on the gate metric (cv MSE 0.817 vs 0.878) even though it memorises far harder (train value loss 0.015 vs 0.467). See `docs/SCALING_DIAGNOSTICS.md` D5. The option ships because it is the only configuration that clears the ceiling UNCALIBRATED and because its temperature transfers across the corpus, but it is not the recommended setting today.
- The gate's 1.0 ceiling is the true "no information" line only for BALANCED held-out labels (the best constant predictor scores `1 - mean(y)**2`). Self-play records both seats, so real labels are balanced — measured `target_mean = 0.0` exactly on the 662k-row split — but a hand-built or filtered split would not be.

**Failure mode.** A stale temperature makes search either over-confident (T too small — the ±1-leaf pathology returns) or mushy (T too large — every leaf reads ~0 and PUCT is driven by the policy prior alone). Both are graceful degradations of an existing failure mode, not new ones, and both are visible in `metadata.value_calibration.calibrated_mse` vs a re-fit. For `trunk_no_printing`, the failure mode is a value head that cannot distinguish card quality, i.e. a strictly weaker evaluator with a strictly more trustworthy scale.

**Fix scope estimate.** Learning the temperature jointly (a trainable scalar on the value logit, optimised on the val split) is ~half a cycle and removes the "fit once, ships forever" staleness — deferred because the post-hoc fit is measurable, reversible, and re-runnable without retraining. Replacing `trunk_no_printing`'s second trunk pass with a bottlenecked printing embedding for the value head only (a low-rank projection instead of a hard zero) is ~1 cycle and would recover some card-quality signal at the current compute cost; not attempted here because the binary version is the one that isolates the diagnosis.

**Impact estimate.** Calibration: zero inference cost (one float, folded into the existing `tanh`), and it takes the 6,000-shard warm start from held-out MSE 1.294 (REJECT) to ≈0.90 (PASS) — see `docs/SCALING_DIAGNOSTICS.md` D5. `trunk_no_printing`: **~1.5× per NN eval at batch 1 on CPU** (the production self-play shape), 1.33× at batch 16/256, 1.3–1.6× on CUDA, and ~1.35× per training epoch — measured 2026-09-25 on the production trunk (`emb 128 / 2 layers / hidden 256`, seq_len 64) via `scripts/bench_value_head_input.py`. Strength effect is UNMEASURED by the eval gate; only held-out value quality has been measured.

**Pinned by:** `tests/training/test_value_calibration.py` (28 cases, incl. the synthetic corr-0.3 saturated predictor scoring >1 raw and <1 calibrated, and the zero-variance head that must NOT be calibrated), `tests/training/test_structured_model.py` (`test_trunk_no_printing_value_ignores_card_identity` + `test_default_trunk_value_does_see_card_identity` as its control, `test_trunk_no_printing_adds_no_parameters`), `tests/search/test_nn_evaluator_structured.py` (`test_from_metadata_applies_the_stored_value_calibration`, `test_from_metadata_missing_calibration_is_the_identity`), `tests/cli/test_calibrate_value_cli.py` (10 cases).


## Board-only opponent model (`opponent_hidden_model="board_only"`, ladder `+boardonly`) does not model ANY hidden opponent card — 2026-10-05, `feature/s2-boardonly-search`

**Where:** `src/mtg_bot/search/determinize.py` (`determinize(..., opponent_hidden_model=)`, `_blank_player`, `make_determinize_fn`); the placeholder printing `src/mtg_bot/cards/hidden.py::HIDDEN_CARD_PRINTING`; threaded by `src/mtg_bot/training/config.py` (`PimcConfig` / `NNPimcConfig.opponent_hidden_model`, ISMCTS `determinize_fn`), `src/mtg_bot/search/hybrid_evaluator.py::HybridPimcConfig.build`, `src/mtg_bot/cli/ladder.py::split_search_modifiers` (`+boardonly`, `+s<K>`), `src/mtg_bot/cli/capture.py --opponent-hidden-model`. Consumers that special-case the placeholder: `src/mtg_bot/legal.py::_can_cast` (never castable -- the exile / graveyard cast-permission paths only check cost; found by the 2026-10-05 horizon run, where 2/20 board-only games crashed resolving an impulse-exiled placeholder, and by a 6,799-world random fuzz on the EoE pool, 0 errors after the fix), `src/mtg_bot/training/state_tokenizer.py::_make_zone_card_token` and `src/mtg_bot/search/_player_capabilities.py::_sorcery_speed_castable_in_hand`. Default `"sampled"` is bit-identical to before (`make_determinize_fn("sampled") is determinize`).

**What the shortcut is.** Opt-in, per seat. In each PIMC world the searcher does not imagine the opponent's hidden cards: every opponent hand / library card the viewer can't identify (`viewer_knows` False) gets the inert `"<hidden card>"` printing (no types, no keywords, no costs/abilities, mana value 0). It can never be cast, played or activated (every hand-cast / land-play path in `legal_actions` is gated on a card type), but it still counts for hand size, cleanup discard, mill, "cards in hand" and the heuristic evaluator's card term. Revealed opponent cards stay real; the searcher's own library is sampled exactly as under `"sampled"`; public zones are untouched. The opponent can still attack, block and activate abilities of public permanents.

**Why it's OK (as an option).** It removes the "non-locality / strategy-fusion" noise of planning against a concrete imagined hand that is wrong almost every time, and the tree no longer spends nodes on imagined opposing casts. Leaf values are unaffected in distribution: from the searcher's (root) perspective the opponent's hand is redacted to `PRINTING_NA` anonymous slots in both modes, so the NN value input at leaves looks exactly like it does under `"sampled"`.

**Which scenarios make it not-OK.**
- The opponent never has a trick, removal spell, counterspell or flash blocker in the tree: the searcher walks into open mana, attacks into combat tricks, and over-values plays that instant-speed interaction would punish.
- The opponent draws only placeholders: in the tree they never make another land drop or cast another spell, so multi-turn lines under-estimate their development (the horizon measurement in `docs/SEARCH_HORIZON.md` shows how rarely trees reach the next turn, which bounds this).
- Effects that interact with the opponent's hidden cards (look at / choose from their hand, mill, "exile the top card of their library, you may cast it") see blanks and are under-valued; mana-value-counting effects see 0.
- PUCT priors at OPPONENT nodes are computed from the opponent's perspective, where their own hand is "visible": placeholders there are tokenized as printing NA with `public_mask=0` in `TOKEN_TYPE_HAND_VIEWER` rows — a pattern the net never saw in training (a viewer always knows its own hand). Only the opponent's prior over attack / block / pass / activations is affected; it can never be a prior on casting a placeholder (masked as illegal).
- Not available with belief-weighted ISMCTS (`NNPimcConfig` raises) and not wired for the Rust decision source (`rust_determinize`); PIMC requires the Python adapter anyway.

**Failure mode.** Systematic over-aggression into instant-speed interaction, and under-respect for the opponent's next turn. Both are visible in the A/B below as a lower win rate if they dominate.

**Fix scope estimate.** A middle ground — sample only the opponent's likely interaction (instants / flash cards in their deck list), blank the rest — is ~1 cycle on top of this seam (`_blank_player` vs `_determinize_player` per card). A belief model over the hand (roadmap Step 2/4) is the real fix.

**Impact estimate.** Perf: the opponent's capability auto-pass fires at more windows (a placeholder-only hand has no instant / sorcery capability), so trees hold fewer opponent-cast branches; measured ms per decision in `docs/SEARCH_HORIZON.md`. Strength (2026-10-05, `ladder_runs/s2_v30_boardonly_n200`, same deals as `ladder_runs/s2_v30_diag_n200`, nodes 200 / samples 2 / 300 games vs `heuristic`): `v30+b1` 53.0 % [47.4, 58.6], `v30+b1+boardonly` 52.3 % [46.7, 58.0] (-0.7 pts, CI [-8.6, +7.3]), `v30+b1+boardonly+s1` 55.2 % [49.5, 60.8] (+2.2 pts, CI [-5.8, +10.1]) -- no measurable cost (or gain) at this budget. Trees reach two turns ahead in 37 % vs 17 % of searches and spend 0 % vs 32 % of their nodes under imagined opponent casts (`docs/SEARCH_HORIZON.md`).

**Pinned by:** `tests/search/test_board_only_determinize.py` (placeholder inertness, determinize invariants incl. CoW no-leak, whole games in a board-only world with tokenization from both perspectives, and a search whose opponent holds Bombard: the sampled tree contains the opponent casting it, the board-only tree contains no opponent cast), `tests/cli/test_ladder_boardonly.py` (label parsing, per-seat config threading, `+s<K>` budget, round-trips).
